gameTypes.name: Feed the Hungry Friend
gameTypes.description: An expressive hungry creature (dragon, monster, whale, hippo, robot) asks for things that match a rule each round; the child gives it the right item and it chomps, gulps, burps, grows, and reacts. The character's personality carries the loop — kids feed it the wrong thing on purpose just to see the silly reaction. One level = one critter and one skill-rule, replayed across rounds. (Merges the feed-the-character shape proposed in all three decks.)
gameTypes.interaction: drag the correct item into the open mouth OR tap the correct one of 3-4; chomp + happy reaction on correct; wrong item gently spat back with a warm wobble (no penalty, never a shame beat)
gameTypes.fitsSkills: K.CC counting/subitizing (feed exactly N), K.OA/1.OA make-a-number & add/sub-to-target, K.CC.C.6/7 comparing more/fewer, K.MD/2.MD sort-by-attribute, K.G/2.G shape & polygon sorting, odd-one-out, RF.K.2/RF.K.3.a beginning sounds & rhyming (feed the /b/ monster), sight-word recognition, categorize-by-meaning vocabulary, 3.NF fractions-of-food, money
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is caretaking + cause-and-effect surprise: the critter reacts uniquely to every food and gets sillier as it eats. The chomp, the burp, and a satisfied full belly ARE the reward system — no metric. Wrong taps are a giggle (tongue out), not a failure; the critter is patient and chatty so there is no clock.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One CA5-rigged creature with separated jaw + eye morphs: idle, mouth-open, chomp, yum/full, gentle-reject (~6 poses) + a tray of draggable food/object props (reuse the 50-theme color image library directly). Stub: CSS mouth-toggle face + DOM item cards.

gameTypes.name: Mystery Reveal (Scratch / Wake-the-Scene)
gameTypes.description: A surprise picture or sleepy scene sits hidden under a grid of covers (fog, snow, sleeping characters). Each correct answer uncovers ONE piece — a tile dissolves, a flower blooms, a window lights up — until the whole surprise is revealed and comes alive. Best for rapid single-skill drilling disguised as a treasure hunt; each game hides a different silly image. (Consolidates mystery-reveal, wake-the-scene, and magic-reveal across all three decks.)
gameTypes.interaction: answer a one-tap/one-drag prompt -> one cover tile flips/dissolves or one element wakes; final tap on the finished picture triggers a celebratory wiggle
gameTypes.fitsSkills: RF.K.1 letter recognition, RF.K.3 letter-sound, sight-word reading, K.CC number/numeral-quantity recognition, 1.OA.C.6/2.OA.B.2 fact fluency, K.G/2.G shape naming, place value, telling time, 3.NF naming fractions, 3.OA multiplication facts, vocabulary word-meaning — any rapid-fire recognition or fluency skill
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is curiosity + suspense: 'what is it?!' pulls the child forward instead of a clock, and 'one more to see the picture' replaces the score. It waits indefinitely; answers uncover more rather than tally points. Replay = a different surprise image and hidden Easter eggs that only appear when fully revealed.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One CA5 surprise illustration per game (animal in a costume, goofy scene) with a short loopable reaction strip + a generic tile/flap cover overlay reused everywhere. Stub: CSS opaque tiles fading out on correct + a silhouette.

gameTypes.name: Hatch, Grow & Tend
gameTypes.description: A living thing the child nurtures over the session — a seed that grows, an egg that hatches (egg -> crack -> baby -> creature), a pet that gets happier, an aquarium that fills. Correct answers 'water / feed / care' it through visible growth stages. Calm, cozy, cumulative; you can never 'lose' it. Shares the reveal engine but the beat is caretaking + accumulation, not a surprise drill. (Merges grow-tend and hatch-grow.)
gameTypes.interaction: answer a prompt -> tap the care action (watering can, food, crank) -> the subject advances one growth stage with a sweet transform; tap it anytime for an affectionate idle reaction
gameTypes.fitsSkills: 2.NBT.A.2/3.OA skip-counting & number sequences (grow by 2s/5s/10s), K.MD/2.MD measurement & comparison (how tall), 3.OA repeated addition toward multiplication, counting-on & accumulating quantities, high-rep fact fluency (1.OA.C.6/2.OA.B.2) where each correct answer advances a stage — anything CUMULATIVE
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is nurture + visible living progress: caring for something and watching it flourish is intrinsically satisfying and pressure-free. Growth stages are non-numeric progress (no track, no count). Replay to grow it fully again or raise a new species; the grown creature stays in a little nursery to keep.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One CA5 subject in 4-6 staged transform poses (seedling -> bloom; egg -> hatch) each with a small idle loop + a care-action prop. Stub: placeholder art swapping 5 stage images.

gameTypes.name: Build-a-World Diorama
gameTypes.description: A persistent scene (farm, town, aquarium, treehouse, garden) the child GROWS by answering prompts; each correct answer drops a new character/object into the scene where it stays, and the child freely chooses where things go. The scene IS the progress — no number tracks it. Distinct from build-a-buddy: this collects 'one earned item per answer' into a shared world rather than composing one object from parts.
gameTypes.interaction: solve a one-tap/one-drag prompt in a side tray -> the earned sprite pops into a free slot in the diorama; the child may freely drag-rearrange any placed sprite
gameTypes.fitsSkills: K.CC counting/cardinality, K.OA/1.OA add & subtract, 1.NBT/2.NBT place value, sight words & vocabulary (place the labeled object), world-knowledge vocab — almost any 'answer one item' skill maps here
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is agency + collection + permanence: the child decorates a world they own, not a race. Watching the empty scene fill with characters is the payoff and rearranging is free play. No timer because dwelling in and arranging the scene is the point.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One CA5 painted background plate per world + a sheet of ~20 standalone character/object sprites (idle + one happy 'pop-in' frame) per world. Stub: DOM background image + draggable placeholder tiles.

gameTypes.name: Build-a-Buddy / Maker
gameTypes.description: The child earns and places parts to BUILD one thing they own and keep — a silly monster, a robot, an ice-cream tower, a sandwich. Each correct answer unlocks a modular part the child drags wherever they like; the result is a unique creation every time. (Merges build-creation, machine-build's keepable-output, and stamp-paint's earn-a-tool creative loop into the compose-from-parts shape.)
gameTypes.interaction: answer to unlock a part -> free drag-and-drop placement onto a canvas; child stacks, arranges, and customizes; a 'show my creation' celebratory wiggle finishes
gameTypes.fitsSkills: K.OA.A.3 compose/decompose & number bonds, 1.NBT/2.NBT place value (build with tens-rods & ones), RF.K.3/RF.1.3 building CVC & longer words (letter-bricks), 3.NF fractions building a whole, 3.OA arrays for multiplication (stamp rows), 1.G.A.2/2.G shape composition, syllable & sentence building — anything COMPOSED from parts
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is ownership + creativity: the child makes a unique thing every time and the arrangement is THEIRS (no 'right' layout). Skill gates the parts; creativity is uncapped. The creation itself is the trophy, so no score is needed; replay makes a sillier one.
gameTypes.assetPattern: Modular mix-and-match CA5 part sprites with consistent attach points (eyes/arms/hats; robot limbs; scoops; letter-bricks) + one happy 'finished creature' wiggle. Stub: DOM draggable placeholder part-rectangles onto a canvas.

gameTypes.name: Dress-Up & Decorate
gameTypes.description: The child customizes a base character or object (bear, cupcake, snowman, room) by earning decorations through prompts and placing them ON it per a rule — the right clothes for the weather, an item that starts with /s/, a hat ABOVE the head. The buddy reacts to each addition and ends with a proud strut. Distinct from build-a-buddy: emphasis is positional/attribute placement + self-expression rather than structural composition.
gameTypes.interaction: answer/choose the correct item -> drag it onto the character at a placement spot; character poses/twirls; freely restyle placed items; a final fashion-show strut
gameTypes.fitsSkills: K.G/K.MD color/shape/attribute & sorting, patterns (place items in an AB pattern), positional words ('put the hat ABOVE', 'shoes UNDER'), 1.MD comparatives big/small, vocabulary (clothing, body parts, weather/season world-knowledge), counting ('add 3 buttons'), 2.G/3.G symmetry
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is self-expression + character delight: there is no 'right' final look so failure is impossible, and the buddy reacts to every choice. Earning decorations gives gentle structure without competition; the fashion show is the reward, and kids replay to make a wilder outfit.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One CA5 base character + a deep wardrobe of placeable accessory sprites at attach points (hats, bows, faces) + 2-3 happy poses (twirl, strut, blush); accessories are simple static layers. Stub: base image + draggable accessory placeholders.

gameTypes.name: Sticker Album / Collection
gameTypes.description: A themed album with empty silhouette slots (a bug collection, sea-creature gallery, alphabet set). Each prompt earns a sticker that snaps into its matching slot with a shimmer; the child wants to complete the page and admire the full set. Tap any collected sticker to hear its name and a fun fact — adding tap-to-learn discovery on top of collection.
gameTypes.interaction: solve a prompt -> a sticker peels/drops into its matching silhouette (drag-to-match or auto-snap) with a shimmer; tap any collected sticker for its name / a fun fact
gameTypes.fitsSkills: vocabulary & world-knowledge naming (the headline use — name the animal/object), alphabet letter-name mastery, sight-word collection, K.CC number recognition, K.G/2.G shape gallery, money coin-collection — best for VOCAB, sight words, and naming
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is collection-completion + the 'gotta-see-them-all' instinct, plus tap-to-learn fun facts give genuine discovery. The full page is the reward; lingering and tapping stickers is encouraged. No timer, no count — just a satisfying complete set.
gameTypes.assetPattern: Minimal new art: one album-page background with silhouette slots + a shimmer effect; the stickers themselves REUSE the 50-theme image library directly. Stub: ready immediately — library art + CSS silhouette slots + a shimmer.

gameTypes.name: Sort-It-Home (Bins & Belonging)
gameTypes.description: Characters or objects need to go where they BELONG — animals to habitats, words to bins, shapes to shape-houses, items to category-rooms with little personalities. Each one settles in happily when sorted right; the home-character thanks the child. Warm 'everyone finds their place / everything tidy' framing. (Merges sort-home and sort-bins-game.)
gameTypes.interaction: drag each item to the correct labeled bin/home -> a tiny happy 'settling in' / 'thank you' animation on correct; mis-sorts gently bounce back with a 'hmm, where do I live?' wobble
gameTypes.fitsSkills: K.MD.B.3/2.MD.D categorize & classify, K.G/2.G 2D/3D & polygon-vs-non-polygon sorting, even/odd bins, greater/less bins, place-value bins (tens vs ones), RF sort words by sound/spelling pattern & long/short vowel, real-word vs nonsense, noun/verb, syllable-count bins, fact families, fraction more/less than half
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is tidying delight + grateful characters: each bin/home has a personality and reacts happily when fed its right thing (the 'everything in its place' satisfaction). The emotional beat is 'I helped them get home,' not 'I beat the clock.' No score — the plop, the thank-you, and a tidy finished shelf are the payoff.
gameTypes.assetPattern: 2-4 CA5 expressive bin/home characters (idle + happy-receive 'thank you' pose) + a set of sortable item sprites that REUSE the library, each with a 2-frame settle-in wiggle. Stub: labeled DOM bins + draggable item placeholders.

gameTypes.name: Friendly Match & Make-a-Pair
gameTypes.description: A relaxed, penalty-free memory/pairing game: flip or tap cards (or draw a line between two columns) to find pairs that go together by a rule. Matched pairs do a delighted synchronized celebration — characters hug/cheer — and lock with a satisfying pop. NO move-counter, NO turn limit, NO timer. (Merges match-pop, matching-pairs, and matching-memory.)
gameTypes.interaction: tap two cards to test a match (or draw a line between two columns) -> match = synchronized happy character animation + pop, locked revealed; non-match = gentle consequence-free flip-back
gameTypes.fitsSkills: RF.K.1.d upper/lowercase, RF.K.3 letter-sound, rhyming/sound pairs, picture-to-word vocabulary, K.CC numeral-to-quantity, 1.OA.D.7 fact-to-sum, 3.OA fact-to-product, 3.NF.A.3 equivalent fractions & fraction-to-model, 2.NBT.A.3 expanded/standard forms, synonyms/antonyms, coin-to-value — pairing-shaped skills
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is the satisfying 'click' of a found pair + the synchronized character celebration (the juice), plus the discovery of flipping to see what's there. No move-counter and no timer — flip as much as you like and mismatches are consequence-free, so it stays calm and cozy. Replay via reshuffled boards.
gameTypes.assetPattern: A card-back design + one reusable CA5 'match celebration' sprite (a confetti/cheer cameo critter, one per pair) with a 2-frame hug + a 'flip-back shrug'; the pair faces mostly REUSE library + letter/number tiles. Extends the existing match-pairs engine. Stub: card frames + placeholder cameo.

gameTypes.name: Pop the Right Ones (Bubbles & Balloons)
gameTypes.description: Gentle floating items (bubbles, balloons, fireflies, leaves) drift slowly carrying answers; the child taps only the ones matching the rule, which pop with a juicy splash/sparkle. Non-targets drift by harmlessly. CALM drift — a treasure-hunt-in-the-air, deliberately NOT a frantic reaction game.
gameTypes.interaction: tap matching drifting items to pop them with a splash/sparkle + soft chime; a mistaken pop does a gentle 'boing' and refills; clear all targets to finish
gameTypes.fitsSkills: identify numbers/letters/sight words, even/odd, 3.OA multiples (pop multiples of 3), beginning/ending sounds & vowels, K.CC count-and-pop exactly N, greater/less than, sort-by-category, rhymes, syllable count
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is tactile pop-juice + selective hunting: the splash, sparkle, and sound are the intrinsic 'sensory snack.' Drift speed is calm and slow on purpose so it never becomes a reflex race — there is no counter and no timer; you simply clear the sky at your own pace.
gameTypes.assetPattern: 3-4 CA5 drifting prop variants (bubble, balloon, firefly) each with a soft idle bob + a 2-3 frame pop/burst frame and a label slot. Stub: CSS-animated floating DOM elements with a pop transition.

gameTypes.name: I-Spy Hidden Scene
gameTypes.description: A rich, busy illustrated scene packed with findable things and little background jokes. The child hunts for prompted items by tapping them in the picture; found things wave, light up, or sparkle and check off a friendly list. One dense scene = one game; the density makes it cozily explorable. (Merges hidden-scene and hidden-object.)
gameTypes.interaction: read/hear the prompt ('find the things that start with S' / 'find 3 triangles' / 'find the numbers that make 10') -> tap matching things in the scene -> happy react + soft chime; gentle 'look again' shimmer hint if stuck; free taps reveal Easter eggs
gameTypes.fitsSkills: RF.K.3.a beginning sounds & letter hunt, K.CC.B.5 counting in context, K.G/2.G find-the-shape in context, sight-word spotting, find-the-number, K.OA find-numbers-that-make-N, K.MD attribute spotting (color/size), vocabulary identification — strong for visual-scan literacy & counting
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is exploration + discovery: a dense scene rewards just looking around, and tapping anything gives a small delightful reaction (Easter eggs). The hunt is cozy, not timed. Replay = the scene hides prompts in new orders and there is always more to notice.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One large detailed CA5 scene plate with ~15-25 individually tappable hotspot sprites layered over it, each with a 1-frame react/wave. Stub: a scene illustration + invisible DOM hotspot rectangles with a CSS pop on tap.

gameTypes.name: The Magic Machine (Function & Word Factory)
gameTypes.description: A funny contraption (number machine, sound machine, word factory, potion lab) takes an input the child feeds in, whirs and clanks, and pops out a transformed result — add the magic-e and out comes a new word; put in 7, turn the crank, +3, out comes 10; feed a base word, get the plural. The whir-and-reveal is the delight and the child predicts/completes the output. (Merges machine-build's transform output and machine-transform.)
gameTypes.interaction: drag the input into the funnel, pull the lever / turn the crank -> machine whirs (gears, blinking lights) -> output pops from the chute; child predicts or completes the output
gameTypes.fitsSkills: 1.OA/2.OA add/subtract function-machine, 1.NBT +1/-1/+10 patterns, RF.1.3 silent-e & word transforms, RF.1.3.f plurals & endings (-s/-ed/-ing), prefixes/suffixes, rounding, skip-count machine, place-value regroup, 3.OA doubling for multiplication, syllable blending — anything that TRANSFORMS an input
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is cause-and-effect machinery + surprise reveals: kids love pulling the lever and watching the gears churn out a result — a little magic trick every time. No score; the whir, the pop-out, and the machine's silly personality are the joy, and predicting the output feels like being in on the trick.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One characterful CA5 machine rig (funnel/input, gears whir-loop, output chute, lever, a little machine face) with a 3-5 frame whir-and-reveal cycle + input/output prop slots. Stub: a machine illustration + CSS shake/blink on lever-pull + swapped output image.

gameTypes.name: Hop Along the Path
gameTypes.description: A friendly character travels a winding path one stop at a time (lily pads, stepping stones, train stops, snail trail) across one illustrated scene. Each correct answer hops the character forward to the next decorated stop, with little surprises at some stops (a bridge, a tunnel, a waving friend); reaching the end is a warm arrival celebration. Naturally fits anything ORDERED. (Merges path-journey and journey-board.)
gameTypes.interaction: answer the prompt on the current stop -> character hops to the next stop with a little walk/jump animation; some stops trigger a mini surprise; arrival plays a reunion/party vignette
gameTypes.fitsSkills: K.CC/1.OA counting-on & number line, 2.NBT.A.2/3.OA skip-counting, add/subtract within 20/100, 2.MD.B.6 number-line operations, ordering numbers/by-size, RF sequencing events & story order, alphabet order, ordinal concepts, time sequencing — anything ORDERED
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is travel + anticipation: where does the path go, what's around the bend, who will I meet? Progress is spatial and visible ('look how far we've come') without being a race — there is no timer and the character waits patiently. The destination reward (a party, a reunited friend) is the payoff; vary the destination per game.
gameTypes.assetPattern: One CA5 path-scene background + a travelling character (4-8 frame walk/hop cycle) + decorated path/stepping-stone tiles + a handful of surprise-stop props + one arrival-celebration vignette. Stub: DOM path tiles + a placeholder character sprite that translates between stops.

gameTypes.name: Story Maker & Puppet Show
gameTypes.description: A short interactive mini-story / comic the child builds and then gets to 'watch': drag picture cards into story order, choose the word that finishes the sentence, pick what happens next, fill a speech bubble — and a pair of friendly puppet characters act it out with dialogue, expressions, and silliness. The finished story plays back as a tiny narrated comic the child authored. (Merges story-quest, story-comic, and puppet-talk — the ELA comprehension/speaking-listening shape.)
gameTypes.interaction: drag-to-sequence panels, tap word/picture choices to fill blanks, build speech bubbles; puppets animate a reaction + a line of dialogue per choice; the finished story plays back panel-by-panel
gameTypes.fitsSkills: RF story sequencing & comprehension (beginning/middle/end), sight-word & sentence reading, cloze sentence completion, vocabulary in context, print concepts (read left-to-right, point to the first word), rhyme & predictable text, fluency phrasing, ELA speaking/listening Q&A, cause-effect, 3.OA word problems framed as a story
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is authorship + character + narrative payoff: the child makes a story they then watch come alive, and funny puppet reactions (not a score) reward each choice. Conversational warmth and open choices give agency — the story differs each time — and the puppets wait for you, so there is no clock and no shame.
gameTypes.assetPattern: A small CA5 cast (two rigged puppets with mouth/eye morphs for lip-flap + 4-6 emotion poses each) reusable across many ELA games + speech-bubble templates + simple panel backgrounds & prop sets. Stub: DOM panels with placeholder character poses + caption/bubble boxes.

gameTypes.name: Magic Trace & Connect
gameTypes.description: Guided tracing/connecting where following the path produces a magical result — trace a letter/number/shape and the line blooms into sparkles, a creature, or a firework; connect dots in number/alphabet order to reveal a hidden picture; draw a line from word to picture; lead a bee/duck/snail along its path. Lenient snapping keeps it no-shame. The writing-readiness + connect gap-filler. (Merges trace-magic and path-trace.)
gameTypes.interaction: drag a fingertip/wand along a dotted guide OR connect points in sequence -> the trail fills with light/sparkle/footprints and a follower character moves along it; completion blooms into a reward animation or reveals/delivers a picture
gameTypes.fitsSkills: L.K.1.a/RF.K.1 handwriting & letter formation, number writing, connect-the-dots counting & alphabet order, K.G/1.G shape drawing & composition, pre-writing strokes, 1.OA/2.OA number-line operations & 3.NF fractions on a line, 2.MD length/measurement paths, 3.OA skip-count dot-to-dot, matching/connecting pairs, maze sequencing
gameTypes.funWithoutCompeting: Fun is the sensory drawing-trail + the transformation/reveal payoff: the satisfying sparkle-trail and the bloom or hidden-picture make the MOTION itself the reward. Lenient tracing means failure is impossible. No score — the magic, the reveal, and the happy arrival are the point.
gameTypes.assetPattern: Dotted-guide overlays per letter/shape (vector data, not art) + a CSS sparkle/footprint trail + a small CA5 bloom creature (4-6 frame spawn) and/or a follower character (bee/duck) with a movement loop + connect-the-dots reveal line-art. Stub: SVG dotted paths + a CSS trail + a placeholder bloom image on completion.

taxonomy.qualityPhilosophy: The moat is not novelty per game — it is RELIABLE DELIGHT at full-curriculum scale: 300+ games each feeling like a hand-made, characterful toy rather than a worksheet in a costume, together covering the honest full K-3 CCSS Math + ELA curriculum (a clear standard behind every game). Free single-skill activities answer "did the child DO the skill?"; these paid games answer "does the child WANT to come back?" — and that difference is what a parent/teacher pays for. It rests on three pillars, each done 300+ times: (1) CHARACTER & DELIGHT — every game has a creature/world/maker/puppet with a tiny personality and a reaction set (chomp, bloom, cheer, thank-you, whir, strut), so the child forms a relationship, not a transaction; surprise, silliness, and cause-and-effect carry the replay that a free drill would carry with a timer/score. (2) JUICE-AS-REWARD-SYSTEM — the operator-locked no-competition rule (no timer/score/points/streak/countdown/leaderboard) is HONORED, not worked around, by replacing score-dopamine with sensory/emotional payoff: the pop, the reveal, the bloom, the happy arrival, the world filling up. The juice IS the reward, and "learning games that never make your child feel rushed or judged" is itself the marketable promise. (3) AGENCY, OWNERSHIP & HONEST PEDAGOGY — the strongest shapes (build, dress-up, story-maker, world, collection, reveal) let the child MAKE, KEEP, or DISCOVER something that is theirs (the deepest source of voluntary early-childhood replay and the clearest line away from the free drills), while every game directly INSTANTIATES its CCSS standard (never merely touches the topic) and is developmentally calibrated to how K-3 children actually learn — manipulatives before symbols, recognition before production, concrete before abstract — which is exactly why each stays SIMPLE/one-level and genuinely playable on a lightweight DOM + CSS-sprite web shell. Volume and polish are compatible because each of the 14 shapes is a REUSABLE ENGINE: one web-shell core is re-curriculum'd by CCSS code and re-skinned by asset swap hundreds of times, so the engine carries the polish while the content carries the coverage. Premium feel is proven STUB-FIRST — every game is fully playable on day one with programmatic placeholder art (the loop is the fun), then ELEVATED by swapping in Cartoon Animator 5 character sprites (the art makes it lovable), with several shapes (sticker-album, sort-home, match-pairs, i-spy) reusing the existing 50-theme color image library directly so they ship near-instantly. Marketable because a parent demoing the free indexable landing + free sample slice immediately feels the warmth, the no-shame tone, and a "real game" feel the free worksheets deliberately don't have — and the honest full-CCSS coverage means one subscription replaces a shelf of single-skill apps.
taxonomy.notes:
Count: 14 locked types (within the 10-16 band). Every type honors the no-competition lock (no timer/score/points/streak/countdown/leaderboard), is buildable on the DOM + CSS-sprite web shell with only tap/drag/drop/match/sort/build/reveal/sequence/trace interactions (no physics/3D/multiplayer engine), is stub-playable with programmatic placeholder art, and carries a clear CA5 character/sprite asset list. Each is gated PREMIUM with a free indexable landing + free sample slice; the FREE decks/worksheet-generators/activities/tools are untouched.

Overlap resolutions across the three proposals: (a) feed-the-character appeared in all 3 -> merged to ONE (feed-the-friend). (b) the reveal mechanic appeared 4-5x (mystery-reveal, scratch/lift-the-flap, wake-the-scene, magic-reveal, hatch-grow) -> split into TWO genuinely-distinct beats that share one reveal engine: reveal-grid (curiosity/surprise, rapid drill) and grow-tend (caretaking/cumulative, sequential skills). (c) the make-and-own family (world-build, build-creation, dress-decorate, stamp-paint, machine-build's keepable output) -> three distinct shapes by skill-fit: build-a-world (collect one item per answer into a shared scene = any-answer skills), build-a-buddy (compose ONE object from parts = compose/decompose/place-value/word-building/arrays), dress-decorate (positional/attribute placement + self-expression). stamp-paint was FOLDED into build-a-buddy (its earn-a-tool creative loop overlaps and it drifts toward open-ended-no-skill on its own). (d) match/memory (match-pop, matching-pairs, matching-memory) -> ONE penalty-free match-pairs (explicitly no move-counter). (e) sort-home + sort-bins-game -> ONE. (f) hidden-scene + hidden-object -> ONE i-spy. (g) machine-build's transform + machine-transform -> ONE magic-machine. (h) path-journey + journey-board -> ONE. (i) story-quest + story-comic + puppet-talk -> ONE story-maker (puppet-talk folded in as the speaking/listening sub-mode — it was nearly identical to story-comic). (j) trace-magic + path-trace -> ONE magic-trace.

Nothing was dropped for needing scoring/timers (all proposals already respected the lock); pop-the-right-ones was KEPT but its spec explicitly mandates CALM drift so it is a selective-tap hunt, NOT a reflex/reaction game (the one shape that could have drifted into time-pressure — guarded against).

Curriculum coverage check (all of CCSS K-3 Math + ELA has at least one strong home): counting/cardinality K.CC -> feed/world/i-spy/path; add-sub K.OA/1.OA/2.OA -> feed/build-buddy/machine/reveal; place value 1.NBT/2.NBT -> build-buddy/machine/sort; fact fluency 1.OA.C.6/2.OA.B.2 -> reveal/grow/match; geometry K.G/1.G/2.G -> sort/dress/i-spy/build-buddy/trace; measurement & data K.MD/1.MD/2.MD -> sort/dress/grow/feed/trace; multiplication & fractions 3.OA/3.NF -> build-buddy/machine/grow/match/path/trace; letters & phonics RF.K/RF.1 -> reveal/match/i-spy/feed/machine/build-buddy; sight words & vocabulary -> sticker-album/match/world/feed/i-spy; writing readiness L.K.1.a -> magic-trace; comprehension/sequencing/speaking-listening RF -> story-maker/path. ELA-comprehension and writing-readiness (the two thinnest areas in the free-activity engine set) are explicitly homed in story-maker and magic-trace.

Complement-not-duplicate guard: these may target the same CCSS codes as the free §20 activities but the locked shapes are character/agency/discovery-driven GAME loops (build/own/reveal/journey/feed), structurally different from the free single-skill practice surfaces (choice-board, ten-frame, builders, place-value, etc.). Several types (sticker-album, sort-home, match-pairs, i-spy) can reuse the existing /image-library-webp/themes color library and image-vocabulary.js per §20.5, so the cheapest-to-ship games are the library-reuse ones — a natural build order: stub-first across all 14 to prove loops, then prioritize library-reuse shapes for fast premium volume, CA5 character art elevating each loop afterward.

games.title: Mochi's Counting Feast
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Mochi the round snow-bear opens her mouth wide and rumbles; drag exactly the right number of floating dumplings in; she pats her belly and does a tiny victory shuffle. Wrong count: she blows them back out with a comic 'pfffbt' bubble.
games.mechanic: A prompt card shows a numeral 1-10. Floating dumplings drift across the screen. Child drags exactly that many into Mochi's mouth one at a time; a running tally dot-strip fills as each enters. When the count matches, Mochi chomps and celebrates.
games.freeSample: Free: rounds 1-5 (numerals 1-5, dumplings only). Paid: rounds 6-20 (numerals 6-10, mixed foods — sushi, mochi balls, berries — and a 'surprise dish' mystery round that reveals a hidden sticker on correct count).
assetNeeds: Mochi snow-bear character (idle, mouth-open, chomping, belly-pat, blowing-back)

games.title: Number Train Conductor
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A little train conductor named Pip needs to hook up cars in the right counting order. Each correctly placed car puffs a smoke ring and toots. A mis-placed car gently rolls back to the siding with a friendly whistle. When all cars are in order the full train rolls through a tunnel and comes out decorated.
games.mechanic: A locomotive and an ordered track of empty hitches appear. Number-labeled rail cars wait in a shuffled siding yard. Child drags each car to its correct hitch in counting sequence 1-20 (split into sets of 5 per round). Each correct placement advances the train one station.
games.freeSample: Free: cars 1-5. Paid: cars 6-10, 1-10 mixed scramble, 11-20, and a 'missing car' variant where some positions are pre-filled and child finds only the gaps.
assetNeeds: Pip conductor character (idle, wave, cheer, puzzled)

games.title: Numeral Kingdom Builder
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A tiny king needs his castle flags numbered correctly. Each flag planted earns a royal fanfare and a villager who waves from a window. The kingdom fills up with cheerful characters as numbers 0-20 get placed.
games.mechanic: A diorama of a castle courtyard has 20 flag poles. A number card is shown; the child picks the matching numeral tile from a scattered pile and drags it to the correct pole. Correct: flag unfurls, a sprite appears in a window. Wrong: flag droops briefly, tile returns.
games.freeSample: Free: numerals 0-5, 6 flag poles. Paid: 0-20 full kingdom, plus a 'royal decree' round where the king calls out a number verbally and child finds it without seeing the written prompt.
assetNeeds: Flag pole with unfurling flag animation

games.title: Subitize Soup Kitchen
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Chef Bubble shows a dot arrangement for just one second, then covers it with a pot lid. Child taps the matching numeral on the counter before the soup goes cold. Correct: the pot bubbles over with sparkles and a vegetable jumps out. Each round reveals a panel of a whimsical kitchen mural.
games.mechanic: A dot arrangement (dice, ten-frame, scattered) flashes for 1-2 seconds on a pot, then the lid slams. Child taps 1 of 4 numeral buttons. Correct tap flips one tile of the background mural. Complete the mural to finish the round.
games.freeSample: Free: quantities 1-5, dice patterns only. Paid: quantities 1-10, ten-frame and scattered patterns, mystery bonus tiles that show silly kitchen scenes.
assetNeeds: Chef Bubble character (reveal, lid-slam, cheer, shrug)
Vegetable jump-out sprites (carrot, pea pod, mushroom)

games.title: More or Fewer Picnic
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two hungry picnic animals — Ant and Grasshopper — each have a plate. Child feeds the one with MORE ants (or fewer) the matching sandwich. The winner does a little happy wiggle; the other gets a crumb anyway so nobody feels left out.
games.mechanic: Two plates appear, each showing a different quantity (dot sets or numerals per round). A prompt asks 'Feed the one with MORE' or 'Feed the one with FEWER.' Child drags a sandwich to the correct plate. Correct: happy nibble animation. Wrong: gentle 'hmm' and the sandwich floats back.
games.freeSample: Free: dot-set comparisons within 5. Paid: dot sets to 10, numeral comparisons to 20, and mixed dot-vs-numeral rounds.
assetNeeds: Ant character (idle, nibble, happy wiggle, crumb-catch)
Grasshopper character (idle, nibble, happy wiggle, crumb-catch)

games.title: Decompose the Dragon's Hoard
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A friendly dragon hoards gems and needs to split them into two piles. Child drags gems into two treasure chests to make a target total — any valid split works! The dragon does a proud puff of sparkle-smoke and a gem crown pops onto its head for each new decomposition found.
games.mechanic: A target number (2-10) is shown. A row of gem sprites sits above two labeled chests. Child drags gems to fill both chests; a running total shows in each. When both totals sum to the target the dragon celebrates and a new decomposition is logged on a 'hoard chart.' Multiple correct splits per target number.
games.freeSample: Free: target numbers 2-5, unlimited tries, no chart. Paid: targets 2-10, decomposition chart fills with each new split found, 'challenge mode' where one chest is pre-filled and child finds the missing part.
assetNeeds: Friendly dragon character (idle, puff sparkle, crown pop, proud pose)
Two treasure chest sprites (open, filling animation)

games.title: Make 10 Rocket Launch
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A rocket needs exactly 10 fuel cells to launch. Some are already loaded; child taps to add the rest. Each cell clicks into place with a satisfying clunk and the fuel gauge rises. At 10 the rocket ignites with a wobbly rumble and blasts off leaving a trail of stars.
games.mechanic: A rocket with a 10-cell fuel bay is shown, N cells pre-filled (N from 1-9). Child taps fuel cells in the empty bays to fill exactly 10 minus N. A numeral readout shows current count. Adding too many triggers a gentle 'overload' fizz; the extras pop out. Correct fill = launch sequence.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 rounds with N=1 to 5 (needs 9 down to 5 more). Paid: all 9 combinations, plus a 'mission log' that collects all 9 as patches on a mission board.
assetNeeds: 10-cell fuel bay UI (cells light up individually)

games.title: Creature Addition Lab
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Professor Zap's lab machine takes two groups of tiny creatures, smooshes them together with flashing gears and a 'zzap,' and out pops the combined group. Child decides how many go in each funnel, or predicts the total from the output chute.
games.mechanic: Two funnel slots accept creature sprites (child drags from a tray, up to 5 in each). A lever pull triggers the machine's combine animation. The output chute shows the combined group and a blank numeral tile; child taps the correct total from 4 choices. Alternatively, a sum is shown in the output and child fills the two funnels to match.
games.freeSample: Free: sums within 5 (drag-and-predict mode). Paid: sums within 10, reverse 'fill-the-funnels' mode, and a 'fastest formula' challenge where correct answers are banked into a collection notebook.
assetNeeds: Professor Zap character (idle, pull-lever, cheer, puzzled)
Two funnel slots with creature-drop animation
Creature sprite (small round blob, 3 color variants)

games.title: Subtraction Pond Splash
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Lily-pad frogs leap away one by one each round. Child watches the group shrink and taps the numeral that shows how many remain. A correct tap sends a happy frog chorus ribbit; a wrong tap makes a single frog look confused and hop in place.
games.mechanic: A pond scene shows N frogs on lily pads (N from 2-10). An animation removes M frogs (they leap off-screen with a splash). Child taps the correct 'remaining' numeral from 4 floating bubbles. Each correct round fills one panel of a frog-pond diorama.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 rounds, start quantities 2-5. Paid: start quantities 2-10, including 'subtract 0' and 'subtract all' special rounds, plus a 'lily-pad mosaic' that unlocks with each correct answer.
assetNeeds: Frog sprite (sit, leap, splash, chorus-ribbit, confused-hop)

games.title: Word Problem Story Theater
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two puppet characters act out a simple add-or-subtract story on a tiny stage. After the story plays, child taps the puppet showing the correct answer. The winning puppet takes a bow and a backdrop swaps to show the next story scene.
games.mechanic: A 2-panel puppet-show plays: panel 1 shows the starting group as puppets, panel 2 shows the change (more arrive or some leave). Child then taps the correct numeral answer from 3 numeral puppets that pop up on the stage curtain. Correct: curtain call celebration. Wrong: puppets shake heads, scene replays.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 stories, sums/differences within 5. Paid: 12 stories, within 10, two story 'genres' (forest animals, space aliens), plus a 'build your own' mode where child picks how many arrive/leave.
assetNeeds: Stage curtain backdrop (2 themes: forest, space)
Numeral puppet UI (3 cards on curtain rod)

games.title: Shape Sort Safari
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Shapes are lost animals that need to find their matching habitat shelter. Each correct sort triggers a little 'ahh, home at last!' settle-in animation. Wrong sorts gently wander back asking 'do I belong here?'
games.mechanic: 3 labeled bins (triangle, square, circle — or 2D vs 3D in later rounds). Shapes drift down from the top. Child drags each to its bin. Every 5 correct sorts adds a decoration to the habitat and a new animal mascot appears inside.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 shapes (circle, square, triangle), 10 rounds. Paid: all 6 target shapes (adding rectangle, hexagon, cone/sphere/cube for 3D), plus 'shape in disguise' rounds where the shape is rotated or colored differently.
assetNeeds: Shape animal mascots (triangle fox, circle owl, square bear, rectangle wolf, hexagon bee, sphere seal, cone penguin)

games.title: Geometry Architect Diorama
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A tiny city needs buildings assembled from named shapes. Each correctly placed shape snaps in with a satisfying click and a friendly construction-worker sprite cheers. The skyline grows across the diorama as more shapes are placed.
games.mechanic: A diorama backdrop shows building outlines with labeled silhouettes. A tray of named shape tiles sits below. Child drags each shape to its matching labeled silhouette. Correct: snap + cheer. When a building is complete a flag pops up and residents wave from windows.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 buildings using circle, square, triangle. Paid: 8 buildings, all 6 shapes, a 'describe it' mode where child hears a property clue ('4 equal sides') and selects the matching shape tile.

games.title: Shape Composer Studio
games.subject: math
games.funHook: An art-robot needs its portrait made — but only from shapes! Child drags triangles, squares, and rectangles onto a canvas to match a target shape-portrait. The robot wiggles when the right pieces are placed and takes a selfie at the end.
games.mechanic: A ghost-outline portrait is shown (e.g., a house from triangle+square, a rocket from rectangle+triangle). A tray of shapes sits below. Child drags pieces to fill the ghost outline; snap-assist pulls pieces into place when close. Complete: robot selfie flash + 'my masterpiece' display frame.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 portraits using 2 shapes each. Paid: 10 portraits using 3-5 shapes, a 'free compose' mode with no ghost outline (open-ended creation that triggers a random robot compliment).
assetNeeds: Art-robot character (idle, wiggle, selfie flash, compliment pose)
Shape tile set (triangle, square, rectangle, circle, hexagon)

games.title: Measurement Market Stall
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A market vendor needs to sort vegetables by height (tall/short) and weight (heavy/light). Each correctly sorted veggie earns a coin that clinks into the vendor's jar. The jar fills and eventually tips over with a shower of coins and confetti.
games.mechanic: Pairs of objects appear side by side. A prompt card reads 'Which is TALLER?' or 'Which is HEAVIER?' Child taps the correct object or drags it to a labeled bin. Correct: coin clink. Wrong: vendor shakes head, objects reset. Each 5 correct sorts add a decoration to the market stall.
games.freeSample: Free: taller/shorter comparisons (height attribute only). Paid: heavier/lighter, longer/shorter, and mixed attribute rounds, plus a 'measure with cubes' mode where child stacks non-standard units alongside an object.
assetNeeds: Market vendor character (idle, coin clink, shake head, confetti toss)
Vegetable sprite set (carrot/tomato/pumpkin/bean in 2 sizes each)

games.title: Data Creature Census
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A zookeeper needs a creature census! Child sorts colorful critters into labeled pens, then the chart board auto-fills. At the end the zookeeper reads the chart with funny commentary ('Wow, SO many turtles!'). Tapping the chart bars makes the creatures in that pen wave.
games.mechanic: A set of 8-12 mixed creature sprites appears in a jumble. Three labeled pens sit below (e.g., wings / no wings / fins). Child drags each creature to its pen. After all are sorted, a bar chart auto-builds column by column with a pop for each unit. A question prompt then asks which group has most/fewest.
games.freeSample: Free: 2-category sort (wings/no wings), 8 creatures. Paid: 3-category sorts, 12 creatures, 3 different census themes (creatures, vehicles, foods), plus Q&A follow-up questions.
assetNeeds: Zookeeper character (idle, point, commentary bubble, laugh)
3 themed creature sets (8 creatures each: animals, vehicles, foods)
Bar chart board with per-unit pop animation

games.title: Number Bond Treehouse
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A treehouse grows a new branch and bird house for every number bond the child completes. The whole tree is eventually alive with colorful birds. Tapping any placed bird makes it sing a little trill.
games.mechanic: A number bond diagram appears with a whole number at the top and two empty branch circles below. Child taps numbered acorns from a tray and drops them into the circles so the two parts sum to the whole (any valid pair accepted). Correct pair: new branch sprouts + a bird flies in. Whole = 2-10, cycling through all decompositions.
games.freeSample: Free: whole numbers 2-5, 5 bonds. Paid: whole numbers 2-10, all bonds, treehouse grows through 4 stages, and a 'missing part' variant where one circle is filled and child finds the other.
assetNeeds: Treehouse (4 growth stages: sapling, small tree, big tree, full treehouse)

games.title: Ten-Frame Village
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A friendly mayor wants to fill a village with exactly 10 cottages per row, then start the next row. Each cottage placed pops open its chimney and smokes. When a row of 10 fills, a little parade of villagers marches through. The second row represents the 'tens' concept concretely.
games.mechanic: A ten-frame grid is the village layout. Cottages (ones) are dragged from a tray and placed in cells left-to-right, top row first. A running numeral and 'tens + ones' display updates live. The prompt asks the child to build a specific number (11-19) using the ten-frame. Filling row 1 triggers the parade automatically.
games.freeSample: Free: numbers 11-15, one row already filled. Paid: numbers 11-19 from scratch, plus a 'how many?' reveal mode where cottages are pre-placed and child reads the number.

games.title: Counting-On Caterpillar Path
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Clover the caterpillar is inching along a number-path garden. Child taps numbered leaves to continue the count from wherever Clover stopped. Each correct leaf tap makes Clover inch forward with a wobble, and the leaf turns into a flower. A mis-tap makes a leaf shake and Clover peeks back questioningly.
games.mechanic: A winding path of 20 leaf segments is shown, numbered leaves appearing blank. Clover sits on leaf N (randomly 1-15). The next 3-5 leaves need to be tapped in counting order to name them. Each tap reveals a numeral and Clover advances. Completing the path reaches a garden gate that swings open.
games.freeSample: Free: start from 1, count to 5. Paid: count-on from any start 1-15 through 20, plus a 'count by 2s/5s/10s preview' variant that plants striped flowers on the skip-count leaves.
assetNeeds: Clover caterpillar character (inch-forward, wobble, peek-back, cheer)
Numeral reveal pop on each leaf

games.title: Sticker Numeral Collection
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A 'Numeral Kingdom' sticker album has 21 silhouette slots (0-20). Each is shaped like a fun character doing something goofy matching its number (zero is a sleeping ghost, one is a tiny unicorn, etc.). Child earns a sticker by tapping the right numeral when shown a matching dot group.
games.mechanic: A dot arrangement (1-20) is shown on a card. Four numeral choices appear below. Child taps the correct numeral. Correct: the matching sticker peels and slaps into its silhouette with a shimmer. Wrong: gentle wrong-tone, another attempt. Tapping any collected sticker plays a silly fact (for 7: 'Seven is lucky!'). Album fills left-to-right.
games.freeSample: Free: stickers 0-5. Paid: stickers 6-20, alternate ten-frame and tally representations, plus a secret 'foil sticker' variant at 0, 10, 20.
assetNeeds: 21 numeral character sticker designs (0=sleeping ghost, 1=unicorn, 2=duck pair, 3=triplet cats... through 20)

games.title: Attribute Fashion Show
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A character needs to be dressed according to attribute clues ('wear something BLUE and ROUND'). Each correctly placed accessory gets a cheer and an applause sound. When fully dressed per the clues the character struts a catwalk with sparkles.
games.mechanic: A character stands in a dressing room. A prompt card describes attribute clues (color + shape, or size + color). A tray of 6 accessory options is below (some matching, some not). Child drags only the matching accessories to the character's placement spots. Mis-matches bounce back. Catwalk strut triggers when all spots are correctly filled.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 rounds, single attribute (color only). Paid: 12 rounds, two-attribute clues, 3 different character types (robot, monster, human), plus a 'design your own' open mode.
assetNeeds: Accessory sprite set (hats, scarves, buttons, patches — in 4 colors, 3 shapes, 2 sizes each)

games.title: Pattern Parade Float
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A parade float needs its banners and decorations in a perfect AB or ABC pattern. Each correctly placed decoration makes a confetti burst and a marching-band member honks a horn. When the float is complete it rolls away down the parade route.
games.mechanic: A float outline has 8-12 blank decoration spots arranged in a row. A pattern starter (e.g., star-circle-star-circle-?) is shown. A tray of decoration sprites sits below. Child drags the next element to the '?' spot. Correct: confetti burst, next blank appears. Wrong: gentle wobble, sprite returns. Float completes when all blanks are filled correctly.
games.freeSample: Free: AB patterns, 6 decoration spots. Paid: AB patterns to 12 spots, ABB, ABC, and AABB patterns, plus a 'what comes next?' tap mode where the pattern extends off-screen and child predicts.
assetNeeds: Decoration sprite set (6 shapes in 3 colors)

games.title: Add-and-Match Bakery
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A bakery display has two columns: picture groups on the left and numeral sum-cards on the right. Child taps a left card, then the matching right card. A correct pair fuses into a frosted cake and slides to the display shelf. Wrong pair gives a friendly 'not quite yet!' wobble.
games.mechanic: 4 pairs on screen at once. Left cards show picture equations (2 muffins + 3 muffins). Right cards show numerals (5). Tap one from each column to test; correct pair animates into a cake and locks. All pairs matched = shelf full = baker celebration. Shuffle after each full set.
games.freeSample: Free: sums within 5, 4 pairs. Paid: sums within 10, 6-pair rounds, and a 'subtraction bakery' variant where left cards show take-away scenes and right cards show remainders.

games.title: Neighborhood Number Hunt
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A busy neighborhood scene hides objects everywhere. The prompt ('Find exactly 4 bicycles!') sends child hunting. Each found object is circled with a glowing ring and a happy ding. Finding exactly the right count triggers a neighborhood party — banners unfurl and residents cheer.
games.mechanic: A scrollable neighborhood scene with 10-20 hidden objects of a target type. A prompt specifies an exact count to find (e.g., 'Find 4 bicycles'). Child taps matching objects; a tally counter fills. Tapping a 4th object when 3 are already found (if there are decoys) allows comparison. Finding exact count triggers celebration.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 scene, counts 1-3. Paid: 4 scenes (neighborhood, park, market, school), counts 1-10, a 'more or fewer' variant that asks 'which type has more?'
assetNeeds: Hidden object sprite sets per scene (6 types, 1-10 instances each)

games.title: Tallying Toad Explorer
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Explorer Toad discovers creatures on an expedition and tally-marks them in a field journal. Each tally mark drawn by the child reveals a new creature sprite on the scene backdrop. When all 5 tallies for a group are done a bundle tie appears with a satisfying snap.
games.mechanic: A scene shows creatures wandering by one at a time. Child drags a tally mark onto the journal page for each creature. After every 4 marks the child draws a diagonal 'bundle' stroke. The journal auto-labels the bundle group with a numeral. After 3-5 creature types are tallied, the explorer reads back the totals.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 creature type, count to 5. Paid: 3 creature types simultaneously, counts to 10, comparison questions after tallying.
assetNeeds: Explorer Toad character (idle, point, read-journal, bundle-snap cheer)
Field journal UI with tally-mark drawing area
Creature sprites (frog, dragonfly, snail — each 5 instances)

games.title: Magic Adding Machine
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A whimsical machine with a big crank takes two groups of critters dropped in two funnels, smooshes them with blinking gears and a 'PING!', and spits a combined group out the bottom chute. Child predicts the output and then pulls the lever to check — the match triggers a confetti shower.
games.mechanic: Two funnel slots are shown. Critter sprites appear in each funnel (auto-filled or drag-filled depending on round). Child counts the input groups, then taps a predicted total from 3 options. Then they pull the lever: the machine combines and the output emerges. Match = confetti. Miss = machine shows a re-count hint.
games.freeSample: Free: sums within 5, machine pre-fills funnels. Paid: sums within 10, child drag-fills funnels themselves, and a 'secret funnel' variant where one funnel is hidden and child infers the hidden addend.
assetNeeds: Whimsical machine sprite (gears, blinking lights, crank animation)

games.title: Caterpillar Skip-Count Sprout
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A caterpillar grows a new body segment with each number in a skip-count sequence. Child taps the next number to add the segment. When the caterpillar reaches the target length it transforms into a butterfly with a dramatic shimmer.
games.mechanic: A caterpillar head sits at left. A sequence starts (2, 4, 6, ?). A prompt shows the next missing number blank. Child taps the correct numeral from 3 leaf-numeral options floating nearby. Correct: new segment pops on with a satisfying extend. Wrong: leaf wilts, returns. Complete sequence = butterfly metamorphosis animation.
games.freeSample: Free: count by 1s to 10. Paid: count by 2s (to 20), 5s (to 50), 10s (to 100), and a reverse countdown variant.
assetNeeds: Caterpillar body segment sprite (repeating, 5 color variants)
Floating numeral leaf sprite (3 options per round)

games.title: 3D Shape Reveal Mystery Box
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A mystery box slowly spins open to reveal a 3D shape. Before it fully opens, child taps its name. Correct: box explodes in sparkles and the shape does a little roll/bounce celebration. Each correct answer uncovers one panel of a 'shape museum' mural.
games.mechanic: A rotating mystery box silhouette gives visual hints (shadow, partial edge). Child taps the shape name from 4 options (cube, sphere, cone, cylinder, rectangular prism). Correct tap = full reveal + mural panel uncovers. 12 panels total, 3 rounds per shape type to reinforce. Wrong: box stays mostly closed, one more hint appears.
games.freeSample: Free: cube and sphere only, 6 rounds. Paid: all 5 shapes, 20 rounds, a 'real world' variant showing a photo clue instead of the shape silhouette.
assetNeeds: 5 animated 3D shape sprites (cube, sphere, cone, cylinder, rectangular prism — each with idle roll/bounce)
Mystery box sprite (spinning silhouette reveal stages)
Shape museum mural (12 panels, whimsical scene)

games.title: Shape Spy in the City
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Agent Dot (a tiny magnifying-glass character) needs shapes spotted in a city scene. Each found shape is highlighted with a detective ring and labeled. Finding all of one shape type makes it 'classified' on a case board. Complete the case board to close the mission.
games.mechanic: A city scene (buildings, park, road) contains 15-20 embedded shapes. A prompt ('Find all triangles') sends child hunting. Tap on each matching shape: glow ring + label pop. After all triangles are found, the case board logs 'TRIANGLES: CLASSIFIED.' Next shape mission begins.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 scene, find circles and squares. Paid: 3 scenes (city, park, kitchen), 6 shapes total, a '3D shapes in the wild' variant where real-world objects are silhouetted.
assetNeeds: Agent Dot character (idle, point, cheer, magnifying-glass raise)
Hidden shape highlights embedded in scenes
Case board UI with classified stamps

games.title: Comparing Length Critter Race
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two critters race along paths of different lengths. Before they start, child must predict which path is longer/shorter. Correct prediction = the child's chosen critter wins the race and does a victory lap. Both critters get a finish banner regardless (no loser shaming).
games.mechanic: Two winding or straight paths of clearly different lengths are shown side by side. Prompt: 'Which path is LONGER?' Child taps. Then a button starts the race — the longer-path critter takes more steps/time. Correct prediction = celebration. Wrong: 'good try!' and a replay to observe again. After 5 rounds, child unlocks a 'design your own track' editor.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 rounds, very obvious length differences. Paid: 8 rounds, subtle differences, indirect comparison via a third 'measuring rope' tool, 'design your track' editor.
assetNeeds: Two critter racers (turtle, rabbit — both cute, neither villainized)
Race-track backgrounds (2 winding, 2 straight per round)

games.title: Ordinal Rocket Crew
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Astronaut animals need to board the rocket in ordinal order (first, second, third...). Each correctly boarded astronaut waves from the porthole. A mis-board sends the animal sliding back down the ramp with a comic 'whoops!' squeak.
games.mechanic: 5-10 astronaut animals wait in a line. Ordinal position labels (1st, 2nd, 3rd...) are shown on rocket porthole stickers. A prompt ('Who is THIRD?') highlights the correct position. Child drags the correct animal to the correct porthole, or taps the correct one. Correct: wave from porthole. Wrong: slide-down animation. Rocket launches when all portholes are filled.
games.freeSample: Free: 1st through 5th. Paid: 1st through 10th, a 'what position is she in?' variant where the line is fixed and child reads the ordinal number.
assetNeeds: 5-10 astronaut animal sprites (bear, dog, cat, fox, rabbit, owl, penguin, frog, lion, duck)

games.title: Bubble Number Pop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Numerals float inside colorful bubbles that drift gently upward. A prompt card shows a number or dot pattern; child pops all matching numeral bubbles (some rounds: pop the bubbles that are GREATER THAN a given number). Each pop gives a satisfying musical 'bloop.' Clearing all targets releases a fountain of mini bubbles.
games.mechanic: 8-12 numeral bubbles drift. A prompt specifies which to pop: 'Pop the 5s' or 'Pop numbers less than 7.' Child taps matching bubbles only. Wrong tap = gentle boing + re-inflate. Clearing all targets = bubble fountain finale and a new round begins.
games.freeSample: Free: 'pop exact number' only, numerals 1-5. Paid: numerals 0-20, greater-than/less-than variants, 'pop the even numbers' variant.

games.title: Building Tens Skyscraper
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Clank the construction robot is building a skyscraper, one floor (one unit block) at a time. Every 10 floors snaps together into a 'tens rod' with a satisfying metallic clunk and the camera zooms out to show the growing tower. Tapping any finished rod makes it flash and Clank does a thumbs-up.
games.mechanic: Child drags unit blocks (ones) onto the building pad one at a time. A counter tracks the total. At 10, the ones auto-snap into a tens rod with an animation. A two-panel display shows '__ tens and __ ones.' Prompt asks child to build a specific number (11-19, or multiples of 10 to 50 in later rounds).
games.freeSample: Free: build numbers 11-13. Paid: 11-19 and tens to 50, plus a 'show me another way' mode where child breaks a tens rod back into ones.
assetNeeds: Clank robot character (idle, thumbs-up, metallic clunk reaction)
Tens rod sprite (stacked 10 units, snaps together)

games.title: Subtraction Story Snacker
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Nibbles the chipmunk has a pile of acorns; some get eaten each turn. Child watches the acorns disappear one by one into Nibbles' cheeks (visible cheek-puff animation), then taps how many are left. Correct: cheeks deflate with a happy exhale and a tiny victory dance. Wrong: Nibbles looks confused and re-counts aloud.
games.mechanic: A pile of 2-10 acorn sprites is shown. Nibbles eats M acorns one by one (animation). Child taps the correct 'remaining' numeral from 4 choices. Correct: cheek-deflate dance. 5 correct rounds fill Nibbles' 'winter stash' display. Empty stash = new game.
games.freeSample: Free: start quantities 2-5. Paid: start quantities 2-10, including subtract-all and subtract-0 rounds, plus a 'predict before Nibbles eats' mode.
assetNeeds: Nibbles chipmunk character (idle, eat-acorn, cheek-puff, cheek-deflate, dance, confused re-count)

games.title: Addition Path Hopscotch
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Froggo needs to reach the lily pad by hopping along a hopscotch path. Each square shows a number; child adds the current square's value to the previous total to find the next square's label. Correct hop = Froggo leaps with a 'boing.' Complete = Froggo lands on the lily pad and does a splash dive.
games.mechanic: A hopscotch grid of 5 squares is shown. Square 1 = a starting number. Each subsequent square has a blank; child adds the given step-value to get the next (e.g., start 2, +3 = blank). Child taps the correct numeral from 3 hovering options. Correct: Froggo hops. Lily-pad finale triggers after all 5 are correct.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 rounds, add within 5. Paid: add within 10, variable step sizes, a 'subtract back' variant, and a 'help Froggo home' story wrapper.
assetNeeds: Froggo character (idle, hop, boing, splash-dive, lily-pad celebrate)

games.title: Giant's Garden Number Line
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A giant friendly beanstalk stretches from 0 to 20. A tiny climber needs to hop to a target number. Child taps or drags the climber along the stalk nodes. Hopping past the target makes the climber slip back with a comic 'whoops!' Landing exactly on target makes the beanstalk burst into flowers.
games.mechanic: A vertical number line (0-20) is shown as beanstalk nodes. The climber starts at a given number. A prompt specifies the target. Child taps each node in order to hop toward it. Each hop produces a small jump animation and a number label lights up. Over-shoot = slip-back. Exact landing = flower burst.
games.freeSample: Free: 0-10 number line, targets 1-10. Paid: 0-20, 'count back' direction, a 'one more / one less' prompt mode.
assetNeeds: Tiny climber character (hop, slip-back, flower-burst celebrate)
Number label lights for each node

games.title: Zero the Hero Collection
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Zero the Hero is a fun character who shows up whenever there are NONE. A sticker album pairs each numeral 0-10 with its 'hero moment' — Zero gets a big special foil sticker. Child earns stickers by recognizing numerals and matching them to empty sets or dot sets. Tapping Zero always triggers a heroic fanfare.
games.mechanic: A prompt shows a dot arrangement (including empty-set = 0). Child taps the matching numeral from 4 choices. Correct: the corresponding hero sticker peels into its album slot. Special: the 0 sticker is foil and triggers a fanfare. Tapping any collected sticker plays a one-liner ('Four is fantastic!'). Album fills 0-10.
games.freeSample: Free: stickers 0-5 including Zero. Paid: stickers 0-10, dot+tally+ten-frame mixed representations.

games.title: Shape Attribute Sorting Runway
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Shapes are runway models judged by a property: number of sides, corners (vertices), or curve-vs-straight. Each shape correctly sorted struts to its bin with a runway walk animation and a cheer from a tiny crowd. Sorting the whole set fills the crowd with cheering fans.
games.mechanic: 3 bins labeled by attribute (e.g., '3 sides', '4 sides', 'curved'). Shape sprites enter from the left one at a time. Child drags to the correct bin. Correct: runway strut animation. Wrong: gentle 'hmm, count again' wobble with a sides-counter hint appearing. After 10 correct sorts the crowd is full.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 bins (has corners / no corners). Paid: 3 bins (3 sides / 4 sides / curved), side-count variant, vertex-count variant.
assetNeeds: Shape sprite set (triangle, square, rectangle, circle, hexagon, pentagon — varied colors/sizes)

games.title: Friendly Fraction Snacks
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two best friends share a snack equally. Child drags the cutting line to split the snack into 2 equal pieces, then feeds one piece to each friend. Both friends do a happy nibble dance. Unequal cuts make one friend look sad (gently — no shame) while the other looks puzzled.
games.mechanic: A food item (pizza, cookie, sandwich) appears on a cutting board. A dotted guide shows 'equal halves'; child drags a knife along it to cut. The two pieces are highlighted. Child drags one piece to each friend. Equal split: both dance. Visually unequal: a hint overlay shows the dotted guide re-appearing.
games.freeSample: Free: round pizza (clearest equal halves). Paid: rectangle sandwich, square brownie, triangle wrap, a 'quarters' variant splitting into 4 for 4 friends.
assetNeeds: 2 friend characters (bear + bunny, idle, nibble, dance, sad-puzzled)
Food sprites (pizza, sandwich, brownie, wrap — whole + two-halves + four-quarters variants)

games.title: Two-Part Story Problem Puppet
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two puppets act out a simple add/subtract story. After the two-part story plays, child chooses the correct answer panel and the puppets celebrate by doing a synchronized silly dance. Child can then replay the story — the puppets re-enact it with extra flair on repeat.
games.mechanic: A puppet stage shows a 3-panel story strip (panel 1: starting group, panel 2: change event, panel 3: question). Child taps each panel in order to advance the animation. Then 3 answer panels appear at the bottom; child taps the correct total/remainder. Correct: puppet dance. Wrong: story replays from panel 1 with a 'let's look again!' prompt.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 stories, sums/differences within 5. Paid: 12 stories, within 10, two themes (farm animals, sea creatures), and a 'fill the blank panel' mode where child creates the story ending.
assetNeeds: Silly synchronized dance animation for both puppets

games.title: Coin Collection Creature Shop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A creature shop has silly pets for sale with price tags (1-5 'coins'). Child sorts and counts coins to buy each creature. Bought creatures go into a 'My Pets' sticker album. Each pet has an idle animation and a funny name-tag. Tapping any pet triggers a silly interaction.
games.mechanic: A pet is shown with a price (1-5 coin stickers). A tray of coin stickers sits below. Child drags exactly that many coins to the payment slot. Correct count: ka-ching animation, pet sticker peels into album. Over/under: coins gently return with a 'not quite!' bounce. Album fills to 10 pets.
games.freeSample: Free: pets costing 1-3 coins. Paid: pets costing 1-5, a 'make change' variant where child starts with more coins than needed and picks the right ones.
assetNeeds: 10 silly creature designs (each with idle + tap-interaction animation)
My Pets album page (10 silhouette slots)

games.title: Longer/Shorter Wand Workshop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A wizard needs a wand of EXACTLY the right length. Child adds or removes segments until the wand matches the target length shown by a comparison bar. Each correctly-sized wand shoots a sparkle burst. Too long: sparks fizzle. Too short: sparkles droop.
games.mechanic: A target wand length is shown (displayed as a comparison bar of colored units). A child's wand starts at 0 segments. Child taps '+' to add a segment or '-' to remove one. A length readout in unit squares updates. When child's wand matches the target, a 'MATCH!' banner pops and the wand shoots sparks. New target appears.
games.freeSample: Free: target lengths 1-5 unit segments. Paid: target lengths 1-10, indirect comparison variant where two wands are compared without direct overlap, and a 'guess then check' prediction mode.
assetNeeds: Wizard character (idle, match-celebrate, too-long fizzle, too-short droop)

games.title: Subitize Stargazer
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Stars flash briefly on the night sky (1-10 stars, in constellation patterns). Child quickly taps the right number on a numeral telescope. Correct: the telescope zooms in and a silly constellation character wakes up and waves. Each correct answer maps to one constellation on the star map, slowly revealing the full sky.
games.mechanic: Stars flash for 1.5 seconds in a constellation shape, then disappear. Child taps 1 of 5 numeral buttons on the telescope. Correct: zoom animation, constellation character waves, one star-map tile revealed. Wrong: gentle 'squint harder!' and a second flash at slower speed. 12 tiles total for the full star map.
games.freeSample: Free: quantities 1-5, standard dot patterns. Paid: quantities 1-10, constellation arrangements, a 'double constellation' variant showing two groups to add.
assetNeeds: 12 constellation characters (one per star-map tile, each with a wave animation)
Night sky star-map background (12 tile overlay)
Star flash sprites (1-10 stars, constellation arrangements)

games.title: Positional Word Treasure Hunt
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Captain Pearl hid treasure and gives position clues ('The coin is BEHIND the barrel, ABOVE the net!'). Child taps where the treasure must be. Correct location: treasure chest pops up with a glitter burst and coins spill out. Wrong tap: gentle 'hmm, look at the clue again!' and the clue highlights.
games.mechanic: A ship-deck scene with objects (barrel, net, crate, anchor). Captain Pearl gives a two-part positional clue (above/below + in front of/behind). Child taps the correct zone. Correct: treasure chest pop + coins. Wrong: clue word glows as a re-read hint. 10 treasure locations per round.
games.freeSample: Free: single-position clues (above/below), 4 rounds. Paid: two-position clues, 10 rounds, 3 scene variants (ship deck, pirate cave, market), 'beside' and 'next to' vocabulary.
assetNeeds: Scene objects (barrel, net, crate, anchor, chest)

games.title: Doubles Domino Dash
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Domino tiles drift across a playful game board. Child matches each doubles domino (same dot count on both halves) with its sum. A correct match makes both tiles snap together with a magnetic click and do a tiny spin. Non-match tiles bounce apart with a comic boing. Completing the set triggers a domino-topple chain animation.
games.mechanic: 8 domino tiles and 8 sum-numeral cards are face-down in a 4x4 grid. Child flips two cards to test a match: a doubles domino (2+2, 3+3, etc.) with its sum (4, 6, etc.). Match = spin + lock. Non-match = flip back. Clear all pairs = domino-topple chain celebration. Doubles from 1+1 to 5+5.
games.freeSample: Free: doubles 1+1, 2+2, 3+3 (6 pairs). Paid: doubles 1+1 through 5+5 (10 pairs), a 'near-doubles' variant (2+3, 3+4), and a speed-find mode (no flip, all visible, tap-pairs-directly).
assetNeeds: Domino tile sprites (all doubles 1-5, with dot patterns)

games.title: Number Bond Pop Factory
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A candy factory shoots numbered candy balls up through tubes. Child pops the pairs that sum to the target number. Wrong pops make the candy ball return with a sticky wobble; right pops make both balls fuse into a golden candy and drop into the collection jar. Fill the jar to complete the round.
games.mechanic: A target sum is displayed (e.g., 7). Numbered candy balls (0-10) drift upward from tubes. Child pops two that sum to the target; they must be popped in sequence. A 'held' indicator shows the first ball selected. Second ball popped: if sum=target, golden fusion + jar fill. If not, both return. Fill jar to 10 to finish.
games.freeSample: Free: target sum 5, balls 0-5. Paid: target sums 5-10, balls 0-10, 'mystery target' variant where target is hidden and child discovers it by finding any pair.
assetNeeds: Candy ball sprites (numbered 0-10, each a distinct color)

games.title: Monster Mouth Comparing Game
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Chomp Monster always eats the BIGGER number (the monster's mouth is shaped like a > sign). Child drags the correct number card into Chomp's mouth. Correct: Chomp gulps with an exaggerated NOM and does a happy belly-jiggle. Wrong: Chomp spits it out with a raspberry and wags a 'not the bigger one!' finger.
games.mechanic: Two numeral cards or dot-group cards appear. Child drags the larger one into Chomp's open mouth (shaped like a > sign, reinforcing the symbol visually). Correct: NOM + belly-jiggle. Wrong: spit + raspberry. A 'comparison sentence' strips below after each correct answer: '7 > 4.' Builds number sense AND inequality symbol.
games.freeSample: Free: numerals 1-5. Paid: numerals 1-20, dot-set comparisons, 'equal' rounds (Chomp closes mouth for equal sets), and a 'who eats less?' mode training < symbol.
assetNeeds: Chomp Monster character (mouth shaped as >, NOM animation, belly-jiggle, spit-raspberry, wag-finger)

games.title: Place Value Packing Machine
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Packer the robot groups loose blocks into packs of 10 as they fall down a conveyor belt. Child pulls the lever to trigger the pack when exactly 10 arrive. A pack of 10 slides to the 'tens shelf' with a click. The ones left over sit in the 'ones tray.' Child reads the two-digit display.
games.mechanic: Blocks fall one at a time onto a conveyor (child taps to advance each). At 10, child pulls the lever and the 10 auto-pack into a rod. The display shows '__ tens __ ones.' After packing, a numeral card is shown; child reads it from a 3-choice tap. Correct: Packer robot does a thumbs-up spin.
games.freeSample: Free: only one pack (numbers 10-19). Paid: two packs (numbers 10-29), a 'broken packs' variant where packs arrive pre-assembled and child un-packs to count ones.
assetNeeds: Packer robot character (idle, thumbs-up spin, lever-pull)

games.title: Hidden Addend Detective
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Detective Squirrel hides acorns in TWO boxes. Child can see one box (how many are visible) and knows the total; they deduce the hidden box's count. Revealing the hidden box with a correct answer triggers a 'CASE SOLVED!' stamp and a magnifying glass flourish.
games.mechanic: Two boxes are shown. One is open (showing N acorns). One is covered with a question mark. Total is displayed above. Child taps the correct missing-addend numeral from 3 choices. Correct: box opens, CASE SOLVED stamp, next hidden-addend puzzle appears. Each solve adds a sticker to the detective board (10 stickers = case closed).
games.freeSample: Free: totals within 5, 5 cases. Paid: totals within 10, detective board with 10 stickers, and a 'two hidden boxes' variant showing only the total and child distributes both.
assetNeeds: Detective Squirrel character (idle, magnifying-glass, CASE SOLVED stamp)
Two mystery box sprites (open, closed with question-mark)

games.title: Tessellation Tile Maker
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A mosaic artist needs the canvas filled with matching shapes — no gaps! Child drags shape tiles to fill a grid outline exactly. Each correctly placed tile flashes a color and adds a cheering mosaic character in the corner. Complete the mosaic to see it frame up as a gallery piece.
games.mechanic: A grid outline (4x4 or 5x4) made of a single shape type (squares, triangles, hexagons) has several tiles pre-placed. Child drags matching tiles from a tray to fill the gaps. Snap-assist pulls tiles to the correct slot when close. Wrong shape: bounces back. Full grid = gallery-frame animation + mosaic 'opening night' fanfare.
games.freeSample: Free: 4x4 square grid, 8 tiles to place. Paid: triangle + hexagon grids, mixed shapes (squares + triangles together), free-compose mode with no outline grid.
assetNeeds: Mosaic artist character (idle, color-flash cheer, gallery-bow)
Shape tile sprites (6 colors per shape)
Mosaic character corner decoration (tiny artist in corner)

games.title: Wiggle the Words
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A silly worm character burrows left-to-right across a giant sentence scroll; the child taps each word as the worm touches it, and tapped words wiggle and giggle. Mis-tapping a letter (not a word) makes the worm sneeze confetti.
games.mechanic: A sentence is displayed on a scroll. Child taps each printed word in left-to-right order as Wormy the worm marches across. Spaces between words glow as Wormy passes. After completing a sentence the scroll unfurls to reveal the next, building a tiny storybook page by page. Tap a letter-gap by mistake and Wormy giggles but keeps going — no penalty.
games.freeSample: Free: first 2 sentences (3 words each) with Wormy's intro animation. Paid: full 8-sentence storybook across 4 scenes, plus a replayable 'silly sentences' mode with nonsense word combos.
assetNeeds: Wormy the cartoon worm character (idle, march-left, march-right, sneeze, celebrate)

games.title: Open the Book Shop
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cheerful bookseller bear needs help arranging the book shop before opening. The child solves print-concept tasks (find the front cover, find the title, point to where reading starts) to earn each book, which pops into a shelf slot in the cozy diorama shop.
games.mechanic: Each round presents a book prop (cover, spine, title page, last page). A prompt card asks 'Where do we start reading?' or 'Which is the title?' The child taps the correct element. Correct answers dock a cute book sprite onto the shop shelf. The shop fills, and when all shelves are full the bear does a happy 'OPEN!' dance.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 rounds (front cover + title identification) and half the shelf filled. Paid: all 12 rounds covering front cover, back cover, title, author, illustrator, first word, last page, spine — plus a free-browse mode where child can tap any placed book for a 3-panel micro-story.
assetNeeds: Bookseller bear character (idle, happy, dance, pointing)
6 cartoon book prop sprites (cover, spine, title page visible)

games.title: Rhyme Rocket Launch
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A tiny alien rocket only launches when you feed it a rhyming word-pair as fuel. Drop two rhyming picture cards into the fuel hatch; the rocket sputters, blasts off with a whoooosh, and a little alien waves from the porthole. Feed it a non-rhyme and the rocket politely spits it back with a 'bloop' and a head-shake.
games.mechanic: A tray of 6 picture cards slides in. The child drags pairs into the rocket's twin fuel slots. When both slots hold a rhyming pair (cat/hat, log/frog, cake/snake) the launch button lights up and the child taps it for liftoff. Three successful launches complete a level and unlock a new planet destination. Non-rhyming pairs bounce back gently.
games.freeSample: Free: planet Earth launch (3 pairs: cat/hat, log/frog, sun/bun). Paid: 5 planets × 4 pairs each (20 rhyme pairs total) plus a 'make a rhyme' mode where the child taps one picture and 3 candidate pictures appear.
assetNeeds: Cartoon rocket ship with fuel hatch (idle, fuel-loading, launching, orbiting)
tiny alien character waving from porthole
