5 planet destination backgrounds (moon, Mars, ice planet, jungle moon, lava planet)
rhyme-pair picture card sprites (12 pairs minimum: cat, hat, log, frog, cake, snake, king, ring, bee, tree, duck, truck, bug, rug, fish, dish)

games.title: Syllable Stomp Parade
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A marching band of animal musicians parades along a path. Each stop shows a picture card; the child taps the correct number of stomp-pads (1, 2, or 3) to match the syllable count. Correct count = the drum-elephant stomps that many beats and the whole band lurches forward with a triumphant toot.
games.mechanic: Character arrives at a parade stop with a picture (cat=1, robot=2, banana=3). Three stomp-pads glow on screen labeled 1, 2, 3. Child taps the pad matching the syllable count. On correct: elephant drummer stomps N times with big bass-drum booms, and the parade advances. Wrong: a gentle 'boing' and the prompt replays. After 8 correct the parade reaches the bandstand for a big finale.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 stops (cat, dog, rabbit, umbrella — covering 1 and 2 syllables). Paid: full 16-stop parade covering 1-3 syllables with all animal band members unlocked, plus a 'conduct the band' free-play mode.
assetNeeds: Elephant drummer character (idle, stomp-1, stomp-2, stomp-3, celebrate)
4 animal band member sprites (trumpet rabbit, tuba frog, cymbals bear, flute bird)
parade path background (town street with decorations)

games.title: Phoneme Pop Party
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A party scene fills with floating balloons, each carrying a tiny picture. The DJ announces 'pop every picture that starts with /s/!' — children tap the matching balloons; they burst into confetti stars. The DJ dances harder with each correct pop.
games.mechanic: 8-12 balloons drift across a party scene, each with a picture. The DJ announces an initial or final phoneme ('pop the /m/ ones!'). Child taps all matching balloons; correct pops burst with confetti; wrong pops do a gentle 'boing' and reinflate. When all targets are popped, the DJ throws a mini celebration. Next round changes the target phoneme.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 rounds targeting /s/, /m/, /t/ initial sounds. Paid: 20 rounds covering all initial consonants, 6 rounds for final sounds, 4 rounds for medial vowels, plus a 'mystery phoneme' mode where the child hears a sound and must identify the picture whose word contains it.
assetNeeds: DJ animal character (rabbit in headphones — idle, dance-level-1, dance-level-2, celebrate)
balloon sprites in 5 colors (with picture slots)
picture icon set: 20 objects covering all initial consonants

games.title: Word Switcher Workshop
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Professor Glitch the robot inventor has a wonderful Word Switcher machine. Drop a picture card in, crank the handle, and the machine changes ONE sound to make a brand new word — the output chute delivers the new picture with a 'ding!' and steam-puff. Sometimes the machine makes funny nonsense words and shrugs adorably.
games.mechanic: A picture card (cat) goes into the funnel. A sound-chip panel shows the word's phonemes. The child selects which sound chip to swap (initial, medial, or final) and chooses the replacement from 3 options. Cranking the handle runs the machine — correct substitution produces the new word's picture from the chute. Wrong input: steam puffs and the machine shrugs (no penalty).
games.freeSample: Free: 3 transformations (cat→bat, hat→hot, bit→sit — initial sound swap only). Paid: 18 transformations spanning initial, medial, and final sound swaps with all word families, plus a 'free inventor' mode where the child mixes any two chips to discover what word (or funny nonsense) pops out.
assetNeeds: Professor Glitch robot character (idle, thinking, cranking, celebrate, shrug)
Word Switcher machine sprite (funnel, gear-spin, chute, steam-puff states)
sound-chip tile sprites (letters in chip shape)
picture card sprites (12 CVC word sets: cat/bat/hat/mat, hot/pot/lot/dot, bit/sit/kit/hit)

games.title: Magic E Castle
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A tiny stone castle grows taller every time the child rescues a word from the 'short vowel dungeon' by adding the magic e to transform it. The castle gains a new tower, flag, or glowing window with each correct transform — tap any tower to hear its word spoken in a royal proclamation voice.
games.mechanic: A CVC word appears on a stone block at the dungeon gate (cap, pin, hop, cub). A big glowing 'e' floats nearby. The child drags the e to the end of the word — the block cracks open, the word transforms (cape, pine, hope, cube), and a new castle piece rises onto the structure. A crown-wearing mouse validates each transform with a 'hear the difference!' button.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 transforms (cap→cape, pin→pine, hop→hope, cub→cube) building the first castle tower. Paid: 20 CVCe transforms across all 5 vowels, complete castle with 5 towers, plus a 'sort the words' bonus round where new words rain down and child sorts them into short-vowel vs magic-e bins.
assetNeeds: Castle build stages (10 progressive sprites: foundation, walls, 5 towers, flags, windows, moat)
crown-wearing mouse character (idle, validate, celebrate, point)

games.title: Sound-Alike Suspects
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Detective Dot has a lineup of word-picture cards that LOOK almost the same but sound different (bit vs bet, cap vs cup). The child sorts them into case files — each solved case snaps shut with a satisfying click and Detective Dot stamps it 'SOLVED' with a magnifying-glass flourish.
games.mechanic: Two bins appear labeled with two similar words (or highlighted vowels). Picture-and-word cards drift in one at a time. Child drags each card to the correct bin. A gentle 'boing' and a question-mark bounce return a wrong sort; correct sorts snap in with a click. After 6 correct sorts, Dot stamps 'CASE CLOSED' and the next pair of similar words opens.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 cases (bit vs bet × 3 cards each). Paid: 10 cases covering all short vowel minimal pairs, 4 cases with initial-consonant minimal pairs, plus a 'build your own case' mode where the child picks two similar cards and describes what's different.
assetNeeds: Detective Dot character (dog with magnifying glass — idle, inspecting, stamp, celebrate)
case-file bin sprites (two per round, labeling changes)
picture-word card set: 40 cards across 10 minimal-pair families

games.title: Sight Word Safari
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Each sight word lives in a special habitat in a Safari album. When a child reads the sight word on a card and taps the matching animal home, a safari animal sticker peels off its backing with a satisfying 'shhhwick' and settles into its silhouette. Tap any sticker to hear the animal whisper the word in a silly voice.
games.mechanic: An album page shows 6 silhouette frames. A sight word card appears with the word displayed (the/and/is/to/a/go/see/we). Four habitat tiles appear; child taps the tile whose label word matches the card. Correct match: a cartoon animal sticker animates into the silhouette frame with a peel-and-settle effect. Wrong: gentle shimmer and a 'not quite' bubble. Fill the page to unlock a new album chapter.
games.freeSample: Free: first album page (6 stickers: the, and, is, to, a, go). Paid: 5 album chapters × 6 pages = 30 Dolch Kindergarten sight words, plus a 'read it fast' replayable flashback mode where placed stickers zoom past and child taps the one called.
assetNeeds: 30 cartoon animal sticker sprites (one per sight word — e.g., a=armadillo, the=tiger, and=ant, is=iguana)

games.title: Story Soup Kitchen
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Chef Pip the porcupine is cooking 'Story Soup' and needs ingredients that answer questions about a mini story. The child listens to a 3-panel illustrated story, then drags answer-ingredients (characters, settings, events) into the bubbling pot. Each correct ingredient causes a delicious puff of steam and a happy taste-test.
games.mechanic: A 3-panel micro-story plays (tap panels left to right, narrated audio on each). Then the pot appears with a prompt: 'Who is in the story?' or 'Where does it happen?' or 'What happens first/next/last?' Three picture-ingredient cards appear; child drags the correct one to the pot. Correct: puff + Pip tastes and grins. Wrong: card bobs back. After 3 correct the soup is complete and Pip serves a bowl to the story characters.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 story (3 panels, 3 questions — who, where, what happens). Paid: 6 distinct stories covering characters, settings, and 3 sequential events each, plus a 'missing ingredient' mode where the soup is partially made and child must identify what's missing.
assetNeeds: Chef Pip porcupine character (idle, taste, happy, serve)
bubbling soup pot prop with steam states
6 micro-story panel sets (illustrated scenes, 3 panels each)
ingredient card sprites (character tokens, setting tiles, event picture cards)

games.title: Retell Theater
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A tiny puppet theater opens and a friendly beaver stage manager appears. The child retells a familiar story by dragging scene panels into sequence — when all three panels are right the curtain rises, puppets perform the scene, and the beaver cheers. The theater audience of stuffed animals reacts with squeaky gasps and claps.
games.mechanic: Three shuffled scene panels for a known story type (lost duckling finds its way home; frog wants to be a chef) appear. Child drags them into the numbered slots on the stage floor (beginning/middle/end). Correct sequence: curtain rises, puppets act out each scene with a line of auto-dialogue. Wrong order: the beaver gently shakes his head and the panels shuffle back. A 'hear the story' button replays narration at any time.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 story retell (duckling story, 3 panels). Paid: 5 story retell sets plus a 'make your own ending' mode where the beginning and middle are set but the child chooses from 3 possible endings and sees it acted out.
assetNeeds: Beaver stage manager character (idle, direct, cheer, head-shake)
puppet theater stage background (curtain open/closed states)
3-4 puppet character sprites (duck, frog, bear, rabbit — wave/bow/emote states)

games.title: Character Costume Clues
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Each blank paper-doll character comes with clues from a mini story ('She was cold and wore red'). The child dresses the character using only the clues — place the red scarf, the boots, the mittens. When all clues are matched the character winks and waves in a little fashion parade.
games.mechanic: A paper-doll outline appears on the dressing canvas. A short narrated story plays (2-3 sentences about what the character did, felt, or wore). A tray of clothing/prop items appears; child drags items that match the story details to the correct placement spots. Items from the story fit; irrelevant items gently float back. When all story-clue items are placed the character does a spin-reveal.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 characters (cold girl in red, happy baker). Paid: 8 story-character dressing sets covering different character traits, emotions, and settings, plus a 'design your own story character' bonus.
assetNeeds: 6 blank paper-doll character outlines (child boy/girl, animal, older adult, fantastical)
80+ clothing/prop item sprites (hats, scarves, shoes, tools, accessories — story-prop variety)
dressing canvas with placement zone glow

games.title: Story vs Poem Sorting House
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two cozy houses sit on a hill: the Story House (shaped like an open book) and the Poem House (shaped like a scroll with musical notes). Tiny text-excerpt cards parachute down from a blimp. The child sorts them into the right house — each correct card causes the house to light up a window and a little resident to wave.
games.mechanic: Excerpt cards fall (short ones): some are prose story excerpts (narrative sentences), some are rhyming or line-broken poem stanzas. Child drags each to Story House or Poem House. Correct: a window lights up and a character waves. Wrong: card bounces back with a gentle 'hmm'. After 8 correct sorts both houses are fully lit and the residents throw a block party.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 cards (2 obvious stories, 2 obvious rhyming poems). Paid: 20 cards with increasing nuance — including free verse, song lyrics, and beginning-of-chapter excerpts — plus a 'write your own' blank card where child picks story or poem and types (or dictates) one line.
assetNeeds: Story House prop (book-shaped, with 5 window stages)
Poem House prop (scroll-shaped with musical-note decoration, 5 window stages)
4 resident character sprites (bear in Story House, owl in Poem House — idle, wave, party-dance)

games.title: Author vs Illustrator Awards Show
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: At the Golden Pencil Awards, two hosts wait on stage: Aurelia the Author (holds a quill) and Ivan the Illustrator (holds a paintbrush). Trophy envelopes arrive by courier penguin. The child drags each envelope to the right host — Aurelia gets 'wrote the words' credits, Ivan gets 'drew the pictures' credits. Each correct delivery gets a beaming acceptance speech.
games.mechanic: A penguin courier delivers an envelope with a clue card ('made all the pictures look beautiful' / 'wrote the story about the lost kitten'). Child drags the envelope to Aurelia or Ivan. Correct: the host opens it with delight, a trophy pops out, and they give a one-line silly acceptance speech. Wrong: the penguin retrieves the envelope and does a confused shuffle. After 6 correct the awards show ends with a confetti drop.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 envelopes (2 author clues, 2 illustrator clues). Paid: 16 envelopes covering author, illustrator, AND a co-author twist, plus a 'book cover creator' where child chooses which role they want to play and adds one element.
assetNeeds: Aurelia the Author character (quill, glasses, excited, speech-giving)
Ivan the Illustrator character (beret, paintbrush, excited, speech-giving)

games.title: Picture Clue Detective Agency
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Detective Doodle is studying a big illustrated scene from a story. The narrated text plays, then clue arrows appear and the child taps elements in the picture that 'the text is talking about.' Every correct tap adds a sticky note to Doodle's case board, which fills into a solved mosaic.
games.mechanic: A richly illustrated scene is displayed. A sentence or two of text plays as audio (e.g., 'The bear was very hungry and looked for honey'). Then 'What does the picture show us about this?' Question cards pop up. Child taps the relevant picture element (the bear's empty belly look, the beehive in the tree). Correct tap: sticky note placed on the case board. After 4 taps the case board reveals a summary doodle.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 scene (hungry bear, 3 taps). Paid: 6 illustrated scenes across fiction and nonfiction contexts, covering how pictures extend or clarify text meaning, plus an 'add to the picture' mode where child drags a missing element onto the scene to match the text.
assetNeeds: Detective Doodle character (small owl with magnifying glass — idle, tap, note-writing, celebrate)
6 richly illustrated story scenes (bear/forest, frog/pond, market, space, under-the-sea, farm)

games.title: Nonfiction News Flash
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A newspaper front page is hidden behind 9 fuzzy 'censor blobs.' The child answers questions about a short read-aloud nonfiction passage — each correct answer peels back one blob to reveal part of the headline photo underneath. When the full picture is revealed, it's always something surprising and delightful (a penguin driving a bus, a dog who paints).
games.mechanic: Narrated nonfiction micro-text plays (3-4 sentences about an animal or object). Then 9 question cards appear one at a time, each with a short question and 2-3 picture choices. Correct answer = one blob removed from the 3×3 grid. Wrong = gentle shimmer; try again. When all 9 blobs clear, the reveal image triggers a celebration sound and the child can 'share' the news flash.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 passage + 4 blobs (penguin topic). Paid: 6 nonfiction passages (penguins, volcanoes, bees, trains, rainforest, ocean) each with a 9-blob reveal and distinct surprise image.
assetNeeds: 9-square censor blob overlay sprites (peel-away animation per blob)
6 surprise reveal illustrations (each with a warm absurdist twist)

games.title: Connection Web Spinner
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A spider named Webster spins a web between two columns: one for causes/individuals/events and one for effects/connections/ideas. The child draws a silk thread from a card on the left to its partner on the right — correct connections cause the web to glitter and Webster does a happy spin. The finished web becomes a shimmery work of art.
games.mechanic: Two columns of 4-5 cards each appear (cause icons and effect icons, or event icons and consequence icons from a nonfiction passage). Child taps left card then right card to draw a silk thread. Correct: thread glitters and stays; Webster dances. Wrong: thread dissolves with a sparkle and the cards flip back. After all pairs are connected Webster rappels across the finished web for a finale.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 topic (rain→plants grow), 3 pairs. Paid: 6 topics across nonfiction domains (weather, animals, community helpers, seasons, cooking, building), each with 4-5 connection pairs.
assetNeeds: Webster the spider character (idle, spin, rappel, dance)
cause/effect icon card sprites (30 pairs covering 6 topics)

games.title: Word Detective's Field Guide
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A field guide album has blank pages for 'mystery words.' When the child encounters a bold vocabulary word in a nonfiction passage and figures out its meaning from picture clues, a holographic sticker of the word's concept materializes and fills its page. Tap a collected sticker to see a tiny 3-frame cartoon definition.
games.mechanic: A short nonfiction sentence with a bold word plays (e.g., 'The caterpillar made a cocoon, a special case around itself.'). A picture-context clue glows in the scene. The child taps from 3 meaning choices. Correct: a holographic sticker pops into the field guide with a satisfying magnetic snap. Wrong: shimmer and try again. After 6 stickers the chapter is complete with a 'my word collection' gallery.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 vocabulary stickers from a nature chapter (cocoon, hatch, nectar, migrate). Paid: 4 chapters × 8 words = 32 academic vocabulary stickers with the full field guide filled, plus a 'use it in a sentence' tap-chain where child hears the word used 3 ways.
assetNeeds: Field guide album prop (nature journal look)
32 holographic sticker sprites (one per vocabulary concept — vivid, memorable illustrations)
chapter divider page sprites (4 themed: forest, ocean, city, sky)

games.title: Front-to-Back Book Explorer
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A tiny explorer mouse traverses a giant pop-up book, hopping from section to section: cover → title page → table of contents → chapters → glossary → back cover. Each hop requires the child to answer a question about that section's purpose. The mouse wears a tiny explorer hat that gains a new badge at each stop.
games.mechanic: The mouse stands at a section of the book (e.g., the table of contents). A question prompt appears: 'What can you find here?' with 3 picture-answer tiles. Child taps correct answer → mouse hops to the next section with a little explorer animation and earns a badge. Wrong: gentle boing and the question reshuffles. After all 6 sections the mouse reaches the back cover and does a victory pose.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 sections (front cover, title page, table of contents). Paid: all 6 nonfiction book sections, plus a 'build your own book' mode where child arranges the parts in correct order to construct a mini nonfiction book cover-to-cover.
assetNeeds: Explorer mouse character (idle, hop, badge-receive, celebrate, thinking)
pop-up book background (6 section spreads: cover, title page, TOC, chapter, glossary, back cover)
6 explorer badge sprites (cover badge, title badge, TOC badge, chapter badge, glossary badge, back-cover badge)

games.title: Two Books, One Topic
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two book characters (Book Benny and Book Bella) each contain information about the same topic (e.g., frogs) but focus on different details. Fact cards float down and the child sorts each card into the correct book — Benny's or Bella's. Both books then have a 'same AND different' page that the child builds by discovering a card that belongs to BOTH.
games.mechanic: Two book-shaped bins appear, each with a title and a cover illustration. 8 fact-picture cards float in one at a time (some unique to each book, one 'both' card). Child drags each to the correct book. Unique cards: book bounces happily. Both-card: a bridge between the two books appears and the card slides to the center. Wrong: gentle bounce back. Final reveal: a Venn diagram fills in showing the overlap.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 topic pair (two frog books), 5 cards. Paid: 5 topic pairs (frogs, bears, the ocean, rain, community helpers) with full Venn diagram reveal, plus a 'write one same and one different' dictation mode.
assetNeeds: Book Benny and Book Bella character props (animated book sprites with faces, bounce states)
Venn diagram prop (center reveals as 'bridge' fills)
fact-picture card sprites (40 cards across 5 topic pairs)

games.title: Alphabet Avenue
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A sunny avenue needs 26 houses, each belonging to a letter of the alphabet. The child places each letter-house by matching it to the right spot on the street — uppercase and lowercase houses must park next to each other. Once placed, a little letter-character pops out waving from the window.
games.mechanic: A long avenue diorama has 26 numbered lots. A house card appears showing a letter (upper or lowercase). 3 lot-position choices light up on the avenue. Child taps the correct spot. Correct: the house snaps in with a 'click' and a character waves. Wrong: house floats back. After 8 correct placements the section of avenue comes alive with traffic and music. Full 26-letter avenue unlocks a 'stroll mode' where tapping any house plays the letter's name and sound.
games.freeSample: Free: first 8 letters (A-H section of avenue). Paid: full 26-letter avenue plus a 'letter hunt' mode where the child finds hidden letters on the completed avenue scene.
assetNeeds: 26 letter-house sprites (each stylized for its letter — A has an arched door, B has a bumpy roof, etc.)
26 letter-character sprites (one per letter, waving from window)
stroll-mode walking animation for a guide dog character

games.title: Noun & Verb Café
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The café has two menus: the THING menu (nouns — foods, objects) and the ACTION menu (verbs — jump, eat, sleep). Word-picture cards keep arriving on a conveyor belt. The café owner, a very organized hedgehog, needs the child to sort them to the right menu bin before the belt runs out. Correct sorts fill the menu; the hedgehog does a little grateful bow.
games.mechanic: Words with matching pictures arrive on a conveyor belt (dog, run, apple, sleep, hat, jump). Two bins labeled THING (noun icon: picture frame) and ACTION (verb icon: running shoe) sit at the ends. Child drags each card to the right bin. Correct: bin lights up, hedgehog bows. Wrong: belt redelivers the card. After 12 correct the café opens and little character-customers arrive to order.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 cards (3 nouns, 3 verbs — obvious examples). Paid: 30 cards including nuanced cases (can 'play' be both?), adjective interludes, plus a 'make a sentence' bonus where child combines a noun and verb card to form a simple sentence.
assetNeeds: Hedgehog café owner character (idle, bow, confused, celebrate)
THING menu bin and ACTION menu bin sprites

games.title: Plural Power Plant
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The Plural Power Plant takes in ONE thing and manufactures MANY. Drop a single picture card into the input hopper, crank the 'pluralizer,' and the output conveyor delivers a pile of them. A little counter flips from 1 to many, and the machine makes a fun cha-chung mechanical sound. The wrong plural attempt causes the machine to produce a hilariously wrong number of objects and shrug.
games.mechanic: A picture card (one cat) enters the funnel. Below the funnel, three plural word choices appear (cats / cates / cat). Child taps the correct plural → machine runs → output delivers several cats with a gleeful pile-up animation. Wrong: machine sputters and delivers a funny wrong result (0 cats, or one giant cat). After 8 correct plurals the plant earns an 'efficiency award.'
games.freeSample: Free: 4 cards (regular -s plurals: cat/cats, dog/dogs, hat/hats, cup/cups). Paid: 20 cards including -es (box/boxes, dish/dishes), irregular (mouse/mice, child/children, foot/feet), plus a 'spot the wrong plural' mode where the machine has already made a mistake.
assetNeeds: Plural Power Plant machine sprite (hopper, conveyor, counter-flip states)
plant foreman robot character (idle, crank, celebrate, shrug)
30 picture card sprites (single and pile-of-many version of each)

games.title: Question Word Quest
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Six question-word monsters (Who, What, Where, When, Why, How) each have very specific appetites — the WHO monster only eats person-cards, the WHERE monster only eats place-cards. A question sentence plays and the child feeds the correct monster the right answer-picture. Happy chomps and incorrect polite spitting-back make it silly and clear.
games.mechanic: A question sentence plays: 'Where is the cat hiding?' Six monster-mouth buttons appear (one per question word). Child taps the monster whose question word matches the sentence's question word, then feeds it the correct answer picture from 3 choices. Correct: monster chomps and does a satisfied rub of its tummy. Wrong: monster spits back gently and shakes. After 6 correct the monsters do a question-word chorus.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 question words in play (Who/What/Where), 4 sentences. Paid: all 6 question words with 18 sentences, plus a 'build a question' mode where child drags a question word to start a sentence and completes it with picture choices.
assetNeeds: 6 distinct question-word monster characters (stylized for each word: Who=wide eyes, Where=compass, When=clock, What=question-mark, Why=thinking cloud, How=gear)
answer picture card sprites (30 cards across person/place/time/reason/method categories)

games.title: Preposition Playground
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cheerful frog needs to be placed exactly right in a playground scene — on the slide, under the bench, beside the tree, in the sandbox. The child reads the preposition prompt, then drags the frog to the correct position. Frog bounces into place with a 'boing!' and croaks a happy note. The scene fills with correctly-placed frogs.
games.mechanic: A playground scene is displayed. A prompt plays: 'Put the frog IN the sandbox.' The child drags the frog-sprite to one of 4 glowing placement zones. Correct zone: the frog settles with a bounce and the preposition word glows on screen. Wrong zone: frog slides back with a gentle wobble. After 8 correct placements the scene is full of frogs in funny positions and a celebration song plays.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 positions (in, on, under, beside). Paid: 14 prepositions across 3 scenes (playground, kitchen, barnyard) including between, behind, above, below, in front of, next to, plus a 'describe it' mode where the child taps a frog and picks the correct preposition label.
assetNeeds: Frog character sprite (idle, bounce, settle, celebrate)
3 scene backgrounds with glowing placement zones (playground, kitchen, barnyard)

games.title: Sentence Builder Bridge
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A gap in a bridge must be filled with sentence planks. The child picks a subject plank, an action plank, and an object plank, then snaps them together — if they form a grammatical sentence the bridge plank glows and a train crosses it with a toot. If the combination is silly but grammatical, the train goes anyway but wearing a party hat.
games.mechanic: Three plank trays appear: WHO (the dog, the girl, a robot), DOES WHAT (runs, eats, flies), and WHAT/WHERE (the cake, over the moon, to school). Child drags one plank from each tray to the bridge gap. If the resulting sentence is grammatical and complete, the bridge plank glows and a train crosses. If incomplete (only 2 planks), the gap wobbles. After 5 bridge sections the train arrives at a celebration station.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 plank sets, builds 2 sections. Paid: 10 plank sets building the full bridge, plus a 'silly sentence mode' where all planks are available and child builds the funniest grammatical sentence possible with a reaction from onlookers.
assetNeeds: Bridge section sprites (plank segments, gap states, glow state)
cartoon train character (idle, approach, cross, toot, party-hat variant)
WHO/DOES WHAT/WHERE plank tile sprites (30 planks total)

games.title: Capital Cop
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Officer Capital is patrolling sentences displayed on big city billboards and needs the child to spot every word that should be capitalized. Tapping a word that needs a capital letter turns it into a shiny uppercase letter with a police badge sparkle. Tapping a word that doesn't need a capital makes Officer Capital shrug with a smile.
games.mechanic: A billboard shows a 4-8 word sentence with some capitalization errors. Officer Capital's cruiser is parked below. Child taps each word that needs to start with a capital (first word + proper nouns + the word 'I'). Correct taps: letter transforms to uppercase with a badge. Wrong taps (lowercase word that's fine as-is): Officer shrugs — no penalty. After all errors are found, Officer stamps 'APPROVED' and the billboard glows.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 billboards (first-word-of-sentence capitalization only). Paid: 12 billboards progressing through proper nouns, the word 'I', and mixed errors, plus a 'write it right' mode where child types a corrected version of a short sentence.
assetNeeds: Officer Capital character (cartoon police officer with badge — idle, drive, shrug, stamp, approve)

games.title: Punctuation Parade Caboose
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A sentence train travels down a track but its caboose is missing the punctuation sign. The child taps the correct punctuation car (period, question mark, exclamation point) to hook it onto the caboose. The train then chugs forward, the whistle matching the punctuation's 'tone' — period=steady toot, question mark=rising toot, exclamation=big BLAST.
games.mechanic: A sentence appears on the train body. Three punctuation caboose cars wait on a siding. Child taps the correct one. Correct: it hooks on with a satisfying click, the matching whistle sound plays, and the train chugs to the next station. Wrong: caboose bounces off the coupling and swings back. After 8 trains the line arrives at a Grand Station celebration.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 trains (period and question mark only). Paid: 20 trains covering all three punctuation marks including tricky statements that end with either (She won! vs She won.), plus a 'write the sentence' mode where child completes a sentence frame and chooses the right ending.
assetNeeds: Sentence train body sprites (different sentence content per car)
3 punctuation caboose car sprites (period/question-mark/exclamation, each with color-coded design)
coupling click + whistle sound animation sprites

games.title: Sound Spelling Sandbox
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A magic sandbox glows when a phonetic sound plays. The child traces the letter that makes that sound with a glowing wand — the sand takes the shape of the letter and a little crab emerges from the sand, reads the letter, and gives a thumbs-up. Wrong strokes get smoothed away by a tiny wave.
games.mechanic: An audio cue plays a phoneme sound (/s/, /a/, /t/, etc.) and shows a picture clue. The child traces the letter on a dotted sand outline with a drag gesture. The tracing wand leaves a glowing trail; completed traces that match the outline turn gold. A crab character confirms with the letter name. After 6 correct traces the crab builds a sandcastle spelling a whole CVC word.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 consonant sounds (s, m, t, a, p). Paid: all 26 letter-sound-to-letter-writing links, plus a 'write the word' mode where 3 sounds play in sequence and child traces all 3 letters to spell a phonetic CVC word.
assetNeeds: Crab character (idle, thumbs-up, thumbs-down gently, builds-sandcastle)

games.title: Category Caravan
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A caravan of colorful wagons is heading to the annual Category Fair — each wagon is labeled for a category (animals, foods, clothes, furniture). Objects rain down from the sky (leftover from a big wind!) and the child must sort each one into the right wagon before the caravan departs. Each correct sort makes a wagon-animal pull happily on its rope.
games.mechanic: 4 category wagons sit on a road, each labeled with a picture-and-word category sign. Objects fall from the top of the screen one by one (picture + word). Child drags to the correct wagon. Correct: wagon bounces, the animal pulling it does a happy hop. Wrong: object bounces back with a 'where do I belong?' jingle. After 16 correct sorts the caravan departs with a festive parade.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 wagons (animals vs foods), 8 items. Paid: 5 rounds with rotating wagon sets (animals/foods/clothes/furniture/vehicles, tools/colors/shapes/toys/weather) × 16 items each, plus a 'name one more' bonus where child taps a wagon and adds a new item from memory.
assetNeeds: 5 wagon styles (animal-themed: horse-pulled, elephant, dog, cat, bird)
object-item picture sprites (80 items across 10 categories)

games.title: Action Word Circus
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The circus ringmaster needs action-word performers sorted by HOW they do things. The 'fast performers' bin is for words like sprint/dash/zoom; the 'slow performers' bin is for words like creep/shuffle/tiptoe. Drop the verb-card performer into the right bin — the right bin opens its curtain and the performer does a demonstration in the ring.
games.mechanic: A verb card appears (sprint, shuffle, stomp, whisper, shout, tiptoe). Two curtained bins are labeled (fast/slow, loud/quiet, big/small movement). Child drags the card to the matching bin. Correct: curtain parts and a tiny animal performs the action with an exaggerated animation. Wrong: card is spat back with a gentle boing. After 8 correct the ringmaster takes a bow. Next round changes the contrast pair.
games.freeSample: Free: fast vs slow (sprint, tiptoe, zoom, creep — 4 cards). Paid: 5 contrast pairs × 8 cards = 40 verb-shade sorts, plus a 'pick the better word' mode where two similar verbs appear and child drags the one that better describes a shown scene.
assetNeeds: Ringmaster character (tiger in top hat — idle, introduce, bow, celebrate)
10 performing animal sprites (one per verb shade — cheetah for sprint, snail for tiptoe, mouse for whisper, lion for roar, etc.)

games.title: Same Word, New Meaning
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A magic word coin has two sides. The child hears a word used two different ways (bat = the animal, bat = the sports equipment) and taps the coin to flip it — one side reveals the animal meaning, the other reveals the object meaning. As meanings are discovered, a 'word coin collection' display fills up, each coin spinning when tapped.
games.mechanic: A word appears in two sentences (audio): 'The bat flew over the house' and 'She hit the ball with the bat.' A coin sprite sits between two picture choices. Child taps the coin and drags it to the meaning that matches each sentence. Correct: coin face reveals the picture and snaps into the collection display. Both meanings collected: coin spins in the collection. 6 word coins = chapter complete.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 coins (bat, bark). Paid: 15 multiple-meaning coins for common K words (bat, bark, right, light, rock, duck, fly, cold, ring, watch, pen, pitcher, safe, run, bill), plus a 'use it in a sentence' tapping game where child picks which sentence uses the word correctly.
assetNeeds: Coin sprite (flip animation, two distinct face designs per word)

games.title: Real Word / Silly Word Bakery
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The bakery makes two kinds of treats: REAL word loaves (go in the Real Bread basket) and SILLY nonsense word muffins (go in the Silly Muffin tin). The baker, a cheerful raccoon, needs help sorting! Real words get a happy 'ding,' silly words get a laugh and a 'bloop.' Every 8 correct fills an order and a new customer waddles in to collect their bread.
games.mechanic: A word appears on a baked-goods card (sat / dit / mop / fep / big / wub). Child drags to the Real Bread basket or Silly Muffin tin. Real word → basket lights up, raccoon dings the bell. Nonsense → tin lid pops with a bloop and raccoon giggles. Wrong sort: item bounces back. After 8 sorts a customer collects the order with delight. Next round introduces new CVC patterns.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 cards (3 real, 3 nonsense — all CVC with obvious patterns). Paid: 40 cards progressing from CVC to CCVC to CVCe patterns, plus a 'bake the word' bonus where child sounds out a nonsense word aloud (self-assessed, tap 'I said it' to advance).
assetNeeds: Raccoon baker character (idle, ring-bell, giggle, proud)
40 baked-goods word card sprites (bread loaf for real, muffin for silly)
customer animal sprites (5 customers — each with a basket)

games.title: Rhyme Time Garden
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Every rhyming pair makes a flower grow in the Rhyme Garden. The child taps a seed labeled with a word, then picks its rhyming partner from 3 flying butterfly cards — match the rhyme and the seed cracks open, a stem shoots up, and a gorgeous flower blooms in a satisfying whoosh. Tap the flower to hear both rhyming words sung in a tiny ditty.
games.mechanic: A garden plot has 6 soil patches. A seed with a word label appears. 3 butterfly cards float nearby with picture-words. Child taps the butterfly whose word rhymes. Correct: seed blooms through 3 growth stages (sprout→stem→flower) with a satisfying animation. Wrong: butterfly floats away and returns. After all 6 patches bloom, a bee flies across the completed garden for a pollination celebration.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 flowers (cat/hat, log/frog, king/ring). Paid: 6 garden plots × 5 rounds = 30 rhyme pairs across 5 complete garden scenes, plus a 'rhyme chain' bonus where one flower grows per link in a chain of 5 rhyming words.
assetNeeds: flower bloom animation (4 stages: seed → sprout → stem → flower per patch)

games.title: Syllable Snap Bakery
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The Syllable Slicer machine takes a long word and snaps it into syllable pieces like a bread-slicing machine. The child predicts how many slices come out BEFORE the machine runs — guess right and the slices fly out perfectly; guess wrong and the machine over-slices or under-slices with a slapstick result.
games.mechanic: A picture card appears (banana). A prediction panel shows buttons 1, 2, 3, 4. Child taps their syllable-count guess. Then the crank is pulled — the machine slices the word into pieces (one per syllable), each piece landing in a tray. If the prediction matches, golden confetti. If wrong, the machine produces the wrong number of slices comedically. Child can then tap each syllable piece to hear it spoken.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 words (cat=1, robot=2, banana=3, caterpillar=4). Paid: 25 words spanning 1-4 syllables, plus a 'put the slices back' bonus mode where 3 syllable pieces must be dragged into order to rebuild the word.
assetNeeds: Syllable Slicer machine sprite (conveyor, blade, tray, slapstick-overslice state)
machine operator character (penguin chef — idle, crank, celebrate, slapstick)
syllable-slice tile sprites (1-4 pieces per word)

games.title: I Know That Sight Word
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An underwater scene hides beneath 12 sand tiles. Each sand tile hides a sea creature. A sight word flashes — the child finds it on floating bubbles and taps it, which blows away a sand tile to reveal what's underneath. Get all 12 and a friendly whale swims through to complete the scene.
games.mechanic: 12 sand tiles cover a 3×4 grid underwater scene. A target sight word appears in a bubble. 4 bubble choices drift across the screen. Child taps the one with the matching sight word. Correct: a sand tile flips to reveal part of the hidden scene (a fish, a treasure chest, coral). Wrong: bubble pops and new ones appear. After 12 correct the full scene is revealed and the whale appears.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 tiles (sight words: the, and, is, to, a, go). Paid: 5 scenes × 12 tiles = 60 sight word recognitions, covering the full Dolch Kindergarten list (52 words), plus a 'flash and find' replayable mode.
assetNeeds: 5 underwater hidden-scene illustrations (ocean, shipwreck, coral reef, mermaid palace, submarine bay — each 3×4 composited)
12-tile sand overlay grid sprites (flip-away animation per tile)
sea creature reveal sprites (12 different creatures)

games.title: Print Walk
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A curious puppy named Page is taking a walk through the neighborhood and keeps seeing words, signs, and books everywhere. At each stop a print-concept question pops up about a displayed text (which way do you read? where does the second word start?). Answer right and Page wags her tail and bounds to the next stop.
games.mechanic: Page stops at a scene (billboard, book page, menu, cereal box). A print-concept question appears with a pointer arrow prompt: 'Tap where reading starts' / 'Tap the space between two words' / 'Tap the first letter of the second word.' Child taps the correct element in the displayed text. Correct: Page wags and hops to the next stop. Wrong: Page tilts her head and a gentle arrow hint shimmers. 8 stops complete the neighborhood walk.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 stops (book page — where to start, billboard — left-to-right direction, two words — find the space). Paid: all 8 stops across 4 environments covering all RF.K.1 sub-skills, plus a 'design your own sign' crafting mode.
assetNeeds: Puppy Page character (idle, walk, wag-tail, head-tilt, leap)
4 environment background scenes (neighborhood, park, grocery store, library)
text display panels (book page, billboard, menu, cereal box prop overlays)

games.title: Compound Word Kitchen
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Chef Flopsy the bunny is inventing compound word sandwiches: smash two word-halves together and a silly character that IS that compound word assembles itself on the plate. Sunflower = a sun wearing a flower hat. Footprint = a foot with a printed stamp. Each assembled compound gives a little bow.
games.mechanic: A word-builder canvas shows a sandwich assembly area. Word-half tiles appear in two columns (sun/flower, rain/coat, foot/print, cup/cake). Child drags one left-half and one right-half tile to the sandwich spots. When they combine to make a real compound word, a character avatar of that compound assembles with a flash. Wrong combo: tiles slide back. 6 successful sandwiches complete the lunch rush.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 sandwiches (sunflower, raincoat, cupcake). Paid: 20 compound word sandwiches, plus a 'what would THIS compound mean?' absurdist mode where the child makes nonsense compounds and the game produces funny hybrid character art.
assetNeeds: Chef Flopsy bunny character (idle, assemble-action, proud, surprised)
20 compound-word character avatar sprites (sunflower character, raincoat character, cupcake character, etc. — each a charming hybrid)
word-half tile sprites (left/right halves, 40 tiles total)

games.title: Shades of Meaning Paint Studio
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An art studio wall has a gradient paint strip: 'a little' on one end, 'a LOT' on the other. Word-paint tubes (whisper/talk/shout; walk/jog/sprint; warm/hot/boiling) arrive by conveyor. The child squeezes each word-tube onto the correct position on the gradient strip — the strip floods with the word's color intensity and the painted word character acts out the meaning.
games.mechanic: A gradient strip runs across the canvas (pale left end, rich right end). 3 verb or adjective paint tubes arrive for the same concept (e.g., warm / hot / boiling). Child drags each tube to the correct position on the strip (left = mildest, right = strongest). When all 3 are placed in correct order the strip fills with a gradient and a character demonstrates each intensity with an escalating animation. Wrong order: tubes slide to corrected spots gently.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 set of 3 (warm/hot/boiling with a pot character reacting). Paid: 8 meaning-gradient sets (temperature, sound volume, size, speed, happiness, sadness, hunger, brightness — 24 words total), plus a 'pick the right one' scene where child selects the best-intensity word for a given situation.
assetNeeds: Art studio background with gradient strip canvas
paint tube sprites (one per word, color-coded by intensity)
character reaction sprites for each gradient set (pot for temperature, face for sound, person for speed/size, sun for brightness)

games.title: Real-Life Word Web
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cozy spider named Spin builds a word web by connecting words to the real-life things they describe. The child taps a word card, then taps its matching real-life picture — Spin zips across the web to connect them with a shimmering thread. When all pairs are connected the web glitters and Spin does a victory dance in the center.
games.mechanic: 8 word cards appear in the left column, 8 picture cards in the right (not aligned). Child taps a word → it highlights; then taps the matching picture. Correct: Spin draws a glowing web thread between them. Wrong: Spin wiggles and the selection resets. All 8 pairs connected: web sparkles and Spin dances. The words are concrete nouns, action verbs, and descriptive adjectives used in real-life contexts.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 pairs (cozy, crunchy, dash, bloom — with nature pictures). Paid: 6 full web rounds × 8 pairs = 48 word-to-real-world connections spanning home, school, nature, community, and food categories, plus a 'tell me about it' mode where child taps a matched pair and describes a real-life experience with that word.
assetNeeds: Spin the spider character (idle, zip-across, dance, victory)

games.title: Reading Buddy Book Club
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cozy reading nook has a lamp, a pile of books, and a sleepy bear cub named Bruno. The child reads along with a 5-panel emergent reader story (simple text + rich pictures), tapping each word as narration plays. After each panel, Bruno wakes up to ask one comprehension question. Getting it right earns a cozy-nook accessory (a pillow, a mug, a star-quilt) that decorates the reading nook.
games.mechanic: Each panel shows illustrated text (3-5 words per line). Audio narration highlights each word as it's read. Child can tap any word for re-read. After each panel Bruno pops up with one question (tap the answer from 2 pictures). Correct: nook item awarded with a cozy animation. Wrong: gentle 'hmm' and Bruno replays. After 5 panels the full story plays back uninterrupted as a celebration 'movie.'
games.freeSample: Free: 1 emergent reader (5 panels, Bruno asks 3 questions, 2 nook items earned). Paid: 6 distinct emergent reader stories covering a range of topics and text levels, plus Bruno's full accessory library of 30 items to collect across all stories.
assetNeeds: Bruno bear cub character (asleep, waking, asking, delighted, pointing)
reading nook diorama (collectible accessory slots: pillows, mugs, quilts, plants, lamps, rugs)
6 × 5-panel emergent reader story boards (simple illustrated text)
nook-item drop-in accessory animation sprites (30 items)

games.title: Who Said That? Speech Bubble Match
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: After a short read-aloud, the characters' speech bubbles get all mixed up. The child matches each speech bubble (a question someone asked or statement someone made in the story) to the correct character face. Correct matches make the character pop up, say the line in their own voice, and wave. It becomes a little character roll-call.
games.mechanic: A 2-3 sentence story plays via narration with illustrated characters. Then speech bubbles appear (left column) and character portraits appear (right column). Child taps a bubble and then a character to match. Correct: the character portrait bounces and speaks the line in a character voice. Wrong: gentle ripple and reset. After all matches the characters all say their lines in order, replaying the mini-story.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 story (3 characters, 3 speech bubbles — a simple bear/rabbit/bird exchange). Paid: 5 stories × 3-4 speech bubbles each = 20 question-and-answer/dialogue matching rounds, covering different genres (realistic, fantasy, informational discussion).
assetNeeds: 5 sets of 3-4 character portrait sprites (each set = a distinct story cast)
speech bubble prop sprites (question-mark variety and statement variety)
story replay panel sprites (same as story panels from story-maker)

games.title: Describe That Thing
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The Description Museum has empty display pedestals needing labels. A mystery object is revealed on a pedestal — and the child picks the BEST describing word from a trio of adjective bubbles to place as the label card. When the right label clicks into place the pedestal lights up and museum visitors (fancy animal patrons) crowd around it admiringly.
games.mechanic: A diorama museum background has 6 empty pedestal-display slots. An object appears on the lit pedestal (a fluffy cloud, a spiky cactus, a shiny coin). Three adjective bubbles float up (fluffy/smooth/loud for the cloud). Child taps the best matching adjective. Correct: label card snaps onto pedestal, visitors gather and murmur with appreciation. Wrong: wrong bubble pops harmlessly. After 6 pedestals the museum opens to fanfare.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 pedestal reveals (fluffy cloud, spiky cactus, shiny coin). Paid: 6 museum rooms × 6 pedestals = 36 attribute-matching descriptions spanning texture, size, color, shape, temperature, and sound descriptors, plus a 'build your own exhibit' mode where child draws and labels.
assetNeeds: Museum hall background (expandable with 6 pedestal slots per room)
Museum visitor animal patron sprites (5-6 patrons who cluster and murmur)

games.title: My Book, My Voice
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The child becomes the author-illustrator of a 3-page picture book. Each page offers a scene backdrop and a word-bank of simple labels; the child drags words or pictures onto the page to 'write' their book. A recording microphone lets them tap to narrate each page in their own voice (or uses pre-set audio prompts). At the end the book is 'published' with a cover-stamp celebration.
games.mechanic: Page 1: choose a scene (forest/ocean/city); drag 2-3 object sticker labels onto it. Page 2: choose what happens (action sticker + character sticker). Page 3: choose an ending (happy/surprising/silly sticker). The child taps a microphone for narration guidance ('Tell me about your page'). When all 3 pages are filled, a 'Publish!' button stamps the cover and the book flips through page-by-page with narration playback.
games.freeSample: Free: page 1 construction only (scene + 2 labels). Paid: full 3-page book maker with 5 scene choices × 3 pages, 40 object stickers, a character chooser, a cover designer, and a 'book library' where up to 5 books are saved and can be 'read again.'
assetNeeds: 3-page book template props (page borders, page-turn animation)
5 scene backdrop sprites (forest, ocean, city, farm, space)
40 object sticker sprites (nouns for labeling: tree, fish, car, etc.)
character sticker sprites (6 characters in action poses)

games.title: Silly Sentence Fixer
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A zany robot called Typo-Bot has been writing sentences all wrong — missing capitals, wrong punctuation, incomplete sentences. The child finds each error in Typo-Bot's printed output by tapping it. Fixed errors turn bright green with a satisfying click. At the end Typo-Bot short-circuits with a dramatic sparking finish and the child's corrected version replaces it.
games.mechanic: Typo-Bot's output appears: a 3-5 word sentence with 2-3 visible errors (missing capital, missing period, wrong question mark, or sentence fragment). Child taps each error zone. Correct tap: error glows and a correction animation plays (lowercase letter flips to uppercase, period appears). Tapping non-errors: Typo-Bot beeps peacefully ('that's fine!'). After all errors found, Typo-Bot sparks and the corrected sentence displays.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 sentences (first-word cap + period errors only). Paid: 15 sentences with escalating error types, plus a 'write it correctly' mode where child types a corrected version of the broken sentence.
assetNeeds: Typo-Bot robot character (idle, print-output, short-circuit, beep-peacefully)
correction flip animations (lowercase→uppercase, period materializes, question mark swaps)

games.title: Alphabet Letter Detectives
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A wild jungle scene is hidden inside an overgrown 'alphabet greenhouse.' The child is given a letter badge and must find EVERY hidden instance of that letter in the scene — some are uppercase, some are lowercase, some are sneakily embedded in signs, banners, or animal spots. Each found letter makes a leaf rustle and a tiny creature say 'Found me!'
games.mechanic: A detailed illustrated scene contains 5-8 hidden instances of a target letter (uppercase and lowercase, in varied fonts/orientations). The child taps each one. Correct: leaf rustle + creature voice + tap glow. After all found: the letter glows in the center and the scene reveals a hidden animal whose name starts with that letter. Wrong area taps: gentle shimmer, no penalty.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 letter scenes (A, B, C). Paid: all 26 letter scenes in the greenhouse, plus a 'contrast hunt' mode where the child finds letter A AND avoids letter D (visually similar letter discrimination).
assetNeeds: Alphabet greenhouse/jungle background (one lush scene with 26 layered plant/vine variants — letter instances hidden as carved/painted/printed elements)
26 hidden-letter creature reveal sprites (one per letter: armadillo for A, butterfly for B, etc.)

games.title: Vowel Village
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Vowel Village has 5 neighborhoods — one for each short vowel. Word-picture cards arrive by delivery cart and the child must direct them to the right neighborhood based on the vowel sound in the middle. Each correct delivery builds a new house in that neighborhood. When all 5 neighborhoods are complete, the village throws a vowel festival.
games.mechanic: 5 neighborhood bins sit in a village diorama (labeled with vowel letters a/e/i/o/u). A picture-word card arrives (cat → a, red → e, pig → i, fog → o, bug → u). Child drags it to the correct neighborhood. Correct: a tiny house builds in that neighborhood with a pop. Wrong: card bounces back. 20 correct deliveries complete all 5 neighborhoods and trigger the festival.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 cards (a/i/u neighborhoods only). Paid: full village with 20 cards across all 5 short vowels, a 'long vowel suburb' extension with 10 more cards (magic e words), and a replayable 'sort-it-fast' challenge mode.
assetNeeds: Village diorama background (5 neighborhood zones, each with distinct color/theme)
5 vowel neighborhood sign sprites (a=apple orchard, e=elm forest, i=igloo village, o=orange grove, u=umbrella plaza)
20 picture-word card sprites (CVC words across all 5 vowels)
house-build progressive sprites (3 stages per neighborhood)
festival finale animation (banners, fireworks, villager characters)

games.title: Storyteller's Treasure Chest
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A treasure chest opens after each story mini-lesson. Inside are vocabulary treasure cards and key-detail gems. The child answers a question about the story's words or key details to 'earn' each gem, which snaps into the chest's velvet tray with a satisfying click-and-glitter. A full tray unlocks a new story world.
games.mechanic: A 4-panel micro-story plays (narrated). Then treasure questions appear one by one: 'What does the word shiver mean in the story?' or 'What happened when the bird found the seed?' Child taps a picture answer from 3 choices. Correct: a gem slides into the chest velvet tray. Wrong: gentle 'not quite' shimmer. 6 gems fill the tray and the chest bursts open with confetti.
games.freeSample: Free: 1 story (4 panels, 3 gem questions — shiver/seed story). Paid: 6 story worlds × 6 gem questions = 36 key-detail and vocabulary comprehension items, plus a 'tell me the story' mode where gem-holders are tapped in sequence to auto-play a retell.
assetNeeds: Treasure chest prop (closed, opening, full-velvet-tray states)
6 gem sprites (ruby, emerald, sapphire, topaz, pearl, amethyst — each glittery)
6 story world unlock animations (brief reveal screen per world)

games.title: Morning Message Fix-It
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Every morning the classroom message machine prints a message — but it has hiccups and sometimes skips capitals, punctuation, or spaces between words. The child feeds each broken message through the Fix-It Roller and taps each error to fix it. The corrected message pops out the other end with a sparkle and gets posted on the classroom wall.
games.mechanic: A classroom message scroll feeds through a rolling machine. The message has 2-3 intentional errors (runwords/missingspace, nocapital, wrongpunctuation). Child taps an error zone → a selection menu appears (add space / capitalize / add period / add question mark). Correct fix: the roller stamps it and moves on. After all errors are fixed the message feeds out the clean end with a satisfied 'ding' and posts to the wall.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 messages (capitalization and period errors only). Paid: 15 messages across 3 error types, plus a 'write today's message' creative mode where the child composes and chooses their own corrections.
assetNeeds: Fix-It Roller machine sprite (feed-in, roller, output states)
error-zone tap-overlay sprites (missing-space mark, wrong-capital underline, missing-punctuation slot)

games.title: Pizza Party Problems
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A cast of hungry animal friends order pizza in a puppet-show diner; the child picks the story path (who ate how many slices, who left, how many remain) and the puppets act it out with exaggerated chomps and burps — every run is a different story.
games.mechanic: Drag character puppets onto a diner stage, tap word/number choices to fill in the add/subtract word-problem blanks, then tap the answer tile to resolve the scene; the puppet reacts with a celebratory dance or a dramatic 'still hungry!' flop.
games.freeSample: Free: the first 3 story scenarios (addition only, sums ≤10) with 2 puppets. Paid: all 20 scenarios spanning addition and subtraction within 20, 6 puppet characters, alternate endings, and a 'play it back' storybook mode.
assetNeeds: Pizza slices sprite-sheet (1-8 slices on a plate)
Diner stage backdrop with table and counter
Speech bubble with fill-in-blank text frame

games.title: Two-Team Tug
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Three quirky animals are on the same tug-of-war team and the child builds the team's total pulling power by placing each animal and watching the rope inch forward — adding three numbers feels like assembling a squad, not doing arithmetic.
games.mechanic: A side tray shows three labeled animal cards each with a strength number; drag all three to their spots on the rope; a strength meter fills after each placement; when the third lands, the opposing rock wiggles loose and flies off-screen with a comic bounce.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 rounds with totals ≤12 and a visible number bond hint. Paid: 18 rounds up to 20, hidden hints (reveal on tap), a 'mix your own team' mode where the child picks which three animals to place, and a silly 'what if a chicken joins?' bonus round.
assetNeeds: Mouse character (idle/straining/celebrating — tiny effort, big result gag)
Rope sprite with tension stages (5 frames)

games.title: Swap Shop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A charismatic raccoon shopkeeper runs a Swap Shop — she takes any addition sentence you put in and swaps the addends around to show the same sum. Kids discover commutativity through the raccoon's theatrical 'ta-da!' reveal, not through a rule.
games.mechanic: Drag a number tile into each side of a two-slot conveyor; pull the raccoon's lever; the machine whirs and spits out the swapped pair with the same sum displayed; the child confirms 'same!' or 'different!' by tapping a big yes/no badge.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 rounds with single-digit addends, sum shown immediately. Paid: 20 rounds including doubles, addends up to 10, a 'predict before the swap' mode, and a 'break the machine' challenge where the child tries to find a swap that does NOT work (it never can — the raccoon crows every time).
assetNeeds: Swap Shop machine with conveyor belt, gear wheel, and output chute
Sum display panel with equals sign
Yes/No badge pair (green checkmark / yellow question mark)

games.title: Missing Piece Bakery
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A forgetful baker keeps writing subtraction recipes with a missing ingredient number — find the missing addend and a tile flips to reveal the finished cake decoration; complete the whole cake for a bakery grand-opening wiggle.
games.mechanic: A 3×3 grid covers a cake illustration; each tile shows a subtraction sentence with one number hidden behind a question-mark frosting blob; tap the correct answer from three number tiles to flip that cover tile and expose part of the cake beneath.
games.freeSample: Free: one 3×3 cake (9 tiles, subtraction within 10). Paid: five distinct cake designs with subtraction within 20, a 'frosting drip' animation that gets messier the longer the child thinks (purely decorative — no penalty), and a 'decorate the flipped tile' sticker reward.
assetNeeds: Cake illustration in 9-panel grid (5 distinct cake designs)
Frosting-blob cover tile with question-mark decoration (idle/drip animation)
Sticker reward set (sprinkles, candles, stars, cherries — 12 stickers)

games.title: Hop the Lily Pads
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A cheerful frog counts on from a starting number to reach a dragonfly friend; the child taps each lily pad in sequence and the frog leaps with a springy boing — counting on feels like a game of precision jumping, not rote drill.
games.mechanic: A number line of lily pads appears; the frog sits on the starting number; a dragonfly hovers over the target; the child taps successive pads to make the frog hop forward exactly the right number of times, counting aloud with each tap.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 journeys counting on by 1 or 2 from numbers ≤8. Paid: 20 journeys counting on up to 5 from any number ≤15, optional 'eyes-closed' mode where the frog leaps and the child must tap to say how many hops happened, and a bonus dragonfly-catching vignette.
assetNeeds: Lily pad path (8-15 pads, animated ripple when landed on)
Hop-count speech bubble (shows current count-on number)

games.title: Fact Family Treehouse
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Three animal siblings live in a treehouse and all their furniture comes in fact-family sets — the child earns each piece of furniture by completing a related fact; when the whole family is in, the treehouse lights up and the siblings have a pillow fight.
games.mechanic: A treehouse silhouette has four empty furniture slots; each round shows a partial equation (addend + addend = ?, or sum - addend = ?); drag the correct number tile to the blank; each correct answer pops a charming furniture sprite into the treehouse.
games.freeSample: Free: one fact family (e.g., 3+4=7, 4+3=7, 7-3=4, 7-4=3) with visible number bond scaffold. Paid: 12 fact families across sums 6-18, three treehouse themes (jungle/underwater/cloud), hidden scaffolds, and the pillow-fight vignette unlock.
assetNeeds: Treehouse silhouette with 4 furniture slots (3 themes: jungle/underwater/cloud)
Furniture sprite set (12 items: lamp, rug, bed, bookshelf, etc.)

games.title: True or False Treasure
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A pirate parrot only eats TRUE equation scrolls and spits fake ones overboard with a dramatic squawk — deciding which equations are true feels like being the parrot's quality-control inspector, a role kids love to play.
games.mechanic: Equation cards drift across the screen on the tide; drag (or tap) any TRUE equation into the parrot's beak; the parrot chomps with a satisfied 'SQUAWK'; drag a FALSE one and the parrot spits it overboard with a cartoonish gurgle and wobble.
games.freeSample: Free: 8 equation cards, sums ≤10, clearly true/false. Paid: 30 cards across three rounds covering sums to 20, equations with missing addends, and equations that use subtraction on either side; parrot collects TRUE ones into a treasure chest that fills up.
assetNeeds: Equation scroll card (parchment style, bold numerals)
Ocean deck backdrop with drifting tide

games.title: Ghost Number Detective
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A friendly ghost has smudged numbers on every sign in a haunted mansion — the child is the ghost-detective who spots what each smudged number must be from the surrounding equation clues; finding all the ghost numbers makes the mansion glow warm and cozy.
games.mechanic: A richly illustrated haunted-mansion scene hides equations on portraits, signs, and banners — each has one number smudged; tap the smudge, choose the correct missing number from a small pop-up panel, and watch the sign clear with a sparkle; find all hidden equations to finish.
games.freeSample: Free: the mansion hallway (5 hidden equations, within 10). Paid: four mansion rooms (20 equations total, within 20, spanning addition and subtraction), Easter-egg ghost reactions on non-equation taps, and a candlelit 'all-clear' celebration vignette.
assetNeeds: Equation sign/portrait with smudge overlay and clear animation

games.title: Number Tower Builder
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A tiny construction crew needs to stack numbered floors on a skyscraper in the right order — mis-ordered floors bounce off with a comic spring and the hard-hat-wearing beetle foreman shakes his head in exaggerated disbelief, then kindly points to the right spot.
games.mechanic: A set of 5 number tiles appears in a side tray in scrambled order; drag each tile to a floor slot on the skyscraper frame; floors must be placed in ascending order; correct placement clicks into place with a clunk; wrong placement bounces off; finish all 5 floors to see the crane drop a flag.
games.freeSample: Free: four rounds ordering numbers 1-30. Paid: 16 rounds spanning 1-120 (numbers in sequence and with gaps), a 'mystery number' mode where one tile is blank and the child must figure out which number belongs, and a skyscraper showcase at the end.
assetNeeds: Skyscraper frame with numbered floor slots (5 floors)

games.title: Bundle-Up Boutique
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A fashionable llama runs a candy shop where sweets are bundled into bags of ten — the child dresses the shop window display by bundling loose candies into tens bags and placing them on the display shelf, then arranges the leftovers; the llama oohs and aahs at the perfectly dressed display.
games.mechanic: A pile of loose candy sprites appears; drag groups of 10 onto a bag to bundle them; each full bag drops onto the tens shelf; remaining candies go on the ones shelf; tap a number tile to label how many tens and ones; the llama strikes a runway pose when the display is complete.
games.freeSample: Free: three displays, numbers 11-30 (at most 3 bags). Paid: 15 displays from 11 to 99, a 'guess the total' mode where bags are pre-bundled and the child reads the tens/ones, and a llama fashion-show walk at the end of each session.
assetNeeds: Candy sprite (small, colorful — loose and bundled-bag states)
Shop window display with tens shelf and ones shelf
Number label tiles (0-9 for tens and ones)

games.title: More-or-Less Duel
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two competitive but friendly dinosaurs each hold a number on a banner and beg to be the one that gets the trophy — the child feeds the trophy to the correct dino (greater or lesser, depending on the round's rule); the winner dino does an outrageously smug victory lap.
games.mechanic: Two dinosaur characters appear holding number banners (two-digit numbers); the prompt says 'Feed the GREATER' or 'Feed the LESSER'; drag the trophy to the correct dino; correct dino celebrates with a tiny victory lap; wrong dino does a gentle 'aw shucks' droop — no shame, just a restart nudge.
games.freeSample: Free: 8 rounds with two-digit numbers ≤50, 'greater' only. Paid: 24 rounds with numbers up to 120, alternating greater/lesser prompts, a 'same?' challenge where the child must notice equal numbers (both dinos share the trophy with a synchronized bow), and unlockable dino costumes.
assetNeeds: Arena backdrop with confetti cannon for victory

games.title: The Adding Machine Café
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A steampunk café has a spectacular adding machine that combines a two-digit order with a one-digit tip — the child puts both numbers in, pulls the espresso lever, and the machine produces the total with theatrical steam and a little bell ding; no carrying anxiety, just invention delight.
games.mechanic: Drag a two-digit number tile into the large funnel and a one-digit tile into the small funnel; pull the lever; the machine animates (gears/steam) then outputs the sum on a receipt; the child taps a 'correct!' stamp or 'try again' button to confirm; a quirky café patron picks up their order.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 rounds, two-digit + one-digit with no regrouping, sum ≤ 50. Paid: 18 rounds including regrouping cases up to 99, a 'predict the receipt' mode where the child writes the sum before the machine reveals, and 6 unlockable café-patron characters.
assetNeeds: Steampunk adding machine (2 funnels, lever, gear wheel, steam vents, receipt slot)
Café patron characters (6: bear/cat/owl/fox/penguin/frog, each with idle/pick-up-order)

games.title: Ten-More, Ten-Less Telescope
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A stargazing mouse has a telescope that can jump exactly ten stars forward or backward in the night sky — answering correctly reveals a constellation animal one star at a time, and the child can name the shape when it's done.
games.mechanic: A grid of star tiles covers a constellation illustration; each tile shows a two-digit number with a prompt (+10 or -10); tap the correct resulting number from three choices to reveal that star; complete all stars to see the full constellation and name it.
games.freeSample: Free: one constellation (8 tiles, all +10 from numbers under 80). Paid: six constellations spanning +10 and -10 from any two-digit number, three 'bonus' constellation tiles that ask ±1 as well, and a telescope star-chart keepsake that fills as constellations are completed.
assetNeeds: Night-sky backdrop with Milky Way band

games.title: Subtract the Skyscraper
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A wrecking-ball penguin is demolishing an old skyscraper floor by floor — subtracting multiples of ten tears off a floor with a satisfying crumble; the child directs the penguin to the right floor each time, and the building shrinks in real time.
games.mechanic: A skyscraper sprite shows floors labeled with multiples of ten from 90 down to 10; the current problem appears (e.g., 80 - 30 = ?) on a blueprint; the child taps the floor corresponding to the answer; correct tap triggers a wrecking-ball swing and the floor crumbles off; the penguin hops to the next level.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 problems subtracting multiples of 10, starting from numbers ≤ 60. Paid: 20 problems from any multiple-of-10 up to 90, a 'mystery starting floor' mode, and a slow-motion demolition replay animation when the building is fully down.
assetNeeds: Skyscraper sprite with 9 labeled floors and per-floor crumble animation

games.title: Ruler Road Trip
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Three road-tripping animals have bags that only fit objects shorter, the same length, or longer than a reference suitcase — sorting luggage into the right compartment before the road trip starts creates urgency-free packing comedy.
games.mechanic: A car with three luggage compartments appears: SHORTER / SAME / LONGER; a reference object sits on the roof rack; object sprites drift over from a pile; drag each object into the correct compartment; a tiny animation of the object fitting snugly (or wobbling because it's wrong) plays.
games.freeSample: Free: 8 objects using direct visual comparison only. Paid: 18 objects across three rounds, including a 'measure with paper clips' mode where a paper-clip ruler appears on the object, and a 'broken ruler' challenge where only relative comparison works.
assetNeeds: Car with three luggage compartments (SHORTER/SAME/LONGER labels)
Object sprite set (18 everyday items of varying lengths)

games.title: Inch-Worm Explorer
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A literal inch-worm named Inca explores the classroom by scooting one inch at a time along objects — the child counts her hops to measure each object, and she gasps dramatically when she reaches the end ('IT'S SIX WHOLE ME-S!!'), making non-standard measurement feel like an expedition.
games.mechanic: An object sprite (pencil, leaf, crayon, etc.) appears with tick-mark positions; the inch-worm starts at the left end; the child taps each tick mark one at a time to hop the worm forward; a counter increments with each hop; when the worm reaches the end, the child taps the counter to confirm the total length.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 objects up to 8 inch-worm lengths. Paid: 15 objects up to 15 lengths, a 'how many paper clips?' variant measuring with a different unit so children compare units, and an explorer map that fills in as objects are measured.
assetNeeds: Tick-mark measurement overlay on each object
Explorer map backdrop with object silhouette pins

games.title: Clock Shop Helper
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A befuddled owl runs a clock shop where every clock has its hands missing — the child earns the hands by telling time correctly and snaps them onto each clock; when every clock is set right, the shop opens with a chorus of ticks, cuckoos, and chimes.
games.mechanic: The clock-shop diorama shows 6 blank-faced clocks on the wall; a digital time prompt appears; the child drags the hour hand and minute hand (on half-hours and hours only) to the correct positions on the active clock; correct placement snaps them in with a tick; wrong placement gently swings back.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 clocks, hours only. Paid: 18 clocks across hours and half-hours, a 'match the digital and analog' pairing mode, a cuckoo-clock that cuckoos the correct number of times as a hint, and 3 unlockable shop themes (underwater/space/enchanted-forest).
assetNeeds: Clock face sprite with movable hour and minute hand (drag-and-snap)
Clock shop backdrop with 6 wall-clock silhouettes (3 themes)
Cuckoo-clock bonus sprite with cuckoo animation

games.title: Tally-Mark Town Census
games.subject: math
games.funHook: The mayor of a tiny cartoon town needs a census — the child collects data by sorting townsfolk into categories and recording tally marks, then peels a sticker for each completed category; the mayor throws a bigger party the more complete the census is.
games.mechanic: Townsfolk characters walk across a street scene; tap each character to sort it into one of three category bins (e.g., hats/no-hats, or dogs/cats/birds); after sorting, drag tally stickers to the chart — a fifth tally auto-crosses the bundle; tap a category bar to confirm its total.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 categories, 10 townsfolk to sort, tally marks pre-started. Paid: 12 rounds with 2-4 categories and up to 20 townsfolk, a 'who has more/fewer?' comparison prompt after each census, and unlockable mayor-party vignette when all pages complete.
assetNeeds: Townsfolk sprite set (20 characters with distinguishing features: hats, glasses, bow-ties, etc.)
Town-street backdrop with party decorations for finale

games.title: Shape Composer Studio
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A robot toy factory needs the child to build robot characters by combining shape parts — a half-circle head on a rectangle body with triangle ears — making geometry composition literally character design; each finished robot does a little personality showcase.
games.mechanic: A robot silhouette appears showing which shapes it needs; a palette of shape parts (triangles, squares, rectangles, half-circles, quarter-circles) sits in a tray; the child drags each shape to the correct slot on the silhouette; shapes can be flipped/rotated with a tap; completion triggers the robot's personality showcase animation.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 robot designs using 2-3 shapes each, no rotation needed. Paid: 12 robot designs using composites of up to 6 shapes (including the new shape decomposing challenge where the child taps an existing shape to split it), 5 robot personality animations, and a robot parade finale.
assetNeeds: Shape part sprites (triangle/square/rectangle/half-circle/quarter-circle in 4 colors, flip/rotate states)
Robot factory backdrop with conveyor belt
Robot parade finale animation with 12 robots marching

games.title: Equal-Share Campfire
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A campfire group of forest friends needs their food divided equally — the child drags each equal piece to the right friend; a friend who gets unequal pieces comically tips over; the one who gets their fair share roasts their portion over the fire with a satisfied sigh.
games.mechanic: A food item (circle/rectangle/square) appears divided by dotted lines into equal or unequal parts; the child must first decide 'equal or not?' by tapping a badge, then drag the equal pieces to matching friend placeholders; unequal pieces bounce back with a gentle wobble.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 rounds, halves only, circles and squares. Paid: 20 rounds covering halves, thirds, and fourths on circles, squares, and rectangles; unequal-part decoy rounds; a 'draw the fold' drag-to-divide challenge; and three unlockable campfire-site themes.
assetNeeds: Food shape sprites (circle/square/rectangle with equal and unequal division overlays)
Campfire backdrop with s'mores prop (3 themes: forest/beach/mountain)

games.title: Counting-On Caterpillar
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A caterpillar grows a new segment every time the child counts on correctly to solve an addition problem — after enough segments the caterpillar spins a chrysalis and bursts out as a spectacular butterfly; kids are genuinely invested in completing the transformation.
games.mechanic: An addition sentence appears (e.g., 7 + 4); the caterpillar sits on the larger addend; the child taps the caterpillar's tail the correct number of times (4 more), counting aloud; each tap adds a segment and the number box ticks up; reaching the sum triggers a satisfied wiggle and segment-lock.
