games.freeSample: Free: 6 problems, count on by 1 or 2, sum ≤10, caterpillar has 8 segments before metamorphosis. Paid: 20 problems counting on up to 6 from any addend ≤14, full chrysalis-to-butterfly metamorphosis animation, 4 butterfly color variants to unlock, and a garden diorama the butterflies populate.
assetNeeds: Caterpillar character (body with addable segments, idle-wiggle/new-segment/satisfied)
Leaf backdrop with garden diorama for butterfly collection
Tap-counter display showing current count-on value

games.title: The Fact Family House
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Each fact family lives in a house and needs all four sentences above their door to move in — the child builds each equation by dragging number and operation tiles into the door frame; when all four are placed correctly the family celebrates a housewarming with streamers.
games.mechanic: A house diorama has four equation frames on the door; number tiles and +/-/= tiles sit in a side tray; drag and drop tiles into the correct slots for all four fact-family sentences; a 'check' banner auto-appears when all four frames are filled; correct = streamers and family move-in animation.
games.freeSample: Free: 2 fact families (sums 7 and 8), operation tiles pre-placed. Paid: 10 fact families from sums 6-18, operation tiles included in the drag tray, a 'memory mode' where one equation is shown then hidden and the child reconstructs it from memory, and 3 house-style themes.
assetNeeds: House diorama frame (3 style themes: cottage/townhouse/treehouse)
Animal family move-in characters (4 per family, 3 family types)

games.title: Number Line Hopscotch
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A bunny hops a hopscotch number line, adding or subtracting tens and ones by jumping; the child chalks the landing square and the bunny makes an exaggerated precision-landing pose — adding on a number line becomes a physical, spatial game.
games.mechanic: A number-line hopscotch path appears from 0 to 100; the bunny stands on a two-digit start number; a problem card shows +/- a multiple of ten or single digit; the child taps the correct landing square; correct tap = bunny's athletic precision-landing; wrong square = friendly stumble and try-again nudge.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 hops, adding/subtracting 10 from numbers under 60. Paid: 24 hops across four sets: +10/-10, +1/-1, +teen/-teen (no regrouping), and a mixed challenge; number line zooms in/out dynamically; a 'blindfold hop' where the child predicts without seeing the full line.
assetNeeds: Hopscotch number line path (0-100 with chalk-square styling)
Bleachers backdrop with cheering crowd silhouette

games.title: Tens-and-Ones Toy Store
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A toy store sells toys in boxes of ten and single loose toys — the child reads the shelf label (a two-digit number) and collects exactly the right boxes and singles as stickers; every correct shelf stocked reveals a surprise toy that bounces to life on the shelf.
games.mechanic: A toy-store shelf page shows silhouettes of box-stickers and single-stickers; a two-digit number appears on the price tag; the child drags the correct number of tens-box stickers and ones-stickers to their silhouettes; all match = shimmer reveal of the shelf toy with a little personality animation.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 shelf pages, numbers 11-39 (at most 3 tens boxes). Paid: 20 shelf pages from 10-99, a 'read the shelf' reverse mode where toys are shown and the child writes the two-digit label, and a toy-store grand-opening celebration when all pages are filled.
assetNeeds: Surprise toy sprites (20 distinct: robot/doll/car/ball/drum/etc., each with 1-second personality animation)

games.title: Comparison Carnival
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two-digit numbers drift through a carnival sky on balloons; a carnival barker cat shouts 'POP ALL NUMBERS GREATER THAN ___!'; popping the right balloon earns a confetti burst while wrong pops gently re-inflate (never punishing, just bouncy).
games.mechanic: Balloons drift slowly across the screen; each holds a two-digit number; a carnival sign shows the comparison target (e.g., 'Pop numbers GREATER THAN 47'); tap the matching balloons to pop them with a confetti splash; tap a wrong balloon and it gently re-inflates with a boing; pop all correct ones to clear the round.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 rounds with 6 balloons each, numbers ≤ 60, greater-than only. Paid: 12 rounds with up to 10 balloons, numbers to 120, alternating greater/less-than targets, a 'between two numbers' advanced round, and unlockable balloon character faces.
assetNeeds: Balloon sprites with two-digit numbers (8 color variants)
Carnival sky backdrop with Ferris wheel silhouette

games.title: Addition Street Parade
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A marching band is assembling for a parade — the child solves addition word problems to unlock each band member who joins the parade in order; a longer parade = louder music and more ridiculous formations, so kids keep solving to build the most chaotic parade possible.
games.mechanic: A word-problem card appears (illustrated, not text-heavy) showing a scene; the child taps the correct sum from three choices; each correct answer pops a band-member sprite onto the parade path; the parade marches in real time with each new addition; all 8 members = finale.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 word problems, sums ≤ 10, two addends only. Paid: 20 word problems covering two and three addends up to 20, a 'remix the parade' mode where the child changes the story numbers to build different totals, and 12 unlockable band-member characters.
assetNeeds: Band leader character (duck with baton, idle/conduct/celebrate)
Band member sprites (12: tuba-bear/drum-cat/flute-rabbit/trumpet-owl/etc., each with marching animation)

games.title: Worm Subtraction Garden
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A garden scene hides the answer to a subtraction problem in plain sight — the child finds the 'missing worms' that slipped underground, completing the subtraction by spotting exactly how many left; the caught worms peek back out with tiny surprised expressions.
games.mechanic: A garden illustration shows a starting group of worms; some have burrowed underground (a hole covers them); the subtraction sentence appears; the child taps each hole to reveal how many hid; when the right number of holes is tapped the subtraction equation completes and the hidden worms pop up in surprise.
games.freeSample: Free: one garden scene, 6 rounds, subtracting within 10. Paid: four garden scenes with 20 rounds each covering subtraction within 20, a 'double hide' where both the starting amount and the hidden amount must be found, and Easter-egg animals that react to non-problem taps.
assetNeeds: Underground hole with cover-state and reveal animation

games.title: Doubles Disco
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A disco dance floor has pairs of identical dancers who only come together when their doubles fact is matched — every correct pair triggers a synchronized dance move; the more pairs matched, the more packed the dance floor and the more elaborate the finale choreography.
games.mechanic: A grid of cards shows doubles addition facts on some and their sums on others; tap two cards to test a match; a match triggers both cards to flip-reveal their matching dancers doing a synchronized move and lock; a non-match gently flips back; fill the floor to trigger the finale.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 pairs (doubles 1+1 through 6+6), 2×6 card grid. Paid: 12 pairs (doubles 1+1 through 12+12), plus 'near-doubles' bonus mode (5+6, 7+8), a 3-layer choreography finale, and unlockable disco-dancer costume accessories.
assetNeeds: Card front (doubles fact or sum, bold numerals on colored background)
Disco dance floor backdrop with mirror-ball and colored lights

games.title: Making-Ten Marshmallow Roast
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Each marshmallow skewer must have exactly 10 marshmallows to roast perfectly — the child builds each skewer by adding the right number of marshmallows to complete the ten; an under-stuffed skewer droops sadly and an over-stuffed one topples comically.
games.mechanic: A skewer sprite appears with some marshmallows already threaded (e.g., 6); a number panel shows 'need ___' more; the child taps marshmallow sprites to add them one by one or drags a bundle; when 10 total are on, the skewer goes over the fire and toasts with a perfect golden-brown glow.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 skewers, starting amounts 6-9, adding to 10. Paid: 20 skewers spanning starting amounts 1-9 (making 10 from any decomposition), a 'trade' mode where the child swaps marshmallow colors to match a target decomposition, and s'mores assembly as a bonus reward.
assetNeeds: Marshmallow skewer sprite (with thread-on slots for 10, toasting animation)
Marshmallow sprites (4 colors, loose and threaded states)
Camper character (bear with chef's hat, idle/pleased/droopy/topple-laugh)

games.title: Near-Doubles Launch Pad
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A rocket launch pad has a doubles booster — put in any near-doubles problem (like 6+7) and the machine shows the doubles anchor (6+6=12) then boosts by one with a rocket-trail effect; the child predicts the final orbit number.
games.mechanic: Drag two near-consecutive number tiles into the launch pod; pull the rocket lever; the machine first displays the doubles step (lower+lower) in a booster chamber; then the +1 boost launches a rocket to the answer orbit; the child taps the correct orbit-ring to confirm the sum.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 near-doubles up to 6+7. Paid: 16 near-doubles up to 9+10 and 10+11, a 'predict before launch' mode, three rocket skin unlocks, and a solar-system diorama that fills as launches succeed.
assetNeeds: Rocket sprite (3 skin variants, launch/orbit states)
Launch pad with booster chamber display and lever
Solar system diorama backdrop with planet placeholders
Scientist character (mouse in lab coat, idle/launch-countdown/cheer)

games.title: Ten-Frame Farm
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A busy farm scene hides ten-frame arrangements of animals everywhere — in the barn, in the field, on the fence; the child spots which arrangements match the target number, turning subitizing into a Where's-Waldo-style hunt.
games.mechanic: A richly detailed farm scene contains a dozen embedded ten-frame panels (some visible, some half-hidden in the scenery); the prompt shows a target number; the child taps every ten-frame arrangement in the scene that shows that number; each correct tap blooms a rosette; miss one and a rooster crows a gentle hint.
games.freeSample: Free: farm scene, 3 rounds, targets 6-8. Paid: four seasonal farm scenes with 5 rounds each, targets spanning 5-20 (including non-standard arrangements), Easter-egg taps on non-ten-frame elements that trigger funny animal reactions.
assetNeeds: Ten-frame panel sprite (embedded seamlessly into scene, highlight state)

games.title: Skip-Count Galaxy
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A space garden grows by skip-counting — water each star-plant with the next number in a counting sequence (by 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s) and it grows to the next spectacular stage; a galaxy blooms as more plants grow, turning number-sequence practice into satisfying galactic gardening.
games.mechanic: A star-plant at a numbered stage needs the next number to grow; the child taps the correct number tile from four choices; each correct choice triggers a watering-can pour and the plant shoots up a stage with sparkle; wrong choice shows a friendly wilting pause then resets the choice.
games.freeSample: Free: counting by 1s to 30, one plant through 5 growth stages. Paid: counting by 2s, 5s, and 10s to 120, six plant species with 8 stages each, a galaxy diorama that fills as plants bloom, and a 'fill the missing count' challenge mode.
assetNeeds: Star-plant species sprites (6 types: crystal/flame/moon/cloud/ice/sun, each with 8 growth stages)
Galaxy diorama backdrop with planet/nebula placeholders filling in

games.title: Greater-Than Monster's Feast
games.subject: math
games.funHook: The Greater-Than Monster always eats the bigger number and the Less-Than Monster always eats the smaller — but they keep switching seats to trick the child; figuring out which monster gets fed adds a delightful identity-puzzle layer to comparison.
games.mechanic: Two monster characters appear holding number cards; a prompt says 'The Greater-Than Monster is hungry!' or 'the Less-Than Monster!'; the child taps the monster who should eat; correct monster chomps with frenzy; wrong monster looks offended and points to the right one with an exaggerated pout.
games.freeSample: Free: 8 rounds, two-digit numbers ≤ 60, monsters stay in fixed seats. Paid: 24 rounds up to 120, monsters swap seats each round (the identity-puzzle mechanic), equal-number rounds where both monsters share (they arm-wrestle into a handshake), and unlockable monster accessories.
assetNeeds: Feast table backdrop with food-pile prop

games.title: Measurement Olympics
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Animal athletes compete in length events and need to be sorted onto the medal podium (longest/medium/shortest); the child measures each athlete with paper-clip units and sorts them; outrageous size mismatches between tiny snails and enormous giraffes playing in the same event make every sort funny.
games.mechanic: Three animal athletes appear with a paper-clip unit ruler; the child drags the ruler end-to-end along each athlete to read the length; then drags each athlete to the GOLD/SILVER/BRONZE podium in descending length order; all three correct = anthem fanfare and medal ceremony.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 events, direct visual comparison only. Paid: 12 events using the paper-clip ruler, including events with deceptive-looking animals (a curled-up elephant shorter than a stretched-out worm), a 'how much longer?' subtraction bonus prompt, and a full medal-ceremony finale.
assetNeeds: Animal athlete sprites (12 pairs: snail/giraffe, worm/elephant, ant/caterpillar, etc., each with stretch/curl/compact states)
Paper-clip unit ruler sprite (extendable by dragging)

games.title: Tally-Chart Weather Station
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A meteorologist frog tracks the week's weather by growing her tally chart — each day's weather observation (tapped from a scene) adds a tally mark and the chart fills up; at week's end the frog makes a weather report that the child helps script, making data feel like storytelling.
games.mechanic: A week-grid shows 7 day-scenes; the child taps each day's sky condition (sunny/cloudy/rainy/snowy) to sort it; each tap adds a tally mark to the correct row; the frog pumps her fist after each mark; after 7 days a comparison prompt ('Which happened most?') unlocks the weather-report script choice.
games.freeSample: Free: one week, 2 weather categories, comparison prompt only. Paid: 4 weeks with 3-4 categories each, totals up to 7, a 'predict the next day' bonus prompt, and the frog's weekly weather-report animation that summarizes the data in a funny broadcast.
assetNeeds: Day-scene sky illustrations (7 per week: sunny/partly-cloudy/cloudy/rainy/snowy variants)
Tally-mark chart with rows and frog's fist-pump animation on each mark
TV-broadcast frame for frog's finale report

games.title: Word-Problem Diorama Detective
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Each word problem is a tiny crime — something is missing from a diorama scene and the child must use the math to solve the mystery and restore the missing sprites; the word 'mystery' and the detective framing makes addition and subtraction feel like power, not chore.
games.mechanic: A diorama scene appears with silhouettes of missing items; a word-problem caption explains the scenario; the child solves the addition or subtraction to determine the missing quantity; then drags that exact number of item sprites from the tray to the silhouettes; all filled = detective stamp and scene lights up.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 mystery scenes, one-step addition within 10. Paid: 20 scenes covering addition, subtraction, and two-step problems within 20; mystery difficulty scale from 'easy case' to 'tough case'; a detective badge that fills with stars; and 3 diorama themes (city/forest/space).
assetNeeds: Detective character (cat with magnifying glass, idle/thinking/stamp)
Diorama scene frames (20 scenes across 3 themes)
Missing-item sprites (20 sets matching each scene)

games.title: Equation Carnival Ride
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A carnival ride only lets TRUE equations board; FALSE ones float away on clown balloons; the child pops every balloon carrying a TRUE equation to let its passengers board while false equations drift off laughing — truth-sorting becomes a rapid joyful scan.
games.mechanic: Balloons float across a carnival-ride queue; each carries an equation (some true, some false, some with a missing number); a prompt says 'Pop only the TRUE ones' or 'Pop ones where the missing number is ___'; tap a TRUE/matching balloon to pop it with a jubilant rider reaction; wrong pop bounces back with a clown honk.
games.freeSample: Free: 8 balloons, true/false only, within 10. Paid: 24 balloons across 4 rounds including missing-number balloons, equations with sums on both sides, and a mixed-operation round; clown character unlocks with accumulated pops.
assetNeeds: Carnival ride backdrop (Ferris wheel with loading gate)
Balloon sprites with equation display (6 color variants)
Balloon pop with jubilant rider animation (small character pops out)

games.title: Clock-Hands Race to School
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A sleepy bear needs to catch the school bus — the child reads the clock at each bus stop and taps the matching digital time to help the bear sprint to the next stop; a too-late tap means the bus just-barely-waits (never leaves — no stress, just comedy).
games.mechanic: A map of bus stops appears; at each stop an analog clock face shows the time (hours and half-hours); the child taps the correct digital time from three choices; correct answer = bear runs jubilantly to the next stop with a silly sprint animation; a wrong choice = bus waits with an exaggerated tapping-foot animation before the retry.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 stops, hours only. Paid: 18 stops across hours and half-hours, a reverse round where the digital time is shown and the child taps the matching analog clock, a 'almost late!' animation sequence for extra drama, and 3 school-route map themes.
assetNeeds: Bus stop scene with analog clock face (drag-free — display only)

games.title: Shape-Sorter Postal Service
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A postal service sorts packages by defining attributes — only triangles go to Triangle Town, only closed shapes go to Closedville, only shapes with no corners go to Roundsville; the postal worker celebrates overzealously for every correctly sorted package and dramatically drops rejected ones.
games.mechanic: Package sprites arrive on a conveyor with shape silhouettes; a postal-worker character announces the sorting rule; the child drags each package to the correct mail-bin (labeled by attribute, not by shape name); correct bin = postal worker does a tiny victory-stomp; wrong bin = package slides back with a gentle 'hmm, check the rule' prompt.
games.freeSample: Free: 8 packages, 2 bins (closed vs open shapes). Paid: 20 packages across 5 rule-sets (closed/open, corners/no-corners, equal sides/unequal, 3 sides/4 sides/more), a 'make your own rule' free-play mode, and unlockable postal-worker character variants.
assetNeeds: Package sprites with shape silhouettes (20 distinct shapes including defining and non-defining attribute variants)
Mail-bin labels (attribute description, not shape name)

games.title: Compose-a-Shape Architect
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A cheerful architect owl commissions the child to build famous buildings out of geometric shapes — a castle from squares and triangles, a rocket from rectangles and triangles — and the building 'comes alive' as each shape is placed, sprouting windows and waving flags.
games.mechanic: A building outline appears with labeled shape-slots; a palette of 2D shapes (triangles, squares, rectangles, half-circles) is in the tray; the child drags shapes to matching slots, resizing/rotating allowed; each correct placement animates a detail appearing on the building (window, door, flag); completion makes the building 'breathe' with a subtle life animation.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 buildings using only squares and rectangles (2-4 shapes). Paid: 12 buildings using all 5 shape types with composing and decomposing challenges (tap a rectangle to split into two squares), a 'free build' mode, and an architecture portfolio showcase.
assetNeeds: 2D shape palette sprites (triangle/square/rectangle/half-circle/quarter-circle in multiple sizes and rotation states)
Building-alive animation details (animated windows, waving flags, chimney smoke)

games.title: Equal-Parts Pizza Maker
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A pizza machine has a cutter that splits doughs into equal parts — but only if the child sets the cutter correctly; wrong settings produce hilariously lopsided pizzas that the machine blows a raspberry at, while equal splits earn a genuine authentic-pizzeria ding.
games.mechanic: A pizza dough appears on the machine conveyor; a customer order specifies 'halves' or 'fourths' or 'thirds'; the child drags cut-line guides across the dough to divide it; the machine checks equality visually (pieces shade green/red); pull the lever to confirm; correct = pizzeria ding and equal slices pop onto plates; wrong = raspberry and redo.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 rounds cutting into halves only (circles and rectangles). Paid: 18 rounds covering halves, thirds, and fourths on circles, rectangles, and squares; a 'how many equal parts?' naming prompt; an 'is this fair?' judgment mode; and 4 unlockable pizza topping combinations as rewards.
assetNeeds: Pizza machine with conveyor, cut-line drag rails, and lever
Pizza dough sprites (circle/rectangle/square, with equal-green/unequal-red shading overlay)
Equal-slice result plate with topping reward
Pizzeria backdrop with checkered floor and oven

games.title: Regrouping Bridge Builder
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A village is separated from its market by a river — the child builds bridge sections by solving two-digit plus one-digit addition (including regrouping); each correct answer places a bridge plank; when the bridge is complete, a parade of villagers crosses and waves.
games.mechanic: A split-village diorama shows a river with plank-shaped gaps; each round an addition problem appears on a plank in the side tray; the child drags the correct answer tile from a number rack, then places the solved plank onto the bridge; correct plank clicks in solidly; wrong answer shows the plank wobble and fall into the river with a splash.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 planks, no regrouping, sums ≤ 60. Paid: 20 planks including regrouping cases up to 99, a 'place-value scaffold' toggle (shows tens/ones decomposition on demand), the villager-parade reward vignette, and 3 village-setting themes.
assetNeeds: Villager parade sprites (6 characters with crossing/waving animation)
River splash effect for fallen planks

games.title: Subtraction Demolition Derby
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Rogue tens-blocks are floating through a demolition zone; the child pops the correct number of them to make the target subtraction result; each popped block crumbles dramatically and the remaining blocks build a satisfying tower showing the answer.
games.mechanic: A starting two-digit multiple-of-ten appears as stacked blocks; a subtraction prompt says '- 20' or '- 50'; colored block-clusters float; the child pops exactly the right number of tens-blocks to subtract; each pop crumbles with rubble effect; when the right number is popped the remaining stack lights up as the answer.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 rounds subtracting multiples of 10, starting from multiples ≤ 60. Paid: 20 rounds from any multiple up to 90, a 'how many did I pop?' mode where the child figures out the subtraction from the demolition result, and unlockable demolition-ball skins.
assetNeeds: Tens-block sprites (stacked tower, individual block, crumble-animation)
Demolition zone backdrop with dust cloud effect
Remaining-stack highlight animation (lights up as answer)

games.title: Number Order Expedition
games.subject: math
games.funHook: An explorer rabbit is mapping a newly discovered number jungle; she must plant numbered flags in the right order along the trail to chart the territory; a mis-planted flag causes a funny map-explosion, then she helpfully re-plants it in the right spot.
games.mechanic: A jungle trail path has numbered flag-poles; a set of number tiles appears scrambled in a side pack; the child taps or drags each tile to the flag-pole where it belongs in ascending order; correct placement = flag unfurls with a flap; wrong = comic map-explosion and gentle corrective arrow pointing to the right pole.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 expeditions ordering 5 numbers within 30. Paid: 16 expeditions with 5-8 numbers to order within 120, gap-sequence rounds (only even or only multiples of 5), a 'backwards expedition' ordering in descending order, and an explorer map that fills in as territory is charted.
assetNeeds: Jungle trail path backdrop (4 environment zones: dense/river/clearing/hilltop)

games.title: Morning Routine Time Match
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A bear's chaotic morning routine is scattered across paired cards — matching the analog clock to the right digital time or scene restores the routine; when the final pair matches, the bear rushes out the door and runs for the bus in a slapstick sprint.
games.mechanic: A memory card grid has analog clocks on some cards and digital times (or illustrated morning-routine scenes) on others; tap two cards to test a pair; match = both cards flip to show the bear doing that activity and lock with a happy sound; no-match = gentle flip-back; complete the grid for the bus-sprint finale.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 pairs, hours only, analog↔digital. Paid: 14 pairs spanning analog↔digital and analog↔scene on hours and half-hours, a 'sequence the routine' bonus challenge where matched pairs must be placed in time order, and 3 bear character color variants.
assetNeeds: Bear character in morning-routine scenes (14 illustrated scenes: wake/brush-teeth/eat-cereal/etc.)
Analog clock card (hours and half-hours, clear hands)

games.title: Defining-Features Fence
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A farmer needs to fence shapes into paddocks by their DEFINING features — triangles always go in the 3-sides paddock regardless of size or rotation; but a shape that looks like a triangle but has a curved side goes somewhere else; the farmer's sheep baa appreciatively at each correct sort.
games.mechanic: Shape sprites hop off a truck; each paddock is labeled by a defining attribute (number of sides, number of vertices, presence of right angle); the child drags each shape to its correct paddock; correct sort = sheep baa and shape settles in; wrong = shape hops back out and a defining-vs-non-defining hint highlights.
games.freeSample: Free: 10 shapes, 2 paddocks (3-sided vs 4-sided), no ambiguous cases. Paid: 24 shapes across 4 paddocks including non-defining attribute variants (large/small/rotated triangles all in the same paddock) and 'trick' non-polygon shapes that must go to a special paddock.
assetNeeds: Farm field backdrop with hay bales

games.title: Treasure Map Number Grid
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A pirate treasure is hidden under one square of a hundred chart — the child reveals squares by answering place-value and ±10/1 clue prompts; each revealed square shows a piece of a treasure-map illustration; the full map reveals the buried chest's exact location.
games.mechanic: A 5×5 grid of covered squares overlays a treasure-map illustration; each round a clue appears ('What is 10 more than 34?'); the child taps the correct answer tile; that square of the grid flips to reveal part of the map below; all 25 squares revealed = dig-up-the-chest finale animation.
games.freeSample: Free: one map (25 squares, ±10 clues only, numbers ≤ 60). Paid: four distinct treasure maps with clues spanning tens/ones decomposition, ±10, and ±1 from any two-digit number; a 'wrong square stays face-down one turn' mechanic adding light strategy; unlockable pirate accessories.
assetNeeds: Treasure map illustration (4 variants: island/cave/ship/jungle) divided into 5×5 grid
Covered grid tile (parchment with question mark)

games.title: Bar-Graph Animal Rescue
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A wildlife sanctuary needs a bar graph to track rescued animals — the child places animal stickers onto the graph to build each bar, and as bars grow the animals themselves appear in their sanctuary habitats; a full graph opens the gates and all the animals interact.
games.mechanic: A bar-graph frame appears with category labels; data cards appear one by one showing rescued animal counts; the child drags that number of animal stickers onto the correct bar column; each sticker snaps into the column with a happy squeak; when all bars are built, the sanctuary habitat animates.
games.freeSample: Free: 3-bar graph, up to 5 per bar, single data set. Paid: 12 data sets with 3-5 bars and totals up to 10; comparison prompts ('Which bar is tallest?'); a 'reverse' mode where the bar is shown and the child reads the quantity; and 3 sanctuary habitat themes.
assetNeeds: Bar-graph frame with category labels and column grid (3 habitat themes)
Animal sticker sprites (5 species × 5 color/pose variants)
Sanctuary habitat animation (animals interact when graph is complete)
Wildlife ranger character (owl with clipboard, idle/place-sticker/cheer)

games.title: Adding-On Rocket Launch
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A rocket grows fuel by solving counting-on addition problems — each correct answer pours one fuel canister into the rocket's fuel meter; the child watches the gauge climb stage by stage until the rocket ignites with a spectacular launch sequence; the anticipation of launch drives repeated play.
games.mechanic: An addition problem appears (start + count-on amount); the child taps the correct sum; each correct answer adds one canister to the fuel gauge and the gauge climbs; wrong answer triggers a gentle 'fuel-spill' animation and a retry; when the gauge is full the 10-stage launch sequence plays.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 fuel canisters to launch, counting on by 1-2, within 10. Paid: 20-canister missions counting on up to 6 within 20, 3 rocket designs to unlock, a multi-stage orbital journey after launch, and a mission-log showing all completed launches.
assetNeeds: Rocket sprite (3 designs, with 10-stage launch sequence animation)
Fuel gauge display (empty/filling/full, with 10 canister slots)
Mission control backdrop with launch pad and launch-sequence lighting effects

games.title: Subtraction Sandwich Shop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A sandwich shop serves big stacked sandwiches but hungry customers keep eating layers — the child figures out how many layers remain (or how many were eaten) and feeds the correct remaining-layer count to the inspecting health bear who only approves sandwiches with the right number of layers.
games.mechanic: A layered sandwich sprite appears with some layers 'eaten' (wiggling away with happy munching sounds); the subtraction sentence appears; the child drags the correct number tile representing the remaining layers into the health bear's clipboard; correct = approval stamp and sandwich delivered; wrong = health bear shakes head warmly and resets.
games.freeSample: Free: 6 sandwiches, subtracting within 10, visual layer count clearly shown. Paid: 20 sandwiches subtracting within 20, a 'find the missing eaten amount' variant (missing subtrahend), a 'build then eat' construction mode, and unlockable sandwich topping combinations.
assetNeeds: Sandwich sprite (layered, with individual layers that wiggle/disappear when eaten)
Number tile clipboard for answer selection
Sandwich shop backdrop with counter and display case

games.title: Captain Syllable's Ship
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A pirate captain chops words into syllables with a rubber sword; the ship hops across ocean stops equal to the syllable count, then a sea-monster buddy erupts from the water at the end doing a victory splash.
games.mechanic: A picture + spoken word appears; child taps once per syllable they hear (tap-tapping a drum on screen), then drags the ship to the matching numbered dock (1, 2, or 3 stops). Correct = ship sails and captain does a jig. Wrong = gentle 'hmm' wobble, try again.
games.freeSample: First 3 destination stops (words: cat, rabbit, banana) playable free; the full voyage of 20+ words across 4 themed ocean zones is paid.
assetNeeds: pirate captain character (idle, sword-chop, jig animations)

games.title: Rhyme Mine
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cheerful miner digs through a sparkling underground scene packed with hidden objects; the child hunts for everything that rhymes with the miner's current 'rhyme target' word. Finding a match makes the gem glow and the miner do a tiny happy dance.
games.mechanic: A target word + picture banner sits at the top (e.g. 'CAT'). The underground scene is full of tappable sprite objects. Child taps items whose names rhyme; each correct tap glows and chimes; a wrong tap gives a gentle 'nope!' wobble. Clear all rhymes to unlock the next underground chamber.
games.freeSample: The first chamber (5 items to find, rhyme family: -at words) is free; chambers 2-8 with progressively denser scenes and blended rhyme families are paid.
assetNeeds: 20+ small object sprites (cat, bat, hat, mat, fan, can, pan, man, etc.)

games.title: Phoneme Popper
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A row of floating speech bubbles each contains a single phoneme sound card. A quirky robot announces the target word and children pop every bubble that is a sound IN that word. The robot celebrates correct sets with a funny beep-boop dance.
games.mechanic: The robot speaks a word aloud (e.g. /ship/). 6 phoneme-bubbles drift (including /sh/, /i/, /p/ plus 3 distractors). Child pops the exact phonemes in the word. Pop all correct ones = celebration; pop a wrong one = gentle boing and it refills. Builds to 4-phoneme words.
games.freeSample: 3 rounds with 3-phoneme CVC words free; full 20-round game with digraphs, blends, and phoneme-swap challenges paid.
assetNeeds: speech bubble sprites (empty and filled with letter combos)

games.title: Word Workshop
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A tiny inventor owl runs a word-transformation factory. The child drops a short-vowel word into the funnel, the machine whirs and adds a magic-e, and a new CVCe word pops out. The owl leaps with delight and a mini scene reveals the new word's meaning.
games.mechanic: A short-vowel word card slides into the machine's funnel (e.g. 'cap'). Child pulls the lever. Machine whirs with gears and lights. Output chute pops out the CVCe word ('cape'). Child then taps the matching picture of the new word from 3 choices. 8 transform pairs per round.
games.freeSample: First 3 transforms (cap→cape, kit→kite, hop→hope) free; full 30-word factory across 4 vowel families paid.
assetNeeds: steampunk word-machine with funnel and chute

games.title: Vowel Team Dream
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A sleepy cloud-cat needs its dreamworld built. Each vowel-team word the child correctly reads or completes earns a dream-object that floats into the cloud-cat's floating dream diorama. The more words, the more magical and whimsical the sky world becomes.
games.mechanic: A word with the vowel-team gapped (e.g. 'r__n') appears with the vowel team choices (ai / ee / oa). Child taps the correct vowel team. Correct = the completed word and its picture sprite float into the diorama slot. Child can tap placed sprites to hear the word again.
games.freeSample: First 4 words and 4 diorama slots (ai family) free; the full dreamworld with 6 vowel-team families and 30+ sprites paid.
assetNeeds: 30 small picture sprites for vowel-team words (rain, train, seal, bee, boat, snow, etc.)

games.title: Digraph Detective
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A magnifying-glass-wielding frog detective sorts clues into labeled filing cabinets. Each cabinet bears a digraph (sh, ch, th, wh, ck). Objects bounce in from the evidence conveyor belt and the frog taps where each belongs. The frog does a triumphant 'case closed' pose when a cabinet fills.
games.mechanic: Picture+word cards arrive on a conveyor belt one at a time. Each shows a word with a digraph (ship, chin, whale, thick, duck). Child drags the card to the correct digraph cabinet. Correct = card files itself with a satisfying click; wrong = gentle slide-back with a curious 'hmm?' from the frog.
games.freeSample: Two digraph cabinets (sh and ch, 6 words) free; all 5 digraph cabinets across 25+ words paid.
assetNeeds: frog detective character (idle, tap, triumphant pose)
5 filing cabinet sprites labeled with digraphs

games.title: Blend Blast-Off
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A hungry alien rocket ship only eats words that START with its labeled consonant blend (fl, gr, st, etc.). Child drags floating word-bubbles into the rocket's open hatch. The rocket giggles and zooms on correct feeds; on wrong words it spits them back with a comical 'blorp'.
games.mechanic: The rocket displays a target blend (e.g. 'bl'). Six word-bubbles drift across the sky: some start with bl (blob, blue, blank) and some are distractors (frog, star, clap). Child drags or taps only the bl-words into the hatch. Fill all correct words to launch the rocket with a fun animation.
games.freeSample: One blend family (bl, 4 words) free; all 8 blend families across 40+ words paid.
assetNeeds: alien rocket character (idle, chomp, zoom, blorp)

games.title: Sight Word Superstore
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cheerful store bear runs a sticker shop where every item is labeled. Child reads the sight word on the shelf sign, then taps the matching sticker from three choices. The sticker peels off and shimmer-drops into the collection album. Tap any collected sticker to hear a bear-voiced sentence using the word.
games.mechanic: A shelf sign shows a sight word (e.g. 'because'). Three sticker choices appear below (images with their word labels). Child taps the correct match. Correct = sticker peels and snaps into album. Wrong = gentle 'oh hmm!' and try again. 10 stickers per album page; pages build across the collection.
games.freeSample: First album page (10 Dolch first-grade sight words) free; 5 additional album pages covering all Grade 1 high-frequency words paid.
assetNeeds: store bear character (idle, peel sticker, wink)
60+ distinct cute sticker sprites matching sight words

games.title: Story Town Mayor
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The child is Mayor of Story Town and earns town buildings by answering questions about a short illustrated story. Each correct answer places a new shop, tree, or character into the town diorama. At the end, the town comes alive with tiny animated residents.
games.mechanic: A short 4-panel illustrated story plays (narrated). After each panel, a question card pops up: 'Who did that?', 'Where did it happen?', 'What happened first?' Child taps the correct answer from 3 picture/word choices. Each correct answer earns a town sprite. Final town plays a 5-second 'alive' animation.
games.freeSample: One short story (4 panels, 4 questions, 4 town sprites) free; library of 10+ stories across settings and character types paid.
assetNeeds: town diorama background (empty and filled states)

games.title: The Message Trunk
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A wise old elephant keeps secret messages inside a decorated trunk. Each time the child identifies the lesson/moral of a short story, one jeweled tile on the trunk lid flips to reveal part of the message. When all tiles flip, the elephant trumpets and the full lesson appears with confetti.
games.mechanic: Child hears or reads a short illustrated 4-sentence story. Then 3 'message' cards appear ('Be kind to friends' / 'Always share' / 'Tricks are funny'). Child taps the best lesson. Correct = a trunk tile flips. Four questions per story unlock the full trunk reveal.
games.freeSample: First trunk/story (4 tiles, 1 story) free; 8 trunk stories with escalating passage complexity paid.
assetNeeds: decorated trunk lid with 4 jeweled tile overlays

games.title: Who's Telling the Tale?
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Three puppet-theater stages are labeled 'The Author', 'The Narrator', and 'A Character'. Speech bubbles drift down from above and the child drags each one to the right stage. Puppets pop up on the correct stage and act out the line dramatically.
games.mechanic: A short story excerpt plays. Then speech-bubble cards drift down ('I wrote this story to...', 'Once upon a time...', 'Help! shouted Rosa'). Child drags each to the correct stage-bin. Correct = puppet animates delivering that line. Wrong = bubble bounces back with a curtain-wobble. 8 bubbles per round.
games.freeSample: First round (3 bubbles, simple narrator vs character only) free; full 5-round game including author-perspective cards paid.
assetNeeds: author puppet, narrator puppet, 3 character puppets

games.title: Feelings Detector
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A mood-meter robot has a blank emotion-dial face. After reading a short passage, the child selects feeling-words and 'installs' them as glowing dial badges on the robot. The robot then acts out the emotion with an expressive animated reaction.
games.mechanic: A story sentence appears ('The puppy shivered in the cold, dark shed.'). Three feeling-word badges appear: 'scared', 'excited', 'silly'. Child drags the best-fit badge onto the robot's dial. Correct = robot acts out the feeling (shivering animation). Then a second sentence; repeat for 6 rounds per story.
games.freeSample: First 3 badge-rounds (simple emotion words) free; 5 story-sets with sensory + nuanced vocabulary paid.
assetNeeds: mood-meter robot character (idle + 6 emotion animations: scared, excited, happy, sad, angry, surprised)

games.title: Story vs. Facts Face-Off
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two friendly book characters — a dragon named Fable (fiction) and a beaver named Facts (informational) — stand on either side of a conveyor belt. Book-page tiles slide by and the child sorts them into the right character's reading pile. Each character does a delighted wiggle when they receive their type of text.
games.mechanic: A book-page tile shows a short excerpt or cover feature (talking animals, a table of contents, a made-up character, a real photo with caption). Child drags it to Fable or Facts. Correct = receiving character cheers; wrong = gently bounces back with a questioning look. 12 cards per round across fiction and informational features.
games.freeSample: First 4 cards (very obvious fiction vs. fact examples) free; full 30-card game including mixed features and genre-detective challenges paid.
assetNeeds: 12+ book-page tile sprites (fiction and informational excerpts)

games.title: Scene Detective
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A magnifying-glass-wearing mouse explores rich illustrated story scenes. The narrator reads a story detail, and the child taps the matching element in the scene. The mouse runs over to each found element and stamps it with a golden badge; wrong taps make the mouse scratch his head in a funny way.
games.mechanic: A detailed illustrated scene (e.g. a cozy kitchen from a fairy tale) is shown. The narrator reads 'Find the thing that shows it is MORNING.' Child taps the correct detail (sunlight through window, rooster, breakfast). 4 prompts per scene, each connecting illustration to story detail.
games.freeSample: First scene (4 prompts, 1 story) free; 8 richly illustrated scenes across different story settings paid.
assetNeeds: detective mouse character (idle, run, stamp, head-scratch)
4+ richly illustrated story scenes (each unique setting)

games.title: Tale Twins Compare Club
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two storybook characters ('Tale Twins') sit across a table comparing their adventures. The child draws lines connecting moments from Character A's story to the matching moment in Character B's story. When a match is made, the twins high-five and their shared trait glows.
games.mechanic: Two columns of cards (4 each, one per character). Child taps a card from each column to test a match: 'Both found something lost', 'Both helped a friend', 'Both were brave'. A correct match = twins high-five. Wrong = gentle flip-back and try again. 4 pairs per round, each pair is a shared adventure theme.
games.freeSample: One story-pair (simple comparison, 4 matches) free; 6 story-pairs with increasing complexity of comparison paid.
assetNeeds: story moment card illustrations (8 per pair, 3 pairs minimum)

games.title: Poetry Mood Garden
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A magical garden has sleeping seeds that bloom into different poem-flowers when the child answers questions about a short poem. Each correct answer waters the seed and it grows a stage. A fully bloomed poem-flower sings a snatch of the poem back in a cute voice.
games.mechanic: A 4-line illustrated poem is displayed and read aloud. After each of 4 questions ('What does the garden do at night?', 'Which word sounds like the wind?'), the child waters the flower (tap watering can). 4 correct answers = full bloom + flower sings. Questions span meaning, rhyme, sensory words, and imagery.
games.freeSample: One seed/poem (4 questions) free; garden of 12 poem-seeds across seasons, animals, and weather themes paid.

games.title: Fact Finder HQ
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A news-reporter hamster is filling her bulletin board with story cards. Each correct answer to a 'who/what/where/why' question about an informational passage places a card on the board. When the board is complete, the hamster 'broadcasts' a funny one-sentence summary of the topic.
games.mechanic: A short informational passage (3-4 sentences, narrated) is shown. Then question cards appear one at a time ('What is the main topic?', 'What does a bee do?'). Child taps from 3 answers. Each correct answer flips a bulletin board tile. 5 tiles = full board = hamster broadcast animation.
games.freeSample: First topic (bees, 5 questions, 1 board) free; 10+ informational topics across science and social studies paid.
assetNeeds: corkboard bulletin grid with 5 card slots

games.title: Connection Bridge Builder
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two illustrated 'islands' of information sit on either side of a river. The child draws a glowing bridge-path connecting a person/event/idea on one island to its related person/event/idea on the other. When all bridges are drawn, tiny animated characters run across them.
games.mechanic: An informational text is narrated ('Bees carry pollen. Pollen helps flowers grow.'). Two islands appear, each with 3 labeled picture-cards. Child draws a line from a card on the left island to its matching connection on the right. 3 connections = bridge complete = characters cross with cheers. 3 rounds per text.
games.freeSample: First informational pair (bees and flowers, 3 connections) free; 8 text pairs covering cause-effect, sequence, and comparison paid.
assetNeeds: 6 connection-card sprites per pair (3 pairs minimum)

games.title: Clue Word Catchers
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Strange vocabulary words float through the air like glowing orbs. A curious cat professor points to the orb with the unknown word, then the child reads the surrounding context and pops only the orbs that contain words/phrases that HELP figure it out. The cat professor puts on dramatic glasses to 'investigate'.
games.mechanic: A sentence is shown with one bold unknown word. 5 context-clue orbs float (synonyms, definitions-in-context, picture labels, antonyms, irrelevant distractors). Child pops only the helpful clue-orbs. The cat assembles the clues into a definition card. 5 word-rounds per game.
games.freeSample: First 2 vocabulary words with obvious context clues free; full 20-word game with increasingly subtle clues paid.
assetNeeds: cat professor character (idle, dramatic glasses, assembly pose)

games.title: Book Feature Safari
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A safari guide lemur explores a giant 'Book Jungle' where every text feature is a different wild creature or plant to spot. The child hunts for the heading, the table of contents, the glossary, the caption, and the index. Each find earns a safari sticker and the lemur does a happy tail-wave.
games.mechanic: A full-spread informational-book-page scene is displayed (rich with all text features). Prompt cards appear: 'Find the HEADING', 'Find the CAPTION', 'Find the GLOSSARY'. Child taps the correct feature in the scene. Correct = safari sticker pops; wrong = gentle 'look more carefully!' from the lemur.
games.freeSample: First scene (3 features to find) free; 6 different book-spread scenes with all 6 text features paid.

games.title: Picture or Words?
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two bins sit on a classroom table: a PICTURE bin (camera icon) and a WORDS bin (speech bubble icon). Fact-cards drift down, each describing a piece of information. The child sorts whether you learn that fact from the picture, from the words, or from both (a 3-bin advanced mode).
games.mechanic: An informational page spread is shown. Fact cards drift in ('The bird has red feathers', 'The bird nests in spring', 'The nest is made of sticks'). Child drags each card to the correct source bin. Correct = card files with a pop; wrong = bounces back with a question-mark wobble. 8 cards per spread.
games.freeSample: First spread (4 cards, picture vs words only) free; 8 spreads with 3-bin sorting and increasing text complexity paid.
assetNeeds: camera bin and speech-bubble bin sprites (plus 'both' bin)

games.title: Author's Proof Wall
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An author hedgehog is building a 'proof wall' for her latest book. Every time the child finds a reason the author gives for her opinion, a star evidence card pops onto the hedgehog's wall. When the wall is full, the hedgehog types 'THE END' on a typewriter with a satisfied ding.
games.mechanic: A short persuasive/opinion passage is read aloud (e.g. 'You should eat vegetables. They make you strong. They taste great. They give you energy.'). Opinion card is pinned first. Then 3-4 reason cards appear mixed with distractor cards. Child taps only the supporting-reason cards to pin them to the wall.
games.freeSample: First passage (opinion + 3 reasons, 4 cards) free; 8 passages on kid-friendly opinion topics paid.

games.title: Two-Text Telescope
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A curious astronaut uses a two-sided telescope to compare two short informational texts on the same topic (e.g. two books about frogs). The child draws lines matching SAME ideas across both texts and circles DIFFERENT ideas. The telescope beeps and reveals a 'what both books teach us' star at the end.
games.mechanic: Two mini-passage columns appear (4 fact-cards each). Child connects same-idea cards with a line (both say 'frogs jump') and taps difference-cards to circle them in a different color. 4 matches + 2 differences per round = complete. Astronaut announces the finding with a fun echo effect.
games.freeSample: First topic-pair (frogs: 4 matches, easy) free; 8 topic-pairs with increasing subtlety of similarity paid.

games.title: Fluency Flight
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A little reading bird flies across a sky path. Each sentence stop shows a sentence; the child taps each word in left-to-right order to 'read' it (timing their fluency). The bird flaps smoothly on well-paced taps and dramatically wobbles if taps are too slow or out of order. Arrive at the sunset perch for a peaceful celebration.
games.mechanic: A sentence appears on a cloud. Child taps each word in order (left to right) to make the bird advance. A silent internal pacing guide rewards smooth left-to-right rhythm with a smooth flight animation and choppy or reversed taps with a playful wobble. No timer is shown to the child — only the bird's smoothness signals pacing. 8 sentences per journey.
games.freeSample: First 3 sentences (simple CVC-level text) free; full sky journey of 30+ sentences across 4 reading levels paid.
assetNeeds: reading bird character (smooth flight, wobble, perch)

games.title: Self-Correct Station
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A friendly error-fixing robot named OOPS reads sentences but sometimes mixes up a word. The child spots the wrong word and sends it through the 'fix-it funnel'; the machine spits out the correct word with a satisfying clang and OOPS does a relieved head-pat.
games.mechanic: A sentence is shown with one word highlighted in red (an obviously wrong word that doesn't fit context: 'The dog ate its hat' when the picture shows 'food'). Child taps the red word to put it in the funnel. Then 3 replacement words appear; child taps the correct one. OOPS celebrates and reads the corrected sentence.
games.freeSample: First 3 sentences (very obvious mismatches) free; 20 sentences with context-dependent error detection paid.
assetNeeds: OOPS robot character (idle, confused, relieved head-pat)

games.title: Capital Detective
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A detective parrot scans printed story pages searching for words that NEED a capital letter but are lowercase (and vice versa). The child taps the rule-breakers. The parrot squawks 'CAPITAL CRIME!' and stamps the word with a glowing fix-badge.
games.mechanic: A story page is shown with 8 sentences; some words that should be capitalized (names, start-of-sentence, days/months) are lowercase, and some mid-sentence words are wrongly capitalized. Child taps every error. Correct tap = parrot stamp; tapping a correct word = parrot headshake. All errors found = case closed!
games.freeSample: First page (4 errors, proper names and sentence starts only) free; 8 pages with dates, titles, and mixed errors paid.

games.title: Punctuation Parade
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Three parade-float characters each ONLY eat their matching punctuation mark: Perry the Period eats statements, Quincy the Question Mark eats questions, and Ella the Exclamation eats excited sentences. Sentence scrolls drift by and the child feeds each to the right character.
games.mechanic: A sentence scrolls in WITHOUT its end punctuation ('The cat sat on the mat'). Child reads it, decides its type, and drags it to the correct character's open mouth. Correct = character chomps happily; wrong = character spits it back with a funny sound effect. 12 sentences per round.
games.freeSample: First 4 sentences (very clear statement/question/exclamation) free; full 36-sentence parade with commas-in-series sentences added in later rounds paid.
assetNeeds: Perry (period ball character, idle, chomp, spit)
Quincy (question mark character, idle, chomp, spit)
Ella (exclamation point character, idle, chomp, spit)

games.title: Noun Town
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The child is building Noun Town from scratch. Each correctly identified noun earns a new building or character for the town. Common nouns build plain buildings; proper nouns build fancy named landmarks with signs. At 20 nouns, the town throws a street party.
games.mechanic: A sentence appears. Child taps all the nouns in the sentence. Correct nouns pop up with a '+1 town piece' indicator. Proper nouns pop with a golden star and a named landmark is added. Wrong taps (verbs, adjectives) give a gentle shake. 3-5 sentences per round; town fills across multiple rounds.
games.freeSample: First round (3 sentences, simple common nouns only) free; full 10-round town-build with plurals, proper nouns, and pronoun challenges paid.
assetNeeds: town building sprites (10 common, 5 proper/landmark types)

games.title: Verb Voyage
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A time-traveling ship has three decks: PAST (brown anchor), PRESENT (green anchor), FUTURE (gold rocket). Verb cards float in and the child sorts them to the right time-deck. The ship's crew cheers each correct sort and the verb animates on its deck (e.g. 'jumped' = crew jumping in a flashback bubble).
games.mechanic: Verb cards float up (jumped, runs, will fly, ate, is hopping, will swim). Child drags each to Past, Present, or Future deck. Correct = card snaps to the deck, crew cheers; wrong = card gently slides back with a questioning pose from the helmsman. 9 verbs per voyage (3 per tense).
games.freeSample: First voyage (simple regular past/present only, 6 verbs) free; full 5-voyage journey including 'will' future and irregular verbs paid.
assetNeeds: helmsman captain character (idle, cheer, question pose)
past/present/future deck indicator anchors and animations

games.title: Adjective Makeover Studio
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A plain gray monster sits in a makeover chair. Adjective word-cards appear and for each correct meaning-match, the child drags a costume/decoration element onto the monster. 'Furry' = fur coat; 'shiny' = glitter; 'tiny' = shrink effect; 'three' = three hats. The finished monster struts a runway.
games.mechanic: A sentence appears ('The _____ monster'). An adjective word-card is shown. Child picks the correct visual decoration from 3 choices (matching the adjective's meaning) and drags it onto the monster. Correct = monster transforms and strikes a pose. 8 adjective-transformations per round.
games.freeSample: First 3 adjectives (color, size, shape — very visual) free; full 30-adjective makeover including number, texture, and feeling adjectives paid.
assetNeeds: gray base monster character (makeover chair, runway strut)
30 costume/decoration overlay sprites (furs, glitters, sizes, colors, counts)

games.title: Sentence Fixer Factory
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Broken sentence-fragments fall into a word-factory on a conveyor belt. The child pulls the lever to diagnose 'SENTENCE or FRAGMENT?' then feeds in the missing piece (subject or predicate) to fix fragments. Whole sentences get stamped 'COMPLETE!' and roll off cheerfully; fragments get rebuilt and then stamped.
games.mechanic: A card appears with a sentence or fragment ('The big dog' / 'Ran fast'). Child taps SENTENCE or FRAGMENT. If Fragment: a drag-in tray offers possible missing pieces; child drags the correct one into the funnel. Machine rebuilds it. Complete sentences are applauded as-is. 10 cards per factory shift.
games.freeSample: First 4 cards (obvious fragments missing subject) free; full 30-card factory with predicate-missing and both-missing fragments paid.
assetNeeds: factory building background with conveyor belt
sentence card and fragment card sprites

games.title: Compound Word Kitchen
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cooking-show rabbit chef combines two ingredient-words in a blender machine to create a compound word. When the blender whirrs and pops out the result, a tiny picture of the new word's meaning appears. The rabbit tastes it and reacts dramatically.
games.mechanic: Two word-ingredient cards sit on the counter (sun + flower). Child drags both into the blender in order, then presses the blend button. The machine whirrs and outputs the compound word + a picture. Child then taps the correct meaning from 3 picture-choices. 10 compound word recipes per kitchen session.
games.freeSample: First 3 recipes (sunflower, football, cupcake) free; 40+ compound word recipes across 5 themed kitchen settings paid.
assetNeeds: rabbit chef character (idle, taste reaction: happy/surprised)
blender machine with input slots and output chute

games.title: Prefix Power-Up
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A plain robot needs power-up badges to gain new abilities. Each badge is a prefix (un-, re-, pre-). Child drags the correct prefix badge onto the robot to complete the target word meaning. The robot glows and demonstrates the new power (re- badge = robot recharges; un- badge = robot unboxes something).
games.mechanic: A root word is shown on the robot's chest panel ('do'). The prompt reads 'How would you say: do again?' Child taps the correct prefix badge (un / re / pre) from 3. The badge snaps on, completing the word (redo) and triggering a relevant robot animation. 10 power-ups per round.
games.freeSample: First 3 power-ups (un- prefix only) free; full 30 power-ups across un-, re-, and pre- with meaning-matching paid.
assetNeeds: plain robot character with chest panel (3 power-up animations: unbox, recharge, pre-plan)
chest panel overlay with word display

games.title: Word Family Neighborhood
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cheerful neighborhood map has house clusters labeled with semantic categories (animals, food, feelings, tools). Word cards come flying in on paper airplanes and the child sorts them home to their neighborhood. Each correct sort makes the neighborhood house light up; when a whole street is full, the residents party.
games.mechanic: Category-house bins are shown (Animals / Food / Feelings / Tools). Word cards fly in one at a time with a picture: 'screwdriver', 'lonely', 'avocado', 'penguin'. Child drags each to the correct neighborhood. Correct = house lights up; wrong = paper airplane bounces back with a question-mark. 16 words per neighborhood game.
games.freeSample: First 4 words (one per category, very clear) free; full 5-round neighborhood with 20 categories and nuanced borderline cases paid.
assetNeeds: 4 house/neighborhood sprites (animal, food, feeling, tool themes)

games.title: Shades of Meaning Paint Studio
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A paint-smock-wearing bear artist has a canvas with a scene to paint. But instead of colors, the palette has INTENSITY WORDS (warm/hot/boiling; big/huge/enormous). Child picks the word that matches the intensity shown in the scene and the scene fills in with that shade of expressiveness.
games.mechanic: A scene with an obvious intensity cue appears (a tiny mouse vs a huge bear). Three 'shade words' appear (big / giant / enormous). Child taps the best-fit word and drags it onto the canvas. Correct = the scene fills in perfectly matched; wrong = the paint looks hilariously wrong (tiny word on a huge image). 8 scenes per studio session.
games.freeSample: First 2 scenes (hot/warm/boiling for a fire; quiet/silent/loud for a library) free; 30-scene paint studio across feelings, sizes, sounds, and speeds paid.
assetNeeds: bear artist character (painting pose, proud reveal, comic-wrong reaction)
8+ scene illustrations with clear intensity levels

games.title: Real-Life Connections Bazaar
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A bazaar vendor cat sells vocabulary stickers. But you can only buy a sticker by connecting the word to a real-life example. The cat asks 'Give me an example of something TRANSPARENT!' and child taps the matching real-world item picture. Correct = sticker peels into the bazaar collection book.
games.mechanic: The cat holds up a vocabulary word card ('transparent'). Four real-life picture tiles appear (glass window, wooden door, brick wall, paper bag). Child taps the correct real-life example. Correct = sticker snaps into album; wrong = cat shakes head with a gentle 'hmm'. 10 vocabulary words per bazaar visit.
games.freeSample: First 3 words (transparent, rough, heavy — very visual) free; full 60-word bazaar across science, social studies, and ELA domains paid.
assetNeeds: bazaar vendor cat character (idle, hold-up card, approve, hmm)

games.title: Story Retell Theater
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A tiny puppet-theater frog is the director of Story Retell Theater. The child assembles out-of-order story panels into the right sequence, taps character-speech bubbles for each moment, then watches the puppet show play back. The frog director gives a standing ovation at the end.
games.mechanic: 5 scrambled story panels are shown (from a 5-event story). Child drags them into order (beginning to end). Then for each panel, a prompt: 'What does [character] say/do here?' offers 3 bubble choices. Child taps the correct speech bubble. All correct = puppet show plays through automatically. 3-4 story options per game session.
games.freeSample: One story (5 panels, 5 questions) free; library of 10+ stories with characters, settings, and lessons paid.
assetNeeds: puppet theater background with stage curtains
frog director character (idle, applause, standing ovation)
story panel illustration sets (5 per story, 3 stories min)

games.title: Character Costume Party
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A blank character silhouette is at a costume party. The child reads character-description sentences from a story and dresses the character to match: brave knight, sneaky fox, nervous turtle. Each costume piece added makes the character react in character.
games.mechanic: A short story excerpt is read aloud describing a character ('Maya was nervous. She bit her lip and hid behind the door.'). A trait word card appears ('NERVOUS'). Child selects from 3 costume/prop options the one that shows nervousness. Character reacts with the matching emotion. 5 character traits per costume session.
games.freeSample: First character (3 traits: happy, tired, surprised) free; 8 characters from diverse stories with subtler traits paid.
assetNeeds: 5 base character silhouettes (girl, boy, animal, fantasy, elder)

games.title: Setting Snapshot
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A story-photographer bear takes photographs of story settings. Each correct answer to a setting-detail question develops one section of a Polaroid photograph. The full setting photograph develops into a rich illustrated scene that the bear proudly displays.
games.mechanic: 4 questions about a story's setting are posed ('When does this story happen?', 'What is the weather like?', 'What sounds might you hear?', 'Who else is there?'). Child taps from 3 picture-and-word answers for each. Each correct answer develops one quarter of the Polaroid. Full photo = bear's happy-snap celebration.
games.freeSample: First story setting (1 Polaroid, 4 questions) free; 10 story settings across diverse time periods and places paid.

games.title: Print Concept Command Bridge
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The child is Captain of a Spaceship with a giant book on the command bridge viewscreen. A quirky computer AI narrates and asks the captain to identify print concept elements. Each found element triggers a ship instrument to light up. All elements found = ship launches.
games.mechanic: A book-page scene is shown (full page with title, sentences, punctuation, paragraph breaks). AI prompts: 'Tap the FIRST WORD of the sentence', 'Tap a PERIOD', 'Find a CAPITAL LETTER that starts a sentence'. 6 prompts per page. Each correct tap illuminates a ship panel; wrong tap gives a gentle 'scanning...' beep.
games.freeSample: First page (3 prompts: sentence start, period, capital) free; 8 pages with every print convention including commas, apostrophes, and page features paid.
assetNeeds: 8 book-page scene illustrations with clear print features

games.title: Phoneme Swap Shop
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A swap-shop raccoon runs a phoneme exchange booth. Child drops in a word and chooses which phoneme to swap out; the machine hums and produces a new real word from the change. The raccoon inspects it with a jeweler's loupe and pronounces it 'a GENUINE new word!'
games.mechanic: A word is shown and spoken (e.g. 'cat'). The machine shows 3 phoneme-swap options: 'Change the first sound to /b/', 'Change the vowel to /u/', 'Change the last sound to /p/'. Child taps one swap and the machine produces the result. Child confirms if it's a real word (real/nonsense sort). 8 swaps per visit.
games.freeSample: First 3 swaps (CVC initial-consonant swaps producing obvious real words) free; 30 swaps including medial vowel changes and final consonant swaps paid.
assetNeeds: raccoon shopkeeper character (idle, jeweler-loupe inspect, genuine-stamp)
exchange booth machine with input/output slots

games.title: Long Vowel Island
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A friendly pelican guides the child across a string of tropical islands, each belonging to a different long vowel sound (Sunny A Island, Breezy E Island). At each stop a word puzzle must be solved to move on. The pelican squawks and does a wing-flap happy dance at each island arrival.
games.mechanic: At each island stop a word appears with its vowel team blank (r__n, s__p, tr__). Child taps the correct vowel team spelling for that island's long-vowel sound (ai / ee / oa). Correct = pelican flaps and the character hops to the next island. Each island has 3 stops; 5 islands total.
games.freeSample: First island (Long A, ai vowel team, 3 stops) free; all 5 Long Vowel Islands (A/E/I/O/U) with multiple spelling patterns per island paid.

games.title: Syllable Stomp Dance
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A stomp-dancing dinosaur is on a dance floor with tiles labeled 1, 2, and 3 syllables. Picture-word bubbles bounce around and the child pops them onto the matching floor tile. Each correct pop makes the dino stomps in time and a disco ball swings.
games.mechanic: Picture + word bubbles drift across the dance floor: 'elephant', 'dog', 'umbrella', 'sun', 'butterfly'. Child taps each bubble to hear the word, then taps the correct floor tile (1, 2, or 3 syllables). Correct = dino stomps and the tile flashes; wrong = bubble bounces gently and lands back in the drift. 12 words per song.
games.freeSample: First 4 words (1-syllable and 2-syllable only) free; full 40-word dance party with 3-syllable words and compound-word detection paid.
assetNeeds: dinosaur dancer character (idle stomp, disco stomp, confused look)

games.title: Word Wall Wizard
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A wizard's spell-book has a secret scene hidden behind tiles. Each sight word the child reads correctly and matches to its picture-clue flips one tile to reveal part of the magical scene. The more sight words, the bigger and more wondrous the revealed image.
games.mechanic: A sight word appears on a glowing scroll. Child matches it to one of 3 pictures that hint at the word's meaning or use. Correct = a tile flips. After every 4 tiles a new scene element is revealed (from a starry wizard workshop to a full magical portal). 16 tiles = full scene reveal + wizard celebration.
games.freeSample: First 4 tiles (sight words: the, and, a, is) free; full spell-book of 60 Grade 1 high-frequency words paid.

games.title: Sentence Builder Diner
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A diner chef needs help assembling sentences like food orders. Child picks the subject-card, verb-card, and object-card from the tray and snaps them together. The chef serves the completed 'sentence meal' to a waiting character who reacts. Wrong ingredient combos make the character make a comically disgusted face.
games.mechanic: A prompt picture is shown (e.g. 'a dog chasing a ball'). Three trays hold word cards: Subject tray (The dog / A cat / The bird), Verb tray (chases / eats / flies), Object tray (a ball / a fish / the sky). Child drags one card from each tray to build the matching sentence. Correct sentence = customer cheers and eats. 8 meals per diner shift.
games.freeSample: First 3 meals (simple SVO sentences) free; full diner with 30 meals, adjectives, and compound sentences paid.
assetNeeds: 4 customer characters with react animations (happy, disgusted)

games.title: Synonym Swap Twins
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Identical twin parrots love words that mean almost the same thing. Cards are face-down and the child flips them seeking synonym pairs. When a pair is found, the two parrots do a synchronized flutter-dance and the cards spin together with a glow.
games.mechanic: 8 paired cards face-down in a 4x4 grid. Child taps two to reveal (e.g. 'happy' and 'joyful'). Synonym match = parrots dance + cards stay revealed. Non-match = gentle flip-back. Also includes antonym-pair rounds (labeled differently) where the parrots 'argue-dance' instead. 4 pairs per round.
games.freeSample: First round (4 synonym pairs, simple: big/large, fast/quick) free; 10 synonym rounds + 5 antonym rounds with nuanced pairs paid.

games.title: Question Catcher
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A curious koala researcher releases QUESTION bubbles about a passage but some pop out as 'ANSWERED by the text!' and some as 'NOT ANSWERED!'. The child pops only the questions the text CAN answer. Each correct pop earns a koala fact-card for her research notebook.
games.mechanic: A short illustrated passage is shown (narrated). Then 6 question-bubbles drift out: 3 that the text directly answers and 3 that it doesn't. Child pops only answerable ones. Correct pops = fact-cards for notebook; wrong pops = koala gasps and the question bounces back. 6 bubbles per passage.
games.freeSample: First passage (3 answerable, 3 not — obvious distinction) free; 10 passages with increasing subtlety paid.

games.title: Story Blueprint
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An architect beaver is designing a Story Building. The building has three floors: BEGINNING, MIDDLE, END. Child reads a story and places the correct event-block on each floor. When all three floors are filled, the beaver adds a roof and the building lights up like a cozy home.
games.mechanic: A short 5-panel story is read aloud. Then 5 event-tiles appear (scrambled). Child drags the correct tile onto the Beginning floor, 2 onto the Middle, and 1 onto the End. The final 'lesson tile' goes on the roof. Correct placements click into place; wrong ones bounce back. 5 events per story.
games.freeSample: First story (simple 3-event linear story) free; library of 10 stories with problem-solution structures, fantasy, and realistic fiction paid.
assetNeeds: event-tile sprites (5 per story, 3 stories min)

games.title: Information Station
games.subject: ela
games.strand: Informational Text — Main Topic & Key Details
games.funHook: A knowledge tree grows taller with every key detail the child identifies about an informational topic. The main topic is the trunk; each correctly identified key detail is a new branch+leaf. When 4 branches grow, a tiny forest animal moves in and explains a fun fact.
games.mechanic: An informational passage is read aloud. Main-topic card is placed at the trunk (given). Then 5 detail-cards appear; child taps and waters only the ones that ARE key details (not random or irrelevant facts). Each correct one grows a branch. Wrong taps wilt a leaf, gently. 4 details per tree.
games.freeSample: First knowledge tree (topic: penguins, 4 correct details + 1 distractor) free; 10 topic-trees across science and social studies paid.
assetNeeds: forest animal character (3 types: owl, squirrel, frog)

games.title: Anthology Matchmaker
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two book-club characters — Penelope (Book 1) and Theo (Book 2) — sit in cozy armchairs. Fact-cards fly out from both books mixed together. The child sorts each fact to its matching book OR drops it in the middle 'BOTH BOOKS' pile. Penelope and Theo give each other surprised looks when a BOTH card lands.
games.mechanic: Two short informational texts on the same topic have been read aloud. Then 8 fact-cards drift in (4 unique to Book 1, 2 unique to Book 2, 2 in both). Child sorts each to Penelope, Theo, or the BOTH pile. Correct = character nods approval; wrong = gentle slide back with a headshake. 8 cards per comparison.
games.freeSample: First comparison (frogs vs toads, 4 same/different facts) free; 8 topic-pairs with increasing overlap complexity paid.

games.title: Cookie Baker's Kitchen
games.subject: math
games.funHook: You're a magical baker filling orders for a whimsical cookie shop — each problem solved earns a cookie that pops into the display case with a warm glow. When the case is full the baker does a little happy dance.
games.mechanic: A story-problem order ticket appears (e.g., 'The shop sold 34 cookies. They baked 18 more. How many now?'); child taps the correct answer from 3 choices in the order tray; correct answer snaps a beautifully frosted cookie into the display-case diorama. Child may rearrange cookies after placing.
games.freeSample: Free: first 4 order tickets (add-only, sums ≤50). Full game: all 20+ tickets spanning add/subtract within 100, two-step problems, all problem types.
assetNeeds: Baker character (apron, chef hat, 3 expressions: neutral/happy/extra-happy)
12 distinct cookie sprite designs (frosted, sprinkled, shaped)

games.title: Fact Rocket Blastoff
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Every rapid correct answer peels back a tile of a hidden planet scene. When the final tile flips, the rocket lands and an alien waves hello — each planet has a different silly alien.
games.mechanic: A grid of 12 tiles covers a mystery planet image. A flash-card fact appears (e.g., '7+8='). Child taps the correct answer bubble; a tile flips away. Speed comes from wanting to see the picture, not from a timer.
games.freeSample: Free: first planet (6 tiles, sums/differences within 10). Full game: 8 planets covering all sums/differences within 20, including all 15 addition pairs and their subtraction twins.

games.title: Odd & Even Party Bus
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A goofy party bus has two sections: ODD SQUAD and EVEN CREW. Animal passengers each hold a number; sorting them into the right section triggers a little seat-bounce dance. Mis-sorts get a puzzled head-tilt from the driver.
games.mechanic: Animal passengers drift in from the left holding number cards (0–99). Child drags each to the Odd Squad or Even Crew section of the bus. After 10 passengers, the bus drives off with a honk and confetti.
games.freeSample: Free: first bus route (numbers 1–20). Full game: all routes (numbers up to 99, including multiples of 10, teen numbers with digits summing to odd/even).
assetNeeds: 8 animal passenger sprites each holding a blank number sign

games.title: Array Garden
games.subject: math
games.funHook: You're planting a magical garden where flowers grow in neat rows. Planting the correct array makes a butterfly flutter in and land — collect different butterflies for different arrays.
games.mechanic: A garden plot appears with a sign showing a repeated-addition sentence (e.g., '3+3+3+3='). Child drags seed packets to fill the correct number of rows with the correct number in each row; flowers bloom into an array. A butterfly matching the array shape arrives to complete the scene.
games.freeSample: Free: 2×2, 2×3, 3×3 arrays. Full game: all arrays up to 5×5, plus prompts that show the array and ask for the repeated-addition sentence.

games.title: Place Value Castle
games.subject: math
games.funHook: You're building a magical castle tower. Hundreds blocks are stone towers, tens blocks are windows, ones are little gems. Each correctly identified chunk adds a castle part with a satisfying click-into-place sound.
games.mechanic: A three-digit number appears on a royal scroll. Child drags the correct number of hundreds-towers, tens-windows, and ones-gems from a supply bin onto the castle canvas. When the castle is complete it lights up with a flag-raising animation.
games.freeSample: Free: numbers with no zeros (e.g., 234, 152). Full game: all 3-digit numbers including those with interior/terminal zeros (104, 320, 200).

games.title: Skip-Count Caterpillar
games.subject: math
