games.funHook: A friendly caterpillar stretches across a leaf path. Each correct skip-count step adds a new body segment with a satisfying pop — the longer the caterpillar grows, the sillier and wobblier it gets.
games.mechanic: The caterpillar's head sits on a numbered leaf. A gap in the sequence appears on the next leaf. Child taps the correct number from 3 choices; the caterpillar extends a new segment and hops forward. Sequences by 5s, 10s, and 100s within 1000.
games.freeSample: Free: skip by 5s (5, 10, 15…55). Full game: skip by 2s, 5s, 10s, 100s, plus backward sequences.

games.title: Number Name Switchboard
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A retro telephone switchboard operator receives calls — each call comes in as a number in one form and needs to be switched to another. The switchboard lights up and buzzes delightfully when you make the right connection.
games.mechanic: A number appears at the top in one form (standard, written-word, or expanded). Child drags a plug cord to the matching socket in a different form. Correct connection: lights flash, a satisfying 'bzzt-click' animation plays. Three forms cycle so every round transforms a different pairing.
games.freeSample: Free: standard ↔ word form up to 99. Full game: all three forms (standard / word / expanded) for numbers up to 999, including numbers with zeros.

games.title: Mountain Climber Comparisons
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Two mountain-goat climbers race up a cliff — you feed the correct comparison symbol (>, <, =) to a hungry sign-post that opens its mouth wide. The winning goat pumps its fist and does a tiny victory leap.
games.mechanic: Two 3-digit numbers appear on cliff faces. Child drags >, <, or = into the sign-post's open mouth. Correct: the correct goat hops up a notch. Wrong: gently spat back with a cheerful 'hmm' wobble. 15 rounds per climb.
games.freeSample: Free: compare numbers up to 200. Full game: all comparisons up to 999, including numbers that share hundreds or tens digits requiring deep comparison.
assetNeeds: Two goat climber sprites (neutral, victory-leap, cheering)

games.title: Hundreds Chart Hot-Air Balloon
games.subject: math
games.funHook: You pilot a hot-air balloon across a sky map — each correct addition or subtraction within 100 drops a sandbag or inflates a lift-bag, moving the balloon to the next destination. Arrival reveals a tiny village diorama element.
games.mechanic: A two-digit addition or subtraction problem appears on a cloud. Child taps the correct answer from 3 cloud choices. Correct: balloon moves right on the sky path and a diorama element (tree, house, windmill) pops into the scene below.
games.freeSample: Free: sums/differences ≤50 no regrouping. Full game: all combinations within 100, with and without regrouping, using multiple strategies cued by the problem design.
assetNeeds: 6 village diorama sprites (tree, house, windmill, pond, barn, flag)

games.title: Base-Ten Block Sculptor
games.subject: math
games.funHook: You're a sculptor in a magical workshop adding base-ten blocks to create a number statue. When complete the statue winks and poses — each correct addend snaps into place with a clay-thud sound.
games.mechanic: A target 3-digit sum is shown on a clay tablet. Up to 4 two-digit addends appear in a supply bin as labeled rods. Child drags the correct combination to the sculptor's workbench; the running total updates with a satisfying click. Final total must match the target.
games.freeSample: Free: add 2 two-digit numbers, sums ≤100. Full game: add up to 4 two-digit numbers, sums ≤200, with varied addend combos.

games.title: Regrouping Repair Shop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A tiny robot brings broken numbers to your repair machine. You feed in the correct blocks, pull the lever, and the machine regroups them — gears turn, blocks visually trade, and the fixed number pops out repaired.
games.mechanic: A 3-digit addition or subtraction problem appears. Child drags the correct trade (e.g., 10 ones → 1 ten block) into the machine's input slot before pulling the lever. Machine animates the regrouping and produces the answer. Covers both add and subtract with regrouping.
games.freeSample: Free: addition with one regrouping, no crossing hundreds. Full game: add/subtract within 1000 with regrouping in any position, including subtracting across zeros.
assetNeeds: Block trade sprites (10 ones ↔ 1 ten, 10 tens ↔ 1 hundred)

games.title: Mental Math Carnival
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Balloons float up from a carnival — each balloon has a number. A prompt says '+10' or '−100'. Pop only the balloons that show the correct result. Correct pops spray confetti; wrong ones do a gentle boing and refill.
games.mechanic: 8 balloons drift up, each showing a 3-digit number. A mental-math rule appears ('+10', '−10', '+100', '−100'). Child pops the 3 balloons that are correct results for the current starting number. No timer — just satisfying pops.
games.freeSample: Free: +10 and −10 only. Full game: all four operations, starting numbers chosen to create interesting patterns (ending in 9, crossing hundreds boundary).

games.title: Ruler Ruler on the Wall
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A wacky inventor's workshop is full of objects of all lengths. You help the inventor find 'everything longer than 8 centimeters!' by tapping objects in the scene — each tapped object gets a little ruler swoosh animation.
games.mechanic: A cozy scene (workshop, kitchen, garden) has 10–12 hidden objects with labeled lengths. A measurement prompt appears ('Find all objects shorter than 10 cm'). Child taps the matching objects; each correct tap animates a mini ruler beside the object. Wrong tap: gentle shimmer 'look again'.
games.freeSample: Free: workshop scene, 'shorter than' prompts only. Full game: 4 scenes (workshop, kitchen, garden, classroom), both shorter/longer, cm and inches, exact length matches.
assetNeeds: Workshop scene background with 12 embedded object sprites

games.title: Measurement Mix-Up Market
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A chaotic market stand has objects measured in BOTH inches and centimeters and someone scrambled the labels. Sort each item into the correct measurement-unit bin — the market vendor does a relieved sigh when order is restored.
games.mechanic: Items float in (a pencil labeled '15 cm', a ribbon labeled '6 inches'). Child drags each to the cm bin or inch bin. Then a second sort: 'which measurement is longer?' bins labeled with numbers. Items settle with a warm 'thank you' wiggle.
games.freeSample: Free: sort by unit only (cm vs inches). Full game: unit sort + which-is-longer comparisons + estimate-and-match rounds.
assetNeeds: 12 everyday object sprites with removable label badges

games.title: Estimation Island
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A friendly island monster loves estimates — feed it your best guess and it chomps down happily if you're in the right ballpark. Wild guesses get a surprised spit-back and a fun 'whoa, that's a LOT!' reaction.
games.mechanic: An object appears (a door, a crayon, a desk). Child drags one of 3 estimate cards (e.g., 5 cm / 50 cm / 5 m) into the monster's open mouth. Correct estimate: chomp + happy dance. Wrong: gentle spit with a visual comparison showing why. 12 objects per session.
games.freeSample: Free: 5 objects, cm only. Full game: 20 objects, both cm/m and in/ft, including oddly shaped objects to prevent anchoring.
assetNeeds: 12 object sprites at realistic relative sizes

games.title: Missing Measurement Detective
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A detective machine compares two objects — feed it one measurement and the difference, and it produces the missing measurement with a satisfying 'case solved!' magnifying-glass pop.
games.mechanic: Two objects appear side by side. One has a label (e.g., 'Rope A: 23 cm'). A difference clue is shown ('Rope B is 8 cm longer'). Child drags the correct answer card into the machine to solve for Rope B. Machine produces a 'Case Closed' stamp animation.
games.freeSample: Free: differences within 20, whole numbers. Full game: differences up to 99, both 'longer than' and 'shorter than', includes subtraction direction.

games.title: Number Line Frog Hop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A tiny frog leaps along a lily-pad number line. Each correct placement makes it hop with a boing and a big smile. Land exactly on 100 to trigger a waterfall celebration.
games.mechanic: A number line 0–100 is shown (with markings at 0, 10, 20…). A problem appears: 'Start at 37. Add 25. Where do you land?' Child taps the correct lily pad. Frog hops there with a bouncy arc. Subtraction rounds have the frog hopping backward.
games.freeSample: Free: addition only, multiples of 10 as addends. Full game: add and subtract any amounts within 100, including non-round numbers.

games.title: Coin Collector Critter
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A cute coin-collecting critter has a shiny album. Solve a money problem and the correct coin or bill peels off and snaps into its silhouette in the album with a sparkle. Tap any collected coin to hear it jingle and see its value.
games.mechanic: A prompt appears: 'Show 47¢ using the fewest coins.' Child drags coins from a tray to match. Correct combination: coins snap into the album page with a shimmer. If fewer coins exist, the critter does a little surprised-delight face. Wrong: gentle bounce back.
games.freeSample: Free: amounts under 25¢, pennies and nickels only. Full game: all combinations through $1.00, includes dollar bills, making change, comparing amounts.

games.title: Clock Shop Keeper
games.subject: math
games.funHook: You run a magical clock shop — customers bring in clock faces and you set the hands to the right time by dragging them. When you get it right the customer claps and places the clock in a beautiful display window.
games.mechanic: A customer arrives with a digital time on a ticket (e.g., '2:35'). Child drags the hour and minute hands on a blank clock face to match. Correct: the clock chimes, a sparkle animates, and the clock joins the display window. 15 customers per session.
games.freeSample: Free: times on the hour and half-hour. Full game: times to the nearest 5 minutes, including quarter-past/quarter-to, a.m./p.m. context, and elapsed time within the hour.
assetNeeds: Large clock face prop with movable hands

games.title: Pictograph Penguin Poll
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A penguin reporter polls other penguins about their favorite things. Each answer you verify places a penguin icon in the correct row of a live pictograph — the graph grows and the reporter penguin nods with approval.
games.mechanic: A pictograph with 3–4 categories and a key (each icon = 2) is shown. Prompts ask: 'How many more penguins chose fish than squid?' Child taps the correct answer from 3 choices. Correct: a new icon pops into the graph. A 'reading the graph' phase follows where the child builds the graph from raw data.

games.mechanic: A short poem stanza appears; child taps the rhyming word pair, OR the repeated phrase, OR answers 'What feeling does this word give?' from three choices; correct turns the dial notch and reveals a tile; finale plays the full poem with a musical animation.

assetNeeds: music-studio scene in 16 segments behind grill
musical-finale character sprites (band: drum, guitar, keyboard)

games.title: Story Architecture Builder
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A tiny story-house is built piece by piece: the child identifies beginning/middle/end and problem/solution from a story, and each correct answer locks in a wall, roof, door, or window — when all parts click in, the house lights up and a family of characters moves in.
games.mechanic: After reading/hearing a short story, five building-part prompts appear one by one (beginning, middle, end, problem, solution); tap the correct retelling sentence from three; correct snaps that part of the house into place; all 5 correct triggers the move-in celebration.
games.freeSample: Free: beginning and end only (2 building parts). Paid: full 5-part story house with 8 different stories across genres.
assetNeeds: house-frame construction prop (with 5 snap-in parts: foundation, walls, roof, door, window)

games.title: Two-Voice Puppet Switch
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two puppet characters tell the SAME story event from different viewpoints; the child picks whose voice is speaking for each thought-bubble, then builds a two-column 'what each puppet thinks' chart — puppets debate each other with silly dramatic flair.
games.mechanic: A story event panel shows; a thought-bubble floats up with a perspective statement; child taps which puppet is thinking it (left or right); correct pins it to that puppet's column with a dramatic puppet-nod; wrong gets a 'Hmm, would I really think that?' from the puppet.
games.freeSample: Free: one 3-event scene with two puppets. Paid: 6 scenes with increasingly subtle POV distinctions, ending with a puppet-debate finale.
assetNeeds: puppet pair x3 sets (each with neutral + thinking + dramatic states)
puppet-debate finale animation (puppets face each other gesturing)

games.title: Illustration Evidence Spotlight
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A page from a picture book fills the screen with a paragraph of text beside it; a spotlight character asks the child to tap the part of the illustration that proves a detail in the text — spotlight sweeps the scene dramatically when searching.
games.mechanic: Illustration and text side-by-side; a question asks 'Which part of the picture shows us [text detail]?'; child taps the matching area; correct triggers a spotlight-ring highlight + narrator confirmation; wrong gives a sweep-hint in the right region.
games.freeSample: Free: one illustration with 2 text-match questions. Paid: 8 illustration+text pairs with 3 questions each, including mood, detail, and 'what can you tell from the picture but not the text?' questions.
assetNeeds: illustration-scene x4 with tappable hotspot zones

games.title: Info Text Question Quest
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An explorer character hops along a jungle path; at each stop, a panel from a real informational mini-text appears and a question rises from a treasure chest — answering correctly lets the explorer hop to the next stop with a triumphant step.
games.mechanic: Short 3-4 sentence informational passage appears at each path stop; a who/what/where/when/why question rises from the chest below it; child taps one of three answers; correct hops the explorer to the next stop with a happy stride.
games.freeSample: Free: 3-stop jungle path on one topic (frogs). Paid: 5 full 8-stop paths on distinct real-world topics (ocean, weather, insects, ancient Egypt, volcanoes).

games.title: Main Topic Magnet
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A giant magnet hovers over a field of floating detail-bubbles; the child labels the magnet with the main topic first, then the magnet swoops to attract ONLY the real key details — detail-bubbles that don't belong drift away with a gentle 'zap' non-match.
games.mechanic: Read a short informational passage; tap the correct main topic from three choices (magnet gets labeled); then drag the floating detail-bubbles into the magnet's field; key details snap in, off-topic ones bounce away gently.
games.freeSample: Free: one passage with main topic identification only. Paid: 8 passages across science/social studies topics with main topic + 3 key detail sorting tasks each.
assetNeeds: magnet prop sprite (label slot + swooping animation)

games.title: Cause & Effect Chain Gang
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A quirky Rube-Goldberg machine with gears, ramps, and balls connects causes to effects; the child identifies a cause from an informational text and feeds it into the machine — the machine traces the effect chain with dramatic gear-cranking animations.
games.mechanic: Read a short informational passage about a real-world event chain; drag the cause-card into the machine funnel; pull the lever to choose the correct effect from three options; correct sends a ball rolling through the full animated chain to ring a bell at the end.
games.freeSample: Free: one 2-step cause-effect chain (rain causes plants to grow). Paid: 8 passages with cause-effect chains of increasing complexity, including 3-step chains.
assetNeeds: Rube-Goldberg machine prop (gears + ramps + ball + bell)

games.title: Vocabulary Context Carnival
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A carnival barker character shouts a vocabulary word in context; three items float past on a carnival float — the child drags the correct meaning-match (picture or synonym phrase) into the barker's collection basket; perfect matches trigger a carnival-horn fanfare.
games.mechanic: Short sentence with a bolded context-clue word appears; three floating answer cards drift by; child drags the correct definition/synonym into the barker's basket; correct triggers horn fanfare; wrong floats away with 'Look at the clue words nearby!'
games.freeSample: Free: 4 vocabulary words from a science passage. Paid: 40+ vocabulary words across informational text domains with context-clue, prefix/suffix, and synonym tasks.

games.title: Text Feature Treasure Map
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A richly designed informational page (like a real nonfiction book spread) fills the screen; a treasure hunter asks the child to tap specific text features (caption, bold word, table of contents, heading, glossary entry) — each correctly tapped feature glows gold.
games.mechanic: Realistic nonfiction page layout fills the screen with 8+ text features; a prompt asks 'Tap the caption' or 'Tap a bold vocabulary word'; child taps the correct element; correct makes it glow gold; when all features are found the treasure hunter does a victory dance.
games.freeSample: Free: one page with 3 features (heading, caption, bold word). Paid: 6 distinct nonfiction page layouts covering all text features including index, glossary, diagram labels, and table of contents.
assetNeeds: nonfiction page mock-up layouts x3 (science, social studies, how-to)

games.title: Author Purpose Sorting Booth
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An author character tosses paper airplanes (short text snippets) and two bins wait below: 'To Inform' and 'To Persuade'; the child catches each airplane and sorts it — correct sends it spiraling into the right bin with a satisfying thunk; wrong bounces off with a wobble.
games.mechanic: A text-snippet paper airplane floats down from the author; child reads it and drags it to the correct purpose bin (inform vs persuade); correct drops in with a spin-thunk sound; wrong bounces back with 'Is the author sharing facts or trying to convince you?'
games.freeSample: Free: 4 snippets, inform vs persuade only. Paid: 24 snippets across inform, persuade, AND entertain categories with increasing subtlety.
assetNeeds: two sorting bins (inform + persuade) with open top

games.title: Photo + Caption Matchmaker
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A museum curator character has mixed up the photo-caption cards; child flips and matches each informational photo to its matching caption — matched pairs light up in a frame and the curator does a relieved happy dance.
games.mechanic: Grid of face-down cards (photos on one side, captions on the other); tap two to reveal; a photo-caption pair that matches locks with a gold frame and a curator cheer; non-matches flip back gently; goal is to match all pairs.
games.freeSample: Free: 4-pair museum with 1 topic. Paid: 5 museum rooms (ocean creatures, weather phenomena, ancient artifacts, landforms, habitats) with 6 pairs each.

games.title: Reason & Evidence Detective
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A detective's evidence board fills with pinned cards as the child identifies whether each sentence from a short persuasive text is a POINT or a REASON supporting it — when the board is complete the detective dramatically solves the case.
games.mechanic: Short persuasive text excerpt appears; sentences float up one by one; child drags each to the correct pin on the board (POINT pin or REASON pin); correct sticks it to the board with a satisfying pin-click; all pinned triggers the detective's case-solved moment.
games.freeSample: Free: one 3-sentence argument (1 point + 2 reasons). Paid: 8 distinct arguments across real-world topics with 3-4 reasons each to categorize.
assetNeeds: POINT banner and REASON banner pin props

games.title: Two-Book Compare Café
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cozy book café has two tables, each named after a different informational book on the same topic; the child reads fact-cards and sorts them to the correct book's table — facts found in BOTH books get placed in a shared 'both' centerpiece.
games.mechanic: Fact-cards about a shared topic drop from above; child reads each and drags to Book A table, Book B table, or the 'Both' centerpiece in the middle; correct placements trigger a happy waiter character doing a little spin; wrong gets gently bumped back.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 fact-cards on one topic pair, two-table sort only. Paid: 5 topic pairs (e.g. lions vs tigers, rainforest vs desert, volcanoes vs earthquakes) with 8 cards each including the 'both' category.
assetNeeds: cozy café background with two tables + centerpiece

games.title: Compound Word Rocket
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two word-parts are the rocket's two fuel tanks; the child snaps them together to form a compound word and the rocket launches dramatically — wrong combinations cause a comical misfire with smoke and a confused alien popping out.
games.mechanic: Two word-part tiles hover in separate fuel-tank frames; drag one into position with the other; correct combination clicks together with a bolt-lock animation and a countdown begins; wrong combinations cause the comical misfire animation.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 compound words with obvious visual cues. Paid: 30 compound words across levels of obviousness, including compound-word-meaning questions after each launch.
assetNeeds: rocket sprite (two-tank parts + assembled + launch + misfire)
alien character sprite (confused + waving from rocket)
fuel-tank prop with slot (empty + filled states)

games.title: Irregular Plural Pet Parade
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A parade of animals marches along a festive path; each float asks 'What's the plural?'; choosing the CORRECT irregular plural (goose→geese, mouse→mice, child→children) lets that animal's float zoom forward with a toot of a horn — wrong choices make the float stall with a silly honk.
games.mechanic: Animal float arrives at a stop; the singular animal name appears; child taps the correct irregular plural from three choices; correct sends the float zooming to the next stop with a horn toot; incorrect stalls it with a honk and 'Try that one again!'
games.freeSample: Free: 3 floats with common irregulars (feet, teeth, mice). Paid: full 20-float parade with all major irregular plurals and an end-of-parade finale.
assetNeeds: parade-float sprite x4 (animal-labeled, zoom + stall animations)
animal character sprite x6 (singular + plural forms shown)

games.title: Irregular Past Tense Time Machine
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A zany time machine takes present-tense action pictures and zaps them into the past; the child pulls the lever to choose the correct irregular past-tense word from three — wrong choices cause a time-paradox explosion with silly mixed-up calendar pages flying everywhere.
games.mechanic: A present-tense action scene card enters the time machine; three past-tense word choices appear on the dial; child taps the correct irregular past tense; correct sends the scene out the other side aged/sepia with the correct word glowing; wrong triggers the paradox animation.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 words (went, ran, ate, saw). Paid: 30 irregular past tense verbs across difficulty levels with a sentence-in-context check after each.
assetNeeds: time-machine prop sprite (funnel + lever + dial + chute)
paradox-explosion animation with flying calendar pages
present-tense action scene card x6 (with sepia filter variant)

games.title: Adjective Order Kitchen
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A chef character needs to describe their dish in EXACTLY the right adjective order (opinion, size, color, noun); the child stacks adjective-ingredient tiles onto a recipe card in the correct sequence — getting the order right makes the dish appear perfectly plated with a chef's kiss.
games.mechanic: A picture of a dish appears; four adjective tiles float in random order; child drags them onto the recipe card in the correct order (opinion→size→color→noun); correct snaps them in sequence with a satisfying click and the chef does a kiss-fingers gesture.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 recipes with 2-adjective ordering only. Paid: 12 recipes with 3-4 adjective stacks and 'taste-test' bonus questions about why the order matters.
assetNeeds: chef character sprite (idle + kiss-fingers + proud + oops)
recipe card prop with 4 tile slots
food dish illustration x4 (plated success + jumbled fail states)

games.title: Conjunction Junction Train
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A train station machine joins two sentence-cars together; the child picks the right conjunction (and, but, or, so, because) to couple the cars — correct coupling makes the train chug forward with a whistle; wrong conjunction causes the cars to bounce apart with a silly clank.
games.mechanic: Two sentence-car tiles sit on the track; a set of conjunction-coupling tiles appear; child taps the best conjunction to couple the cars; correct clicks them together and the train chugs with a whistle; wrong bounces them apart with a hint about meaning.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 sentence pairs with and/but only. Paid: 30 sentence pairs across all five coordinating conjunctions with context-meaning choices.
assetNeeds: train-car sprites x2 (with text-slot panels, coupled + uncoupled states)

games.title: Capital Letter City
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A city map fills in building by building as the child correctly capitalizes proper nouns in sentences; each correct capitalization raises a new building on the skyline with a celebratory sparkle — wrong capitalizations leave the lot empty with a gentle 'that's not a proper noun!' wobble.
games.mechanic: A sentence appears with all lowercase; tap each word that SHOULD be capitalized (proper noun: name, city, day, month, title); correct taps make the letter glow gold; tap a word that shouldn't be capitalized and it wobbles red gently; complete the sentence correctly to raise a building.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 sentences with names and days only. Paid: 24 sentences across all proper noun categories (names, cities, days, months, holidays, book titles) with a full city skyline finale.
assetNeeds: city skyline background with empty lot slots x8

games.title: Apostrophe Bakery
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A hungry baker character needs words written CORRECTLY with apostrophes (contractions and possessives) to fill their bakery display; the child drags the correctly spelled form into the display case — correct forms get baked into a pastry shape and displayed beautifully.
games.mechanic: Baker holds up a phrase (e.g. 'belonging to the dog' or 'do not'); three word-card options appear; child drags the correct apostrophe form into the display case; correct triggers a baking animation; wrong is gently placed back on the tray with 'Not quite — check that apostrophe!'
games.freeSample: Free: 4 contractions (don't, can't, I'll, it's). Paid: 30 items across contractions + possessives with a bakery-full celebration finale.
assetNeeds: baker character sprite (idle + baking + proud + gentle-return)

games.title: Shades of Meaning Color Wheel
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A giant color wheel on the wall has intensity slots from lightest to darkest; the child places synonyms with different intensity shades (whisper/say/shout, tiny/small/big/enormous) in order from weakest to strongest — the wheel glows brighter as words are correctly placed.
games.mechanic: Four synonym-gradient word cards appear; child drags them onto the color wheel in intensity order (weakest to strongest); correct placement makes that wheel segment glow; all four correct makes the wheel spin with a light-burst celebration.
games.freeSample: Free: one 3-word gradient (small/big/enormous). Paid: 12 word families (adjectives and verbs) with 4-word gradients each and a 'use-in-a-sentence' reveal for each word.
assetNeeds: color wheel prop with 4 gradient segments (glow animation)

games.title: Real-Life Word Web Spinner
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A friendly spider character spins a web connecting a vocabulary word in the center to real-life examples around it; the child places correct real-life connection cards on web nodes — the spider bounces happily across the web when it's complete.
games.mechanic: A vocabulary word sits in the center web node; five scene-picture cards (some that connect to the word's meaning, some that don't) appear in a tray; child drags connections to web nodes and rejects non-examples back to the tray; complete web triggers the spider's happy bounce.
games.freeSample: Free: one word web (curious) with 4 connection choices. Paid: 20 vocabulary words across concrete and abstract categories with 5-choice connection tasks each.
assetNeeds: scene-picture connection cards x5 per round

games.title: Narrative Time-Capsule
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: The child seals a 'time capsule' story about something that HAPPENED to them; they sequence event-picture panels into order, pick detail-sentences to add richness, and choose an ending that wraps it up — a rocket then launches the capsule into space with a warm 'your story is out of this world!' message.
games.mechanic: Three scrambled event-picture panels appear; child drags them into the correct beginning/middle/end sequence; then taps a detail sentence to add to each panel; finally taps the best ending conclusion from two choices; correct sequence launches the rocket.
games.freeSample: Free: one 3-panel story with sequence only. Paid: 8 distinct story starter scenarios with sequencing + detail-adding + conclusion choices.
assetNeeds: time-capsule rocket prop (with panels attached, launch animation)
story-event panels x3 per scenario (scrambled + ordered states)

games.title: Synonym Swap Shop
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A word-swap machine swaps boring overused words for vibrant synonyms; the child feeds a dull word in (e.g. 'said', 'nice', 'big', 'went') and the machine upgrades it to the most precise synonym matching the context — incorrect synonyms cause the machine to clank and spit it back.
games.mechanic: A sentence with an underlined target word enters the machine; three synonym options appear on the dial; child taps the most precise synonym for the context; correct sends the upgraded word shooting out with a sparkle; wrong clanks with 'Close — but which fits this sentence best?'
games.freeSample: Free: 4 swaps for overused 'said'. Paid: 40 context-precise synonym swaps across 10 overused word families with a word-wall collection display.
assetNeeds: word-swap machine prop (dial + funnel + chute + sparkle-chute)
overused-word token sprites x5 (worn, faded look)
upgraded-synonym token sprites x5 (bright, vivid look)

games.title: Sentence Type Circus
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A circus ringmaster introduces four performing acts: the Statement lion, the Question clown, the Command acrobat, and the Exclamation firework — sentences flying in on trapeze get sorted to the right act; each correct sort triggers that performer's signature trick.
games.mechanic: A sentence card swings in on a trapeze; child reads it and drags it to the correct circus act (statement/question/command/exclamation); correct triggers the performer's signature trick animation; wrong gently swings back with 'Listen to how it ends!'
games.freeSample: Free: 4 sentences, two categories (statement vs question). Paid: 32 sentences across all four types with an end-of-show grand finale.
assetNeeds: circus ring background with 4 act platforms

games.title: Story Map Explorer
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An explorer hops across a story map — each landmark is a story element (characters, setting, problem, events, solution, lesson); at each stop the child places the correct retelling card onto the map landmark to unlock the path forward.
games.mechanic: Story map path has 6 landmark stops; at each stop a retelling element prompt appears; child taps the correct retelling phrase from three; correct pins the card to the landmark and the explorer hops forward with a cheer; all 6 complete triggers a treasure reveal.
games.freeSample: Free: 3-stop map (characters, setting, problem) on one short story. Paid: 6 stories with full 6-landmark maps including lesson/theme identification.
assetNeeds: story-map background (parchment style with 6 landmark markers)

games.title: Poetry Word Museum
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A word museum curator collects vivid, musical words from poems; the child reads each poem stanza and identifies the word that creates a rhythm, mood, or image — correctly identified words get framed and displayed in the museum; tapping a displayed word reveals a fun 'why this word rocks' fact.
games.mechanic: A stanza appears; three words are highlighted; child taps the one the question asks about (e.g. 'which word makes this feel fast?', 'which word rhymes with _?'); correct peels a golden sticker into the museum frame; tapping the sticker reveals the fun fact.
games.freeSample: Free: 4-poem museum with rhyme identification only. Paid: 20-poem full museum across rhythm, rhyme, repeated phrases, and mood-conveying words.
assetNeeds: museum interior background with frame slots

games.title: Prefix & Suffix Word Inventor
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: An inventor character builds NEW words from parts; the child snaps a prefix, base, and suffix together like robot parts — the resulting word-robot comes to life and acts out its meaning with a funny animation unique to each word.
games.mechanic: Prefix tile + base-word tile + suffix tile appear separately; child drags them into three slots on the invention bench in correct order; correct snaps them together and the word-robot animates its meaning; wrong combination causes the parts to fly apart comedically.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 two-part words (prefix+base). Paid: 20 words with prefix, base, and suffix combinations including meaning-match mini-challenge after each invention.
assetNeeds: word-robot sprite x4 (acts-out-meaning animations per word type)

games.title: Dictionary Diver
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A deep-sea diver descends through a giant underwater dictionary; at each depth a word swims by and the diver must answer a question about how to find it (alphabetical order, guide words, which page, what entry number) — correct answers let the diver descend to the next level with bubbles and a happy kick.
games.mechanic: At each depth stop, a dictionary-skill challenge appears: drag words into ABC order, OR tap the correct guide-word pair, OR identify which letter section to look in; correct lets the diver descend with a kick; 10 correct reaches the treasure chest at the bottom.
games.freeSample: Free: 3-level dive with alphabetical order only. Paid: full 10-level dive with guide words, letter section identification, and entry-number reading.

games.title: Main Idea Magician
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A magician character hides the 'big idea' of an informational text behind a curtain; each correct key detail the child identifies pulls away one curtain panel — when all panels are gone the revealed main idea appears with a magical flourish and the magician bows.
games.mechanic: Read a short informational passage; identify key detail sentences by tapping them from a mix of real details and irrelevant sentences; each correct tap pulls away a curtain panel; after all correct details are found, the main idea appears and magician bows.
games.freeSample: Free: 4-panel curtain, one passage. Paid: 8 passages each with their own 9-panel curtain reveal, with main idea varying between explicit and implicit.

games.title: Vocabulary Word Collector
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A personal word journal fills with collected vocabulary stickers; the child earns each sticker by correctly matching a word to its meaning, picture, or context-clue sentence — tapping a collected sticker plays a child-friendly 'word fact' and a silly example sentence.
games.mechanic: A word and three meaning-match options (picture, definition, context sentence) appear; child taps the correct one; correct peels the word sticker into the journal with a shimmer; tapping any collected sticker plays its word-fact with a funny character illustration.
games.freeSample: Free: 5-word starter collection. Paid: 60-word full collection across academic, science, and social studies vocabulary with the silly-example-sentence reveal.
assetNeeds: word-journal prop with page layout and sticker slots
word-fact character illustration x4 (poses for different word types)

games.title: Story Panel Sequencer
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A film director character holds a clapboard; scrambled story panels need to be placed in the correct beginning-middle-end order to make the film; once ordered correctly the panels animate as a mini movie with the director's 'and... ACTION!' call.
games.mechanic: 4-5 scrambled illustrated story panels appear in a tray; child drags them into storyboard slots in correct order; optional detail sentence can be added to each; when all placed correctly the director calls action and the panels animate in sequence.
games.freeSample: Free: 3-panel sequence on one story. Paid: 8 stories with 5-panel sequences and an optional detail-sentence layer for added richness.
assetNeeds: film-director character sprite (idle + clapboard + action call)
story-panel illustrated cards x5 per story

games.title: Contraction Rocket Builder
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Two word-blocks fuse together in a rocket factory and an apostrophe-shaped laser zaps out the missing letters — the child identifies WHICH letters get zapped and WHERE the apostrophe lands; getting it right launches the rocket with a whoosh.
games.mechanic: Two word tiles appear (e.g. 'do' + 'not'); child taps which letters disappear (the 'o' in 'not'); then taps the apostrophe icon and drags it to the correct position; correct fuses the words and launches the rocket; wrong causes a funny misfire.
games.freeSample: Free: 4 contractions with don't/can't/won't/isn't. Paid: 24 contractions with the apostrophe-placement mechanic and an 'undo the contraction' reverse challenge.
assetNeeds: word-block tiles with deletable letter slots
rocket-launch success animation + misfire fail animation

games.title: Nonfiction Feature Hunt
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A curious scientist character grows their 'nonfiction knowledge plant' each time the child correctly answers what a text feature is FOR (not just what it is) — the plant sprouts a new leaf, blossom, or fruit for each correct feature-purpose answer.
games.mechanic: A text feature is highlighted on a simulated nonfiction page (e.g. a heading, bold word, diagram); the scientist asks 'What does this help the reader do?'; child taps the correct purpose from three; correct triggers the plant growing a new feature-type element with a satisfying sprout animation.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 features (heading, caption, bold word — just the identify phase). Paid: full 12-feature plant across all text feature types with purpose questions and a 'create your own feature' bonus.
assetNeeds: scientist character sprite (idle + water can + excited)
knowledge-plant sprite (8 growth stages with feature-themed decorations)
nonfiction-page mock-up with highlighted feature zones

games.title: Reflexive Pronoun Mirror Maze
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: Characters walk through a mirror maze where their 'reflected' selves need the right reflexive pronoun (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, themselves) label — the child picks the correct label so the mirror-character can pass through; wrong labels cause a funny mirror-wobble.
games.mechanic: A sentence with a blank appears at a mirror-stop; a character is pictured; child taps the correct reflexive pronoun from three; correct makes the mirror-character wave and the path opens; wrong wobbles the mirror with 'Hmm — who is doing the action?'
games.freeSample: Free: 4 sentences using myself/yourself/himself. Paid: 28 sentences across all 7 reflexive pronouns with singular vs. plural distinction challenges.

games.title: Informational Infographic Builder
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A creative designer character needs to fill in a blank infographic about a topic; the child reads the short text and drags the right label, diagram piece, or key detail into the correct infographic zone — when all zones are filled the infographic comes to life with little animations.
games.mechanic: A partially blank infographic about a real topic sits on a design board; short text passages appear in a sidebar; child reads each passage and drags the correct label/diagram/fact into the blank zone; complete infographic triggers the come-to-life animation.
games.freeSample: Free: one 4-zone infographic about butterflies. Paid: 6 infographic topics (water cycle, food chain, community helpers, planets, animal adaptations, life stages) with 6-8 zones each.
assetNeeds: infographic template frames x3 (with blank zone slots)
label and fact chip sprites with text slots
come-to-life animation effect (mini character moves on the infographic)

games.title: Comma Greeting Mail Sorter
games.subject: ela
games.funHook: A cheerful mail-carrier character holds letters with greetings and closings; the child taps WHERE each comma should go in the greeting and closing — letters without correct punctuation get marked with a friendly red stamp and sent back; correct letters get dropped in the mailbox with a satisfying clunk.
games.mechanic: A letter with blank comma slots appears; child taps the correct slot locations to place commas; correct placements make the slot glow; complete the letter correctly and the mail-carrier stamps it 'Delivered!' and drops it in the box.
games.freeSample: Free: 3 letter greetings (Dear [Name], format). Paid: 16 letters including greetings, closings, lists with commas, and addresses.
assetNeeds: letter prop template with comma-slot positions
mailbox prop with slot and open/full states

games.title: Fraction Feast Cart
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A round little food-cart creature opens its mouth asking for 'one-third of a pizza' — the child drags the correctly-partitioned pizza slice from three options into the chomping maw; wrong slices wobble and bounce back with a cheerful burp.
games.mechanic: Drag the fraction model (correctly shaded shape) that matches the spoken/shown fraction symbol into the cart creature's open mouth; 8 rounds per session cycling through halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, eighths with circle, rectangle, and set models.
games.freeSample: First 3 rounds (halves and thirds with circles only) fully playable; the remaining 5 rounds and all shape variety locked.
assetNeeds: Round cart creature with open/closed mouth states and happy-chomp animation
Pizza/pie circle models pre-partitioned in 2/3/4/6/8 with various shading
Gentle 'spit back' wobble animation for cart creature

games.title: Equal Slices Diner

games.funHook: A word-problem-solving machine has two slots for two operations — the child feeds the problem into the machine, selects the correct first and second operations on gear-shaped dials, and pulls the lever to see the answer shoot out.
games.mechanic: A two-step word problem appears on a scroll; child selects operation 1 (add/subtract/multiply) on dial 1 and enters intermediate result via number tiles; then selects operation 2 on dial 2 and final answer; pulling the lever animates both processing steps; 6 problems per session.
games.freeSample: First 2 problems (add then subtract, all within 50) fully playable; problems involving multiplication in one step and results over 100 locked.
assetNeeds: Two-slot gear machine with two dials and a scroll input/output
Dial sprites (operation symbols on each gear)
Machine operator character (bear mechanic with wrench)

games.title: Area Word Problem Safari
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A safari ranger needs to figure out area for animal enclosures — each story panel shows an enclosure problem and the child selects the correct length×width expression then the area; correctly solved enclosures fill with the animal doing a happy dance.
games.mechanic: A 2–3 panel story describes an area problem (e.g., 'The lion enclosure is 8m long and 6m wide. What is the area?'); child selects the multiplication expression and then the answer; correct completion populates the enclosure with a dancing animal sprite; 5 stories per session.
games.freeSample: First 2 stories (rectangle areas with dimensions ≤6) fully playable with animal dance; distributive-property decomposition problems locked.
assetNeeds: Safari ranger character with binocular/point/clap animations
5 animal sprites with happy-dance animations (giraffe, elephant, lion, zebra, flamingo)

games.title: Perimeter Unknown-Side Detectives
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A detective mouse finds the missing fence boards in a yard — the child taps the correctly labeled board (the unknown side length) hidden among props in a messy backyard scene; the mouse stamps 'FOUND IT' when correct.
games.mechanic: A polygon with a missing side length is shown; the perimeter and all other sides are labeled; the missing side's value appears written on boards hidden in a scene (garden tools, barrels, plant pots); child taps the correct board; 8 problems per session.
games.freeSample: First 4 problems (rectangles with one unknown side, perimeter ≤40) fully playable; irregular polygons with 1–2 unknown sides locked.
assetNeeds: Detective mouse character with magnifying-glass/stamp/'FOUND IT' animations
Backyard scene background with 10–12 prop items
Board sprites each labeled with a different number
Perimeter diagram overlay (polygon with labeled sides)

games.title: Multiplication Pattern Pop
games.subject: math
games.funHook: Arithmetic pattern bubbles float up — the child pops the ones that follow the rule (e.g., 'even × odd = even?'); correctly popped bubbles release a pattern of sparkles in the same color sequence as the rule.
games.mechanic: A pattern rule is shown (e.g., 'Pop all products that are EVEN'); 12 bubbles drift upward labeled with multiplication expressions or products; child pops only the ones matching the rule; 5 rounds per session, one rule each (even/odd products, multiples-of-5, multiples-of-10, commutativity pairs).
games.freeSample: Round 1 (pop even products) and Round 2 (pop multiples of 5) fully playable; rounds for odd/even rules, commutative pairs, and zero-property locked.
assetNeeds: Bubble sprites (3 tints) with arithmetic expression labels
Sparkle-pattern release on correct pop (color-coded to rule)
Boing re-inflate animation on wrong pop
Rule-display banner at top of screen

games.title: Fraction Bar Build
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A fraction bar robot needs its sections painted — the child drags colored segments into the bar to build a given fraction, then compares two bars by dragging them side-by-side; the robot flexes when both bars are built and compared correctly.
games.mechanic: A fraction bar (denominator given, e.g., sixths) is shown; child drags colored segment tiles into the bar to show the correct numerator; a second bar is then built for comparison; child drags the correct <, =, or > symbol between bars; robot flexes; 7 build-pairs per session.
games.freeSample: First 3 build-pairs (halves vs. fourths with same numerator) fully playable with robot flex; pairs requiring reasoning about same denominator or equivalent fractions locked.
assetNeeds: Fraction bar robot character with flex/idle/surprised animations

games.title: Multiplication Commutative Flip Show
games.subject: math
games.funHook: A flip machine takes an array and flips it 90 degrees — the child sees 3×5 become 5×3, confirms the product stays the same, and the machine stamps 'Same Product!' with a satisfying kerchunk; the machine eats unusual sizes and spits out funny flips.
games.mechanic: An array is shown (e.g., 3 rows × 5 columns); child cranks the flip lever; the array animates rotating 90°; child confirms both expressions equal the same product by tapping the correct number; 8 flip pairs per session with varied factors.
games.freeSample: First 4 flip pairs (factors 2–5) fully playable with rotation animation; flip pairs with factors 6–9 and distributive-property decomposition locked.

games.mechanic: A large rectangle (e.g., 6×9) is shown; child drags a dividing line to split it; labeled sub-dimensions appear; child enters sub-areas and total by tapping from number choices; each correctly solved building piece joins a growing neighborhood scene; 5 floors per session.
games.freeSample: First 2 floors (breaking a ×7 or ×8 factor using smaller known facts) fully playable with neighborhood piece appearing; larger factor decompositions locked.

critiques.qualityNotes: "The CONCEPT is genuinely premium and marketable IF executed: a full-curriculum K-3 game library, no-pressure tone, character/collection delight, one-level simplicity, all behind a paywall while practice drills stay free — that is a coherent and defensible conversion lever. A parent/teacher pays for (a) breadth (one subscription = the whole year's curriculum as GAMES), (b) the no-shame no-timer promise (a real differentiator vs Prodigy/SplashLearn which lean on streaks/points), and (c) the character/diorama/sticker-album reward loops that make a child WANT to return. The risk is NOT the idea, it is that ~12 of the 13 gameTypes (feed-the-friend, magic-machine, reveal-grid, path-journey, sort-home, build-a-world, sticker-album, pop-the-right-ones, match-pairs, etc.) repeat so heavily that the set can feel like one engine re-skinned 195 times — exactly the 're-skin of a drill' trap the operator wants to avoid. The strongest games (Mochi's Counting Feast, Monster Mouth Comparing Game with the > / < mouth, Number Train Conductor, Decompose the Dragon's Hoard, Array Garden, the diorama/world-builders) earn their premium label because the reward IS the play. The weakest ~15-20 are flash-card-with-timer-removed (Fact Rocket Blastoff is the clearest offender) — those undermine the 'genuine game, not a drill' promise and should be cut or rebuilt, not shipped as padding. To make a parent pay over the free activities: lean into the persistent reward-world (the diorama/album/world fills up ACROSS sessions and ACROSS games — a meta-collection), and ensure every game's win-state is a character/surprise/build payoff, never just 'correct, next.' Honest recommendation: ship the strong ~145 MATH games, fix the ~20 mis-tagged/padding ones, fill the 8 real coverage gaps, and rely on the parallel ELA set to reach 300+ — better a tight, genuinely-fun, fully-covered set than 195 with visible re-skin fatigue."

Syllable Snap Bakery (K) vs Syllable Stomp Parade (K) — both RF.K.2.b syllable-count, both 'tap the count' at K. Two is redundant; keep one.
Setting Snapshot (gr1, RL.1.3/1.7) overlaps 'Scene Detective' (gr1, RL.1.7) and 'Story Town Mayor' (gr1, RL.1.3) — three gr1 games circling character/setting Q&A with picture answers. Trim one.
coverageGaps: RF.1.3.F (read words with inflectional endings -s/-ed/-ing) — NO grade-1 game. Suggest a magic-machine 'Ending Add-On' (base word in, child taps -s/-ed/-ing, output word+picture).

Writing at GRADE 1 entirely absent — W.1.1 opinion, W.1.2 informative, W.1.3 narrative have NO games (gr2/gr3 have writing games). Suggest build-a-world 'sort sentence-cards into essay parts' clones of the gr3 Opinion Builder, graded down.
W.3.2 (informative/explanatory writing) — MISSING at grade 3 (only W.3.1, W.3.3, W.3.7, W.3.8 present). Suggest build-a-world 'Info Report Builder' (sort topic-sentence/detail/conclusion cards).
W.2.1 + W.2.2 (opinion + informative writing) — MISSING at grade 2 (only W.2.3 narrative). Suggest sort-home essay-part builders.

Grade-1 grammar holes: L.1.1.C (verb agreement), L.1.1.D (pronouns), L.1.1.G (conjunctions), L.1.1.H (determiners/articles), L.1.1.I (prepositions) have NO games. Suggest sort-home + feed-the-friend variants (Preposition Playground exists at K — make a gr1 sibling for L.1.1.I).
L.1.2.C/D/E (commas in series, phonetic + conventional spelling) — MISSING at grade 1. Suggest pop-the-right-ones 'correctly spelled' bubbles (the gr3 Spelling Pattern Bubbles graded down).
RI.3.7 (use info from illustrations/maps) — MISSING at grade 3 (only RL.3.7 Constellations covers literary). Suggest i-spy-scene over an infographic/map.
RF.K.2.c (blend onset+rime orally) — no PREMIUM game (only the free activity). Suggest magic-machine 'snap onset to rime'.
RI.K.8 (identify reasons author gives) — MISSING at K (present as RI.1.8). Suggest build-a-world 'pin the reasons' graded down from Author's Proof Wall.
L.3.3 (use knowledge of language/conventions for effect) + L.2.3 (formal vs informal) — MISSING. Lower priority but uncovered.
SL at grades 1 and 2 entirely absent (SL.1.x, SL.2.x) — K and gr3 have speaking/listening games. Suggest reveal-grid listening-comprehension (gr3 Listening Quest graded down) for gr1/gr2.
paddingFlags: Fluency games (RF.K.4 Reading Buddy, RF.1.4.B Fluency Flight, RF.3.4 Fluency Express, RF.2.4 Fluency Puppet) — 'tap each word in order, smoothness rewarded' is a weak GAME under the no-timer/no-score lock; with no pacing feedback it reduces to tapping in order. Strengthen with characterful payoff or cut to one strong fluency game per grade-band.

Print-concept games (Wiggle the Words, Print Walk, Print Concept Command Bridge, Open the Book Shop) — RF.x.1.a-c are tap-the-spot/word-order tasks that are barely distinguishable from the free practice activities; risk reading as drills. Keep ~1-2 strong ones, ensure genuine surprise/reward.

Two-text-compare games (Two Books One Topic K, Two-Text Telescope gr1, Two-Book Compare Cafe gr2, Compare Two Books gr3, Anthology Matchmaker gr1) — sort-into-A/B/Both is the SAME mechanic five times; each is fine alone but the family is repetitive — vary the mechanic across grades.

Self-Correct Station (gr1) + Morning Message Fix-It (K) + Silly Sentence Fixer (K) + Sentence Surgery (gr3) — error-find-and-fix is heavily reused; confirm each has distinct delight, not just 'tap the error'.
Capital Cop / Capital Detective / Capital Letter City — capitalization-find across three grades is mechanically identical (tap-the-word); needs escalating content + reward to justify three.

Cause-&-Effect family (Connection Web Spinner K, Connection Bridge Builder gr1, Cause & Effect Chain Gang gr2, Cause & Effect Chain Factory gr3, Connections Constellation, Comprehension Connections Web) — six connect-the-cards games; some are padding.

Author-purpose sort (Author vs Illustrator K, Author Purpose Sorting Booth gr2, Author's Purpose Sorting Office gr3) — fine spiral but drag-to-bin is low-agency; ensure the character payoff carries the fun.
critiques.qualityNotes: "The set is genuinely strong on the SUBSTANCE that makes a parent pay: it spans the FULL ELA strands (RL/RI/RF/L/SL/W) across K-3 with curriculum-credible CCSS targeting, and the gameType variety (i-spy, build-a-world, magic-machine, feed-the-friend, sort-home, path-journey, sticker-album, reveal-grid, story-maker, match-pairs, grow-tend, dress-decorate, pop-the-right-ones, build-a-buddy, magic-trace) gives real texture beyond drill. The no-timer/no-score lock is respected — fun is sourced from collection (sticker albums), surprise (machine misfires, reveal grids), character delight, and agency (build/sequence). That IS marketable: a parent sees 'a real game for every reading skill my kid is learning,' which the free single-skill activities cannot match. RISKS to premium feel: (1) ~15-25 games lean drill-shaped (tap-the-word/sort-to-bin) and need their character/reward layer to actually land or they feel like the free activities re-skinned — the operator's own 'demonstrate not touch the standard' and 'genuine game not a drill' bars must be enforced per-game at build. (2) The same 6-8 mechanic templates recur heavily; replayability depends on the per-session content shuffle (the §20.2 Fisher-Yates pattern) plus enough item pools (≥7 originals per §A.13.60) — without that, a 'game' is a one-and-done. (3) Writing (W) and Speaking/Listening (SL) are the thinnest strands and are exactly where the free activity engines DON'T compete — leaning into strong W/SL games is the clearest premium differentiator and the biggest current gap. Honest call: this is a fundable premium set, but it's closer to ~165 keepers after cutting re-skins, and the path to 300+ is to FILL the W/SL/grammar gaps (which add real coverage value) rather than ship more rhyme/syllable/sight-word/compare re-skins (which pad)."

bundles.name: Kindergarten Math Game Club
bundles.subject: math
bundles.marketingAngle: Every kindergarten math standard your child meets this year — as a real game, not a worksheet. Count, compare, add, build shapes, and sort, with feed-the-friend creatures and a sticker album that fills up as they play. No timer, no score, no tears — just play that happens to be the whole K curriculum.

bundles.name: Kindergarten Reading & Letters Game Club
bundles.subject: ela
bundles.marketingAngle: From 'which way does the book open?' to first sight words and rhymes — a playful game for every early-reading skill. Letter detectives, rhyme rockets, story theaters, and a word-sticker safari. The free practice activities teach one skill; this is the storyworld that makes them want to come back.

bundles.name: Grade 1 Math Game Club
bundles.subject: math
bundles.marketingAngle: Add and subtract within 20, master place value, tell time, and compose shapes — the full Grade 1 math year as characterful games. Fact-family treehouses, lily-pad number lines, monster comparisons. Built for the kid who 'hates math worksheets' but will happily play.

bundles.name: Grade 1 Reading & Language Game Club
bundles.subject: ela
bundles.marketingAngle: Digraphs, blends, long vowels, story structure, and first grammar — every Grade 1 reading and language standard as play. Vowel-team islands, story-town mayors, sentence-builder diners. Includes the writing and grammar games the free single-skill activities don't cover.

bundles.name: Grade 2 Math Game Club
bundles.subject: math
bundles.marketingAngle: Two- and three-digit numbers, regrouping, money, time, measurement, and arrays — the whole Grade 2 math curriculum as games with persistent reward worlds. Place-value castles, coin carnivals, array gardens. One subscription = the year, played not drilled.

bundles.name: Grade 2 Reading, Writing & Language Game Club
bundles.subject: ela
bundles.marketingAngle: Prefixes and suffixes, story architecture, cause-and-effect, irregular verbs, and real writing games. Prefix labs, character crews, narrative time-capsules. The writing and speaking games here are exactly where free practice tools can't compete — that's why parents pay.

bundles.name: Grade 3 Math Game Club
bundles.subject: math
bundles.marketingAngle: Multiplication, division, fractions, area and perimeter — the make-or-break Grade 3 math year as games that build understanding, not speed-anxiety. Multiplication dojos, fraction feasts, area tile-layers, no timers anywhere. The anti-Prodigy: mastery through play, never pressure.

bundles.name: Grade 3 Reading, Writing & Language Game Club
bundles.subject: ela
bundles.marketingAngle: Main idea, inference, figurative language, affixes, opinion and narrative writing — the full Grade 3 ELA scope as games. Idiom diners, inference islands, opinion-builder workshops. Deep enough that a third-grader who 'finished' the free activities still has a year of play here.

buildOrder: 1) Build the persistent reward shell FIRST (cross-game meta-collection: a diorama/world/sticker-album that fills across sessions AND across games) — both critics agree this is THE thing that makes a parent pay over the free activities and the only defense against re-skin fatigue; every game plugs into it, so it must exist before game #1.

2) Pilot the 6-8 strongest, most-distinct games as the demo slice — Mochi's Counting Feast, Monster Mouth Comparing Game (>/< mouth), Number Train Conductor, Decompose the Dragon's Hoard, Array Garden, Multiplication Dojo, Fraction Feast Cart, a story-maker — to validate the no-timer-still-fun premise and the free landing + free-sample-slice + paid-gate conversion mechanic before scaling.

3) Grade 3 Math Game Club next — highest willingness-to-pay band: multiplication/division/fractions/area is the make-or-break year, the strand where parents most fear their kid falling behind, and it is the clearest 'I'd pay to avoid Prodigy's pressure' sell. 42 keepers, near-complete.

4) Kindergarten Math + Kindergarten Reading Clubs — largest addressable audience (every entering family), strongest existing game quality (the counting/comparing/feed-the-friend set is the critic's top tier), and establishes the brand at the on-ramp grade. Build math and reading in parallel so the K family gets a complete year.

5) Grade 2 Reading/Writing/Language Club — prioritize because its Writing and Speaking/Listening games are where the FREE activity engines structurally cannot compete (critic 2's clearest premium differentiator); leading with the W/SL fills, not more rhyme/sight-word re-skins.

6) Grade 1 Math + Grade 1 Reading Clubs — fills the K→2 continuity gap so a family can subscribe across the whole early span; apply the heavy Grade 1 dedup (fact-family, shape-composer, compound-word, sight-word, tens-bundling collisions) during this build.

7) Grade 2 Math + Grade 3 Reading Clubs — completes the 8-bundle matrix; these are solid but have the most internal dedup work (gr2 graph family 4→2, gr3 multiplication-fluency 3→2, gr3 vocab/dictionary collisions), so do them once the shell and templates are battle-tested.

8) Coverage-gap fill pass LAST, as small targeted waves — the ~16 genuinely-missing standards (W.1.x, W.2.1/2.2, W.3.2, gr1 grammar L.1.1.C-I, K.G.B.5, 2.MD.D.9, 2.MD.B.5, 3.OA.A.4, RI.3.7, SL.1/SL.2) ADD real curriculum value, unlike more re-skins; fold each into its bundle when authored so 'full-curriculum coverage' is literally true at launch.
bundle.completenessNotes:
Honest count: 390 listed → after applying the critics' drops (~24 net math removals incl. 3 K.NBT builders→1, graph family 4→2, shape-composer collapse, fluency/two-text/cause-effect/capital family trims) ~152 math + ~147 ELA keepers = ~299 GENUINE games. This sits right at the operator's 300+ floor BEFORE the gap-fills — the ~16 coverage-gap games (see build step 8) push the launchable, full-curriculum total to ~315. So 300+ is achievable ONLY if the gap-fills ship; do not pad with re-skins to hit it.

RISKS (both critics, load-bearing): (1) Re-skin fatigue — 13 gameTypes carry ~300 games, so the set lives or dies on (a) the persistent cross-game meta-collection shell and (b) the §20.2 per-session Fisher-Yates shuffle + §A.13.60 ≥7-originals-per-game pool. Without item-pool depth, each 'game' is one-and-done and the paywall feels thin. (2) ~20 math + ~20 ELA games are drill-shaped (Fact Rocket Blastoff, the fluency games, print-concept tap-the-spot, sort-to-bin author-purpose) and must EARN their character/reward payoff per-game at build or they read as the free activities re-skinned — the operator's 'genuine game, not a drill' and 'demonstrate not touch the standard' bars must gate each one.

MIS-TAGS to fix not ship (math): Caterpillar Skip-Count Sprout (skip-count is not a K standard — cut or convert to count-forward-from-N), Skip-Count Galaxy (counting-sequence drill mis-tagged 1.NBT.A.1 — retag), Pattern Parade Float + Attribute Fashion Show (AB-patterning is not CCSS-K; retag as readiness or cut), Coin Collection Creature Shop (money starts 2.MD.C.8, not K — move to gr2), Sentence Scramble Safari (sequencing, not 2.OA.A.1 — strengthen the equation step or retag), Tessellation Tile Maker (weak K.G.B.6 fit).

GENUINE COVERAGE GAPS still open after dedup: math — K.G.B.5 (build shape from parts), 2.MD.D.9 (line plot at gr2), 2.MD.B.5 (length word problems within 100), 3.OA.A.4 (missing factor/quotient), thin 2.OA.C.4 array coverage, verify 3.NF.A.2.a vs .2.b split. ELA — RF.1.3.F (inflectional endings), ALL of grade-1 Writing (W.1.1/1.2/1.3), W.2.1/W.2.2, W.3.2, grade-1 grammar L.1.1.C/D/G/H/I, L.1.2.C/D/E, RI.3.7, RI.K.8, RF.K.2.c premium game, SL.1.x + SL.2.x entirely absent. Writing and Speaking/Listening are the thinnest strands AND the highest-value premium differentiators (free engines don't cover them) — treat these gap-fills as priority content, not afterthoughts.

DISTRIBUTION NOTE: every game needs a FREE indexable landing + FREE sample slice with the full game gated (the conversion lever) — this is a per-game SEO/route obligation (cf. §21/§22 landing-program), not just a build task; budget for ~315 new landing pages × 11 locales downstream, though launch can be EN-first."
